Perfect Reprise.name: Perfect Reprise
Perfect Reprise.description: The user spends three attention charges and calls "Encore" to physically repeat the last ordinary Encore technique they completed this scene, at its original range and strength, despite its cooldown. The user pays twice its normal exertion and performs every motion again; targets can react afresh. The user cannot repeat an Ultimate, awakened ability or reprise, and cannot use the Quirk for the rest of the scene afterward. Strain: severe.

Shelter Gel Network.name: Shelter Gel Network
Shelter Gel Network.description: The user feeds connected gel channels across thirty meters for three turns, forming six padded cradles that carry injured adults at walking pace and sealing up to four doors against pursuit. Faces and exits for rescuers stay clear. Cutting a channel stops its cradle or door seal, vehicle impacts tear the gel, and the user cannot produce more gel until an hour of rest afterward. Strain: severe.

Measured Living Dressing.name: Measured Living Dressing
Measured Living Dressing.description: The user maintains a medicinal gel coat on one adult within ten meters for the rest of the scene. The user senses pressure and warmth through the connected gel, adjusting its grip to seal accessible bleeding and support a damaged limb during movement. The coat speeds repair over hours, never regrows limbs or replaces blood, and cannot reach hidden internal wounds. The user must remain conscious and cannot produce other gel while treating the patient. Strain: severe.

Solstice Front.name: Solstice Front
Solstice Front.description: The user releases pale-blue fire and deep frost together across a whole city block, filling the streets with thick fog and putting barriers and cover through thermal shock for the rest of the scene. Enemies inside take heavy fire and cold damage as their weapons and armor crack, while allies move unseen through the mist; held back, the surge cracks only gear and locks foes to the ankles in steaming ice while sparing bystanders. Driving both natures across a block swings the user's core into fever and chills, triggering their Drawback at once. Strain: severe.

Extreme Stillpoint.name: Extreme Stillpoint
Extreme Stillpoint.description: The user places a temperature lock on up to a dozen objects, walls or patches of ground across a street for the rest of the scene, holding each at steady heat or deep freeze regardless of surrounding fire or weather. They can keep a sagging floor frozen solid, hold rescue lanes warm, or flip any locked spot between heat and frost to crack stone, steel doors or enemy armor for heavy fire and cold damage; held back, the flip breaks only locks and weapons. Keeping the locks active drains the user's body heat, slowing them to a walk. Strain: severe.

Squall Canopy.name: Squall Canopy
Squall Canopy.description: The user swells their personal storm cloud across a whole city block for the rest of the scene, filling the street with rain, static cover and guided wind channels. Each turn they can drop a charged downdraft on foes in the block for heavy force and electric damage that pins and numbs them until the end of their next turn, or lift allies a story high on static updrafts; held back, the downdrafts only hold foes flat. Sustaining both natures across a block scrambles every radio and camera inside and triggers the user's Drawback at once. Strain: severe.

Slipstream Conduit.name: Slipstream Conduit
Slipstream Conduit.description: The user threads dozens of thin wind channels through a building or street for the rest of the scene, turning the air into insulated wiring. They can steer lightning paths around corners and past hostages to hit chosen foes for heavy electric and force damage, catch any live current in the area and ground it safely, or pipe fresh air to trapped people; held back, the arcs only numb and disarm. The user must stand still to hold the channels, and moving snaps the charge back to stun them until their next turn. Strain: severe.

Mantle Basin.name: Mantle Basin
Mantle Basin.description: The user drives both palms into the pavement and spreads fused heat and shaping across a whole city block for the rest of the scene. They soften streets into knee-deep hot mud traps that halt vehicles and runners, fuse fallen rubble into glassy shelter arches over trapped people, and deal heavy fire and bludgeoning damage to enemies on the stone; held back, the mud cools around their legs and only pins them. The user must cool each stretch before civilians step on it, and the absorbed heat triggers their Drawback at once. Strain: severe.

Obsidian Weld.name: Obsidian Weld
Obsidian Weld.description: The user melts and quenches stone in a single heartbeat, turning broken concrete, brick and bedrock along a street into seamless volcanic glass. In one turn they seal a collapsing tunnel, draw all lingering heat out of a burning building's masonry so rescuers can enter, and cast poured-stone cuffs onto every enemy on the street for heavy fire damage; held back, the cuffs quench cool in mid-flow and lock them harmlessly in place. Pulling that heat through their hands leaves the user unable to use the Quirk until the end of their next turn. Strain: severe.

Geyser Canopy.name: Geyser Canopy
Geyser Canopy.description: The user vents all their stored water and heat skyward at once, blanketing a whole city block in a roiling bank of pressurized steam for the rest of the scene. Within the block the user senses every person by how the vapor parts around them, smothers every open fire, and can drive a steam-piston downdraft onto any enemy for heavy force and fire damage; held back, the bank stays a warm mist that only blinds enemies and cushions falls. When it ends, the user is parched and cannot use the Quirk for the rest of the scene. Strain: severe.

Closed-Loop Valve.name: Closed-Loop Valve
Closed-Loop Valve.description: For the rest of the scene the user recycles their vented steam, drawing the moisture and heat back through their skin before it dissipates so even dry air or a freezing room cannot weaken the Quirk. Each turn they can fire a pinpoint pressure valve jet across a street that lifts a bus-sized slab of rubble, bursts a vault door, or deals heavy force and fire damage to one target; held back, it cools in flight and only pins them to a wall. Keeping the hot loop sealed builds core heat, so if the user takes a heavy hit the loop breaks and triggers their Drawback at once. Strain: severe.

Glacial Bastion Ward.name: Glacial Bastion Ward
Glacial Bastion Ward.description: The user drives both frost-plated hands into the pavement and grows ribs of stone-hardened ice across every sagging wall, doorway and shelter line in a city block for the rest of the scene. Collapsing roofs lock still on the petrified ice, allies behind the plates take no harm from gunfire or blasts, and enemies who charge a rib take heavy bludgeoning and cold damage; held back, the ribs only shove them back. Open fire melts the nearest rib, and running both natures across a block roots the user in place until the scene ends. Strain: severe.

Shared Carapace Forge.name: Shared Carapace Forge
Shared Carapace Forge.description: The user lays hands on up to four allies within reach and grows fitted, jointed suits of stone-hardened ice over their clothes for the rest of the scene. Each armored ally shrugs off blades, clubs, pistol rounds and falling debris, and their unarmed blows deal heavy bludgeoning and cold damage; held back, their strikes only knock targets down. Fire or intense heat melts a suit away, and pouring out both natures at once leaves the user shivering at half walking speed and unable to plate their own skin for the rest of the scene. Strain: severe.

Convalescent Canopy.name: Convalescent Canopy
Convalescent Canopy.description: The user drives roots into the street and raises a canopy of flowering vines, moss beds and fruiting boughs across a whole city block for the rest of the scene. Calming pollen drifts through the block to numb pain, vine stretchers draw every injured person onto moss dressings that stop bleeding and mend wounds slowly, and enemies who force entry are struck by boughs for heavy bludgeoning damage and bound; held back, the vines only hold them still. The canopy wilts without light and water, and feeding it drains the user to collapse when the scene ends. Strain: severe.

Grafted Lifebloom.name: Grafted Lifebloom
Grafted Lifebloom.description: The user plants a living seed in a moss dressing over a patient's severed limb, crushed organ or mortal chest wound and feeds it with water and their own stamina. Fine rootlets thread the injury, keep the patient alive while heart or lungs fail, and slowly knit tissue, nerves and bone back together over the rest of the scene, leaving a faint green scar when the blossom withers. It cannot revive the dead, the user must keep both hands on the dressing the whole time, and afterward the user falls unconscious from exhaustion. Strain: severe.

Induction Corridor.name: Induction Corridor
Induction Corridor.description: The user links every lamppost, rail, pipe, car and wire along a city block into one electromagnetic corridor for the rest of the scene. On command it accelerates bearings into volleys or slams metal-armored enemies into walls for heavy force and electric damage, pinning them until they wrench free with a hard effort; held back, it only knocks targets down and disarms steel weapons. Running both natures across a block fries every phone, camera and battery there and slows the user to a walk while it lasts. Strain: severe.

Faraday Cagework.name: Faraday Cagework
Faraday Cagework.description: The user weaves standing coils of current and magnetic force between steel girders, cars or pipes around a crowd or over a live bomb for the rest of the scene. Metal projectiles, shrapnel and electric attacks hitting the cage stop dead, every radio trigger and detonator inside dies without firing, and any enemy who forces through takes heavy electric damage and is thrown back; held back, the cage only shoves them clear. Holding both natures in tight balance roots the user to the spot and empties their charge when the cage drops. Strain: severe.

Ricochet Cyclone.name: Ricochet Cyclone
Ricochet Cyclone.description: The user turns feather-light and ricochets from wall to wall and roof to roof across a whole city block in a blur, stretching arms out to scoop bystanders clear of danger or snapping heavy at the moment of each strike. Every enemy in the open across the block takes heavy bludgeoning damage and is knocked off their feet; held back, each glancing pass only disarms and topples them without lasting injury. Dozens of weight reversals in seconds leave the user retching and unable to stand or use the Quirk until the end of their next turn. Strain: severe.

Counterweight Web.name: Counterweight Web
Counterweight Web.description: The user stretches their arms and fingers into a lattice across a street or courtyard and shifts weight through the strands on the fly for the rest of the scene. Every punch, thrown object or charging villain that strikes the lattice is robbed of weight and rebounded straight back at its source for heavy force damage; held back, the strands wrap and pin the attacker in a heavy fold without harm. Blades and fire still wound the user's stretched flesh, and the user cannot leave the spot until they pull their limbs back in. Strain: severe.

Slipstream Skyway.name: Slipstream Skyway
Slipstream Skyway.description: The user sheds flight feathers into a wind ring that spans a whole city block from street to rooftops for the rest of the scene. Inside it, the user hovers without flapping to pluck people from windows, and feather-guided updrafts catch every falling person and float trapped groups to safety; enemies in the currents take heavy force damage and are thrown back, or are only pinned in place when held back. Strong crosswinds at the perimeter fray the ring, and when it ends the lost feathers and exhausted back ground the user for an hour. Strain: severe.

Whispering Pinion.name: Whispering Pinion
Whispering Pinion.description: The user stills the air around every feather on their wings, erasing all sound and wind trail from their flight for the rest of the scene while keeping a thin shell of compressed air along each wing edge. They fly unseen and unheard through smoke or darkness, slip between falling slabs by feeling air pressure on each quill, and strike one target per turn for heavy slashing and force damage that cuts steel cable; held back, the wing flat only stuns and disarms. Holding silent pressure prevents the user from speaking or sending gusts at range. Strain: severe.

Echoing Quarter.name: Echoing Quarter
Echoing Quarter.description: The user sends a deep, vibrating vocal chord rolling through the air and walls across a whole city block for the rest of the scene. The returning echoes map every room, basement and smoke-filled floor through solid walls, locating every person inside, while the user can focus the hum on any window, lock or bolted barricade in the block to shatter the glass or shake its bolts loose from afar; directed at enemies, it deals heavy sonic damage or, held back, only stuns them to a knee. When it ends, the user's hearing drops to a muffled ring for an hour. Strain: severe.

Null Resonance.name: Null Resonance
Null Resonance.description: The user hums a multi-layered counter-tone that wraps themselves and allies within half a street in a moving pocket of governed vibration for the rest of the scene. Inside it, sonic attacks, shockwaves and vibration Quirks cancel out harmlessly, collapsing rubble loses its shake before it can fall on survivors, and once per turn the user can flip the pitch on one target in sight to drop them to their knees with nausea and heavy sonic damage, or only stun them when held back. Keeping the weave leaves the user's throat raw and unable to speak above a whisper afterward. Strain: severe.

Calamity Stride.name: Calamity Stride
Calamity Stride.description: The user steps onto a burning, flooded or collapsed street, breathes its air once, and adapts by the end of their next turn to every environmental hazard across a whole city block for the rest of the scene: fire, cold, water, toxic gas, smoke, live wires and falling debris. They cross the block unharmed, shield and haul groups of trapped people out, and drive foes back for heavy bludgeoning damage; held back, they only shove them clear. Fresh enemy attacks still land first, and afterward the user cannot adapt again until they rest an hour. Strain: severe.

Wary Flesh.name: Wary Flesh
Wary Flesh.description: For the next three turns, the user's nerves sense the air push of a swing, radiant heat, ozone or trace gas a split second before contact, growing the counter-adaptation on the struck spot before the first hit lands. Blows, shots, fire, cold, electric shocks and gas they see or hear coming are halved even on first contact, and close counters deal heavy bludgeoning damage; held back, they only disarm or floor a foe. Unseen attacks still land in full, and afterward their Drawback strikes at once and blocks new shifts for a turn. Strain: severe.

Gloaming Quarter.name: Gloaming Quarter
Gloaming Quarter.description: The user releases hundreds of small smoked-glass shards across a whole city block for the rest of the scene, each casting a pool of real shade even under floodlights. On any turn the user can step between any two shards' shade on the block, pull a bystander through to safety, or shatter a planted shard so its fragments deal heavy piercing damage and pin the shadows of enemies within a few strides; held back, blunt fragments pin their shadows uncut. Sustaining the swarm parches the user and drains their shadow until they rest. Strain: severe.

Faceted Umbra Weave.name: Faceted Umbra Weave
Faceted Umbra Weave.description: The user fuses their shadow into smoked-glass plates over their body and a ring of planted shards across a street for the rest of the scene. While the armor holds, their blurred outline makes attacks beyond arm's reach miss, allies stepping into a shard's shade emerge under any shard the user picks, and an enemy whose shadow meets a shard takes heavy slashing damage and is locked in place, or only pinned if held back. The user grows parched, casts no shadow and cannot use the Quirk until the end of their next turn if a plate breaks. Strain: severe.

Intersection Cold Surge.name: Intersection Cold Surge
Intersection Cold Surge.description: The user circulates right-side cold and left-side heat through their chest, then releases cold flames and a spreading mass of ice across an intersection up to sixty meters wide. It extinguishes exposed fires and deals massive cold damage; held back, it freezes empty ground and equipment while sparing bodies. The ice remains until broken or melted. Allies need cleared shelter, and the user cannot emit either half until their following turn ends. Strain: severe.

Circulating Cold Mantle.name: Circulating Cold Mantle
Circulating Cold Mantle.description: The user maintains the circulation of both halves through their chest for three turns, carrying cooling flames around their body while closing through intense heat. Each turn the user can press a cooled hand against one opponent within reach to freeze clothing and restrain a limb until the ice breaks or melts. Held back, contact avoids bare skin. The cooling can be overwhelmed, needs uninterrupted concentration and leaves the user unable to continue it for the scene. Strain: severe.

Crowd Contact Lift.name: Crowd Contact Lift
Crowd Contact Lift.description: The user touches one person with all five fingertip pads and spreads weightlessness through people touching that target, continuing through a connected crowd across a city block. Dozens float for up to three turns, beyond the ordinary three-tonne limit, and attacks needing ground traction lose their footing. Disconnected people are unaffected; allies in the chain also float. The user cannot steer the crowd and is unable to activate the Quirk again for the scene. Strain: severe.

Gentle Crowd Return.name: Gentle Crowd Return
Gentle Crowd Return.description: The user eases an already floating crowd and its loose equipment back toward the ground across a city block over two turns, restoring gravity gradually without pressing the fingertip pads together. The controlled return avoids an abrupt mass drop and lets rescuers receive injured people. The user cannot move targets sideways or stop incoming attacks and must stay conscious throughout; afterward they need help standing and cannot activate the Quirk for the scene. Strain: severe.

Ten Minute Dispatch.name: Ten Minute Dispatch
Ten Minute Dispatch.description: The user maintains overdrive through strengthened, previously regrown exhausts for up to ten minutes, covering several city districts while making controlled stops to collect or deliver one passenger at a time. Each stop needs room to brake and each passenger needs a secure hold; the user gains no protection from collisions. Fuel must be sufficient before starting, and the engines stall afterward until the user rests, refuels and cools them for at least ten minutes. Strain: severe.

Cold Exhaust Courier.name: Cold Exhaust Courier
Cold Exhaust Courier.description: The user receives external cooling across both exhaust assemblies, secures one passenger and drives at maximum output along several kilometers of open roadway in under a minute. Carefully timed throttle changes keep the passenger held through planned bends and the final braking run. Cooling must be supplied by an ally or equipment; this Quirk produces none. Obstacles force an abort, and afterward the engines stall for the rest of the scene. Strain: severe.

Floodwall Rescue Circuit.name: Floodwall Rescue Circuit
Floodwall Rescue Circuit.description: The user combines wall adhesion, swimming and loaded leaps for up to ten minutes across a flooded three-story building, retrieving one adult at a time with their twenty-meter tongue and delivering each to a reachable dry landing. Repeated trips let the user evacuate a whole small group without increasing tongue length or carrying capacity. Cold water can still trigger hibernation, and afterward the user's legs and tongue cramp until they rest for at least ten minutes. Strain: severe.

Hidden Tongue Escort.name: Hidden Tongue Escort
Hidden Tongue Escort.description: The user keeps their skin and extended tongue camouflaged against changing surroundings while moving along a wall for three turns. Each turn the user can secure one person within twenty meters, draw them behind cover and loosen the tongue without dropping them, or hold one opponent's arms with the same careful coil. The carried person remains visible; sound, touch and damaged surfaces reveal the approach. Afterward tongue cramps prevent further tongue techniques for the scene. Strain: severe.

Wide Night Guard.name: Wide Night Guard
Wide Night Guard.description: In deep darkness, the user directs the enlarged creature through an open street or hall for the rest of the scene. It stays connected to the user while catching falling people, blocking heavy debris and restraining several opponents within its extended reach. Each turn the user must actively command it; a lapse lets it strike whoever is nearest. Bright light drives it back to the user's side. Strain: severe.

Deep Dark Carry.name: Deep Dark Carry
Deep Dark Carry.description: The user has the creature lift them and several people above a collapsing street for the rest of the scene, using its enlarged body to shield the passengers from falling debris. It can set each person down within its connected reach and strike an attacker for heavy bludgeoning damage, held back to a shove. The user must keep giving orders, and a strong floodlight or a heavy blow can force everyone to land. Strain: severe.

Building Pulse Survey.name: Building Pulse Survey
Building Pulse Survey.description: The user plants both jacks into a building's connected structure and tracks vibrations across its floors for the rest of the scene. They can report the position of moving people, active machinery and fresh collapses to a rescue team each turn. The reading cannot find a silent person on an isolated surface, and one major impact can overwhelm the user's hearing and interrupt the survey. Strain: severe.

Twin Pulse Barrage.name: Twin Pulse Barrage
Twin Pulse Barrage.description: With two working amplifiers, the user sends repeated heartbeat pulses along a connected street or hall for the rest of the scene. Each pulse knocks advancing opponents back and deals heavy sonic damage; held back, it breaks their footing without striking their bodies directly. The pulses travel through the chosen surface and can endanger allies standing on it. The user's ears bleed, and the technique ends if either jack or amplifier is damaged. Strain: severe.

Street Marker Circuit.name: Street Marker Circuit
Street Marker Circuit.description: The user works through a prepared network of compatible targeting markers for the rest of the scene, choosing one marked position each turn for a disabling discharge. A target beside that marker takes heavy electric damage; held back, the shock immobilizes them until the end of their next turn. The markers can be removed, and conductive ground may carry current beyond the chosen target. Sustaining the circuit steadily clouds the user's thinking. Strain: severe.

Last Charge Stand.name: Last Charge Stand
Last Charge Stand.description: The user releases repeated broad electrical bursts from their body for the rest of the scene, stopping an advancing group across an open street. Each burst deals heavy electric damage and stuns uninsulated targets; held back, it stops after they fall. Allies must stay clear, and water or metal can spread the current beyond the intended space. When the release ends, the user's brain short-circuits and they cannot act coherently until they recover. Strain: severe.

Streetwide Tape Catch.name: Streetwide Tape Catch
Streetwide Tape Catch.description: The user rapidly layers strips between firm buildings or poles across a street for the rest of the scene. The web catches several falling people or stops a charging group, holding each until rescuers free them; held back, the tape cushions rather than crushes. Heavy vehicles can tear through it, every span needs sound anchors, and sustained output leaves the user's elbow skin cracked and painful. Strain: severe.

Continuous Anchor Run.name: Continuous Anchor Run
Continuous Anchor Run.description: The user fires and reels alternating tape lines across a district's connected roofs and walls for the rest of the scene, carrying one person at a time to safety or wrapping opponents along the route. A wrapped opponent remains restrained until they cut or tear free. The user must see and reach each new anchor, and a failed attachment can cause a fall. Prolonged output dries the dispensers and ends the run. Strain: severe.

Blockwide Beacon.name: Blockwide Beacon
Blockwide Beacon.description: The user fires a sustained navel laser across a city block, cutting a clear route through several barriers in one straight line. It deals massive light damage to anything left in that line; held back, the user aims above people to break empty upper sections for an evacuation route. The user must confirm the entire path is clear of civilians, and afterward stomach pain prevents further firing for the rest of the scene. Strain: severe.

Threaded Passage.name: Threaded Passage
Threaded Passage.description: The user controls the beam in a succession of short, exact cuts while turning their body, opening locks, restraints and debris around several visible people inside one building. Each cut follows a straight line from the navel, and each person is freed without a direct hit. The user must see every intended surface; one obscured cut is skipped. When the work ends, cramps prevent another laser use until the end of the scene. Strain: severe.

District Scatter.name: District Scatter
District Scatter.description: The user scatters balls across several connected streets from a high position, turning entrances, vehicle paths and escape lanes into sticky obstacles for the rest of the scene. People caught by a ball must free themselves or wait for its hold to fade. The user leaves a clearly marked evacuation lane, but cannot make the balls spare an unmarked civilian; the mass plucking draws blood and ends further ball use. Strain: severe.

Rebound Corridor.name: Rebound Corridor
Rebound Corridor.description: The user places a precise chain of balls across a damaged building, then rebounds through turns, vertical shafts and broken rooms to retrieve several stranded people one at a time. The user chooses each landing so a passenger never touches a sticky ball. The route lasts for the rest of the scene, but a missing or covered ball breaks that section, and the user's scalp needs rest afterward. Strain: severe.

Building Bearer.name: Building Bearer
Building Bearer.description: After consuming a large prepared sugar supply, the user supports a failing section of a building for the rest of the scene, keeping a floor and its escape route open while many people leave. They must remain planted at one load-bearing point and cannot protect another area at the same time. Their thinking grows severely dull during the effort, and the structure needs permanent support before they release it. Strain: severe.

Measured Power.name: Measured Power
Measured Power.description: The user divides a prepared sugar supply into successive short strength surges, adjusting their grip between them to move heavy debris around several trapped people without crushing the spaces they occupy. Each surge still dulls the user's thinking, so an ally must give simple directions and check each placement. When the supply is spent, the user loses the boost and must rest before another activation. Strain: severe.

Building Survey.name: Building Survey
Building Survey.description: The user grows and extends a dense spread of additional arm branches through the open passages of a building, forming eyes and ears at their ends. For the rest of the scene they can report visible hazards and audible survivors across several floors to an evacuation team. The branches cannot cross sealed walls, and the flood of separate sights and sounds prevents the user from following a detailed conversation. Strain: severe.

Shelter of Hands.name: Shelter of Hands
Shelter of Hands.description: The user branches their extra arms into many shorter gripping limbs around a group within one room, holding people steady and catching loose debris while guiding them toward an exit. The protection lasts until the end of the user's next turn and stops impacts the limbs can physically reach. Each caught blow hurts the user, and they must remain anchored in the room; afterward the injured arms need rest. Strain: severe.

Unbroken Tail Circuit.name: Unbroken Tail Circuit
Unbroken Tail Circuit.description: The user sustains coordinated tail braces, close blocks and footwork for five minutes while escorting people through a damaged building. Each turn they can steady one person within two meters against a stumble while keeping their own footing. The tail remains its normal length and cannot stop heavy rubble; afterward its base cramps and cannot bear weight until the user rests. Strain: severe.

Tail Counter Capture.name: Tail Counter Capture
Tail Counter Capture.description: The user combines a hand parry, a tail hook and a hip turn against one visible attacker within two meters, redirecting the attack into a controlled ground hold without a crushing strike. The tail holds the opponent until they overpower it or the user releases them. The sequence requires firm footing and a readable close attack; afterward the tail trembles and cannot strike until the end of the user's next turn. Strain: severe.

Sustained Steel Service.name: Sustained Steel Service
Sustained Steel Service.description: The user sustains the steel transformation for five minutes of rescue work across one building, carrying one adult at a time and shielding them with the user's body from small debris. Repeated heavy impacts can still exhaust the form early, and gas remains dangerous. The work spends the user's available iron reserves; afterward they cannot transform again until they have rested and eaten. Strain: severe.

Heated Steel Counter.name: Heated Steel Counter
Heated Steel Counter.description: The user lets an existing heat source heat their steel body until it glows, then times a punch within arm's reach to deal heavy bludgeoning and fire damage. Held back, the user strikes a weapon or shield and stops before touching skin. The user creates no heat, cannot spare allies from hot contact and must leave the heat this turn; afterward they need cooling and rest before transforming again. Strain: severe.

Sustained Hand Evacuation.name: Sustained Hand Evacuation
Sustained Hand Evacuation.description: The user keeps both hands enlarged for five minutes while evacuating a building, carrying up to two cooperative adults at a time in supported palms through clear passages. Each trip still requires walking and room for the hands; no one gains protection from gas or heavy collapse. Repeated loads exhaust the shoulders, and afterward the user cannot enlarge their hands again until they rest. Strain: severe.

Graduated Palm Catch.name: Graduated Palm Catch
Graduated Palm Catch.description: The user catches one adult falling from a window up to one story above, enlarging both hands beneath them and lowering their arms while bending the knees to slow the fall. The user adjusts hand size and finger placement to support the head and torso without crushing. The catch requires firm footing and a visible fall; greater height can injure both, and afterward the hands cannot bear another passenger until rest. Strain: severe.

Building Vine Enclosure.name: Building Vine Enclosure
Building Vine Enclosure.description: The user spreads healthy vine hair around the open corridors and exterior of one small building within fifty meters for three turns, screening exits and loosely binding up to eight visible opponents. One marked exit remains open for evacuation, and faces and airways stay clear. Solid walls block the spread unless a gap exists; fire or cutting can open routes, and afterward the spent growth needs water and sunlight to recover. Strain: severe.

Interwoven Rescue Lanes.name: Interwoven Rescue Lanes
Interwoven Rescue Lanes.description: The user divides their vines between three supported rescue slings within twenty meters, independently lowering one adult in each by up to five meters over two turns while keeping a clear path for rescuers. Clothing or blankets must cover skin against thorns. Every sling needs an intact anchored bundle, and the user stays braced and cannot attack; a severed support drops its load, and afterward neck strain prevents further lifting until rest. Strain: severe.

Wide Area Watch.name: Wide Area Watch
Wide Area Watch.description: The user maintains the full spread of up to fifty pieces across several neighboring streets for the rest of the scene. Detached eyes and ears relay where people are trapped or fleeing, while hands open accessible doors and guide evacuees. Each piece still has to travel through an actual opening, and several destroyed or trapped pieces leave the user too drained to regenerate them all during the scene. Strain: severe.

Last Piece Return.name: Last Piece Return
Last Piece Return.description: The user scatters nearly the whole body before a crushing impact, steering the pieces clear and rejoining at a safe point within the same street by the end of the user's next turn. They may bring a small carried item held by a detached hand. The pieces must have a physical route to that point; broad flames, sealed spaces or captured pieces can still harm them, and replacing losses leaves the user exhausted. Strain: severe.

Long Passage Run.name: Long Passage Run
Long Passage Run.description: The user strings together memorized wall and floor passages across several connected rooms for the rest of the scene, using rebounds to emerge wherever their planned route reaches open space. They can scout exits and approach a trapped person despite barriers. Each phase still cuts off sight, sound and breath; a newly sealed passage or lost route can eject them into danger, and no passenger can phase with them. Strain: severe.

Return Point Strike.name: Return Point Strike
Return Point Strike.description: The user repeatedly phases around one nearby opponent and becomes solid for a single controlled strike each turn for the rest of the scene. Each landed blow deals moderate bludgeoning damage; held back, it drives the opponent back without a grave injury. The user must breathe and take bearings between phases, and each solid fist or foot remains exposed to a prepared counter. Strain: severe.

Sustained Meal Form.name: Sustained Meal Form
Sustained Meal Form.description: After preparing and eating several suitable foods, the user maintains multiple manifested traits across the whole body for the rest of the scene. Tentacles can hold two nearby people clear of danger while shell protects the user and wings assist a descent. Every trait must come from food actually eaten, and the forms weaken as that food is digested; maintaining them leaves the user exhausted. Strain: severe.

Rapid Trait Exchange.name: Rapid Trait Exchange
Rapid Trait Exchange.description: For the rest of the scene, the user rapidly moves traits from recently eaten foods between body parts, replacing a broken shell guard, extending tentacles to catch a falling person or forming wings for a short glide. Only traits from food still being digested are available. Each new feature remains vulnerable to injury, and the repeated changes consume the user's stamina and food supply. Strain: severe.

Whole Street Spiral.name: Whole Street Spiral
Whole Street Spiral.description: The user releases a broad, controlled spiral down a clear street, pushing rubble aside and driving opponents away from an evacuation path for the rest of the user's next turn. Those directly struck take heavy bludgeoning damage; held back, the wave only forces them back. It cannot turn around buildings, and anyone left in its path can be hit, so the user must clear the route before release. The effort sharply drains their stamina. Strain: severe.

Endless Wave Current.name: Endless Wave Current
Endless Wave Current.description: For the rest of the scene, the user maintains a continuous spiral stream beneath their feet for flight while directing smaller waves from their hands to slow falls or keep opponents away from civilians. Every output still spends stamina, and the waves remain visible and slow enough to evade. When the stream ends, the user must land at once and is too exhausted to produce another large wave during the scene. Strain: severe.

Streetwide Feather Evacuation.name: Streetwide Feather Evacuation
Streetwide Feather Evacuation.description: The user sends their full feather stock along a visible hundred-meter street and carries up to eight ordinary adults at once to clear ground by the end of the user's next turn. Smaller bundles retrieve dropped children or phones instead of adding adult loads. The user remains grounded, needs unobstructed routes and cannot perform other feather tasks until the bundles return; burning or trapped feathers reduce the number rescued. Strain: severe.

Quill Signal Coordination.name: Quill Signal Coordination
Quill Signal Coordination.description: The user stations small feathers throughout one building within a hundred meters and reads footfalls and voices while larger feathers carry two survivors along already checked routes for three turns. The user distinguishes urgent calls from movement without gaining remote sight or seeing through rubble. Dense noise masks speech, all deployed feathers reduce flight, and managing both tasks leaves the user unable to fight until the operation ends. Strain: severe.

Avenue Flame Discharge.name: Avenue Flame Discharge
Avenue Flame Discharge.description: The user braces and drives a broad, concentrated flame discharge fifty meters along a clear street, dealing massive fire damage to exposed targets until the end of this turn. Held back, the user directs a shorter discharge across empty pavement ahead of opponents, leaving them a retreat. The user must clear civilians and fuel from the line first; dangerous overheating prevents further flame generation for the rest of the scene. Strain: severe.

Threaded Thrust Extraction.name: Threaded Thrust Extraction
Threaded Thrust Extraction.description: The user holds one adult clear of their exhaust, uses foot flames to hover beside a window and divides hand flames into fine streams that sever up to three exposed metal restraints within reach. The user withdraws with the passenger to clear ground within thirty meters by the end of the user's next turn. Contact with a stream still burns, hidden restraints cannot be targeted, and overheating prevents more flames until the user rests and cools. Strain: severe.

Repeated Street Retrieval.name: Repeated Street Retrieval
Repeated Street Retrieval.description: The user chains tightly timed bursts and breathing stops along a hundred-meter street, retrieving up to four cooperative adults one at a time over three turns. Each passenger travels against the user's torso to the same clear refuge, with checked landings instead of high-speed collisions. The user needs breathable air and a clear return lane for every trip; a blocked lane ends the sequence, and afterward the user cannot propel until they catch their breath. Strain: severe.

Close Quarters Redirection.name: Close Quarters Redirection
Close Quarters Redirection.description: The user alternates precisely angled sole bursts with brief wall contacts inside a room fifteen meters across until the end of the user's next turn. The user changes direction around two allies, intercepts one approaching attacker and deals heavy bludgeoning damage with a checked kick; held back, it becomes a trip. The route requires visible clear surfaces and offers no protection from unseen attacks, and the user exhausts their stored air afterward. Strain: severe.

Building Concrete Partition.name: Building Concrete Partition
Building Concrete Partition.description: The user keeps both hands on a substantial concrete structure and reshapes connected floors and walls across sixty meters for three turns. The user raises twelve partitions up to twenty meters high, dividing a visible crowd into accessible courtyards with open exits for civilians. The operation redistributes existing material rather than creating it; reinforcement and structural loads restrict placement, and afterward the user cannot shape until rested. Strain: severe.

Braced Passage Exchange.name: Braced Passage Exchange
Braced Passage Exchange.description: The user keeps a hand on a damaged concrete building and alternates precise reshaping between support columns and an adjacent evacuation passage within thirty meters for three turns. The user transfers weight onto new braces before moving the next slab, opening a route to survivors whose positions rescuers already confirm. The user cannot sense hidden people, move reinforcement or exceed available material, and a mistaken load estimate can still cause collapse. Strain: severe.

Athletics.name: Athletics
Athletics.description: Covers: lifting, pushing, carrying, jumping, throwing heavy objects and forcing doors through bodily strength. Not: scaling walls, which is Climbing. Primary attribute: Power.

Climbing.name: Climbing
Climbing.description: Covers: scaling walls, cliffs, rubble and structures by grip and strength, with or without rope. Not: free-running across obstacles at speed, which is Parkour. Primary attribute: Power.

Swimming.name: Swimming
Swimming.description: Covers: moving and staying afloat in water, diving, holding breath and surface rescue swims. Not: rescue work on land, which is Search and Rescue. Primary attribute: Endurance.

Running.name: Running
Running.description: Covers: sprints, chases and distance running on foot. Not: vaulting obstacles mid-run, which is Parkour; moving by Quirk, which is Quirk Mobility. Primary attribute: Speed.

Parkour.name: Parkour
Parkour.description: Covers: free-running over rooftops, walls, railings and urban obstacles at speed, including safe landings. Not: slow vertical ascents, which is Climbing. Primary attribute: Speed.

Acrobatics.name: Acrobatics
Acrobatics.description: Covers: balance, tumbling, flips, rolling out of falls and twisting in midair. Not: evading an incoming attack, which is Dodging. Primary attribute: Speed.

Stealth.name: Stealth
Stealth.description: Covers: moving unseen and unheard, hiding, and slipping past people in the moment. Not: watching a target over time, which is Surveillance; locks and alarms, which is Infiltration. Primary attribute: Speed.

Conditioning.name: Conditioning
Conditioning.description: Covers: sustained exertion, enduring heat, cold, pain and hunger, staying conscious through injury and recovering breath. Not: resisting fear or mind control, which is Willpower. Primary attribute: Endurance.

Striking.name: Striking
Striking.description: Covers: unarmed blows: punches, kicks, elbows, knees and headbutts with footwork and guard. Not: holds and throws, which is Grappling; blows driven by a Quirk, which is Quirk Output. Primary attribute: Power.

Grappling.name: Grappling
Grappling.description: Covers: holds, throws, takedowns, joint locks, pins and escaping them. Not: binding a subdued person with tape or cuffs, which is Capture. Primary attribute: Technique.

Melee Weapons.name: Melee Weapons
Melee Weapons.description: Covers: fighting with hand weapons: batons, staves, knives, blades, chains and improvised clubs. Not: thrown or fired weapons, which is Marksmanship. Primary attribute: Technique.

Marksmanship.name: Marksmanship
Marksmanship.description: Covers: aiming and firing guns, launchers and support-gear projectiles, and throwing weapons accurately. Not: aiming a Quirk, which is Quirk Output or Quirk Control. Primary attribute: Technique.

Capture.name: Capture
Capture.description: Covers: restraining a subdued or cornered person safely with capture tape, cuffs, zip ties, binding cloth or nets, and keeping them restrained. Not: winning the fight first, which is Grappling or Striking. Primary attribute: Technique.

Dodging.name: Dodging
Dodging.description: Covers: evading attacks, projectiles and falling debris the character can see coming. Not: absorbing a hit on a guard or shield, which is Blocking. Primary attribute: Speed.

Blocking.name: Blocking
Blocking.description: Covers: taking a hit on a guard, arms, shield or hardened body and staying on one's feet. Not: getting out of the way, which is Dodging. Primary attribute: Endurance.

Combat Tactics.name: Combat Tactics
Combat Tactics.description: Covers: reading a fight, spotting openings and weaknesses, positioning, terrain use and planning an engagement. Not: directing teammates, which is Team Coordination or Leadership. Primary attribute: Intelligence.

Team Coordination.name: Team Coordination
Team Coordination.description: Covers: fighting and working beside others: combination moves, covering a partner, formations, relaying signals and timing Quirks together. Not: giving orders to a group, which is Leadership. Primary attribute: Cooperativeness.

Quirk Control.name: Quirk Control
Quirk Control.description: Covers: precise, safe and partial use of the character's own Quirk: fine targeting, holding back, shaping, utility and nonlethal use. Easy: a practiced everyday use. Hard: precise use in chaos or near civilians. Exceptional: a fine feat at the edge of the Quirk's scale. Not: raw force or damage, which is Quirk Output. Primary attribute: Technique.

Quirk Output.name: Quirk Output
Quirk Output.description: Covers: the force, damage, area and range of the character's own Quirk when used to attack or to move something heavy. Easy: a standard attack. Hard: overpowering a strong opponent or obstacle. Exceptional: a blow at the very top of the Quirk's scale. Not: precision and restraint, which is Quirk Control. Primary attribute: Power.

Quirk Stamina.name: Quirk Stamina
Quirk Stamina.description: Covers: keeping a Quirk active for a long time, using it again and again, pushing through its drawback and holding on at high Quirk Strain. Easy: a long practice session. Hard: a full fight at high Strain. Exceptional: staying functional past the Drawback's limit. Not: general bodily endurance, which is Conditioning. Primary attribute: Endurance.

Quirk Mobility.name: Quirk Mobility
Quirk Mobility.description: Covers: moving by means of the character's own Quirk: flight, propulsion, leaps, swinging, gliding, sliding and burrowing, including landings and carrying a passenger. Easy: a practiced route. Hard: a pursuit through a city or a passenger in danger. Exceptional: a maneuver at the Quirk's limit. Not: moving on foot, which is Running or Parkour. Primary attribute: Speed.

Quirk Analysis.name: Quirk Analysis
Quirk Analysis.description: Covers: working out how a Quirk works from what is seen, spotting its limits and counters, and using sensing or detection Quirks well. Easy: identifying a common Quirk type. Hard: reading an unfamiliar Quirk mid-fight. Exceptional: predicting a Quirk's hidden condition. Not: knowledge of famous heroes, which is Hero Industry. Primary attribute: Intelligence.

First Aid.name: First Aid
First Aid.description: Covers: emergency care in the field: bleeding control, splinting, burns, CPR, the recovery position, shock and moving the injured safely. Not: diagnosis and hospital treatment, which is Medicine. Primary attribute: Technique.

Search and Rescue.name: Search and Rescue
Search and Rescue.description: Covers: finding and extracting trapped or injured people: clearing rubble, shoring structures, rope, water and fire rescue, and carrying the injured. Not: moving crowds out of danger, which is Evacuation. Primary attribute: Power.

Evacuation.name: Evacuation
Evacuation.description: Covers: getting crowds and bystanders out of danger: calming them, directing exits, keeping order and reassuring victims. Not: extracting one trapped person, which is Search and Rescue. Primary attribute: Cooperativeness.

Perception.name: Perception
Perception.description: Covers: noticing things with the senses: details, ambushes, hidden people, sounds and changes in a room. Not: drawing conclusions from evidence, which is Investigation. Primary attribute: Intelligence.

Investigation.name: Investigation
Investigation.description: Covers: examining scenes and evidence, interviewing witnesses, following leads and working out what happened. Not: watching a target over time, which is Surveillance. Primary attribute: Intelligence.

Surveillance.name: Surveillance
Surveillance.description: Covers: watching people and places over time, stakeouts, tailing through a city, observation with cameras and spotting someone watching back. Not: moving unseen in the moment, which is Stealth. Primary attribute: Technique.

Persuasion.name: Persuasion
Persuasion.description: Covers: convincing people honestly: appeals, reasoning, encouragement and talking someone down. Not: lying, which is Deception; bargaining terms, which is Negotiation. Primary attribute: Cooperativeness.

Insight.name: Insight
Insight.description: Covers: reading people: emotions, intentions, lies, discomfort and what someone needs. Not: clinical assessment, which is Psychology. Primary attribute: Cooperativeness.

Deception.name: Deception
Deception.description: Covers: lying, bluffing, misdirection, keeping a cover story and holding a false identity in conversation. Not: physical disguise, which is Disguise. Primary attribute: Intelligence.

Intimidation.name: Intimidation
Intimidation.description: Covers: frightening, pressuring or cowing people through presence, threats and displays of strength. Not: honest persuasion, which is Persuasion. Primary attribute: Power.

Leadership.name: Leadership
Leadership.description: Covers: directing a group, giving orders in a crisis, keeping morale and taking responsibility, from class representative to agency team lead. Not: fighting in sync with a partner, which is Team Coordination. Primary attribute: Cooperativeness.

Media Presence.name: Media Presence
Media Presence.description: Covers: being in public view: interviews, press conferences, fans, hero image, social media and public speaking. Not: producing footage, which is Media Production. Primary attribute: Cooperativeness.

Etiquette.name: Etiquette
Etiquette.description: Covers: manners and protocol: formal Japanese speech and honorifics, business and agency meetings, ceremonies, and behaving well among the wealthy and powerful. Not: winning an argument, which is Persuasion. Primary attribute: Cooperativeness.

Negotiation.name: Negotiation
Negotiation.description: Covers: bargaining terms: contracts, sidekick and agency deals, prices, broker fees, ransoms and hostage talks. Not: lying, which is Deception. Primary attribute: Intelligence.

Streetwise.name: Streetwise
Streetwise.description: Covers: the street and the underworld: finding brokers and black markets, reading gang territory, hearing rumors and knowing who to avoid. Not: the law, which is Hero Law. Primary attribute: Intelligence.

Hospitality.name: Hospitality
Hospitality.description: Covers: service work: waiting tables, retail, convenience stores, cafes, customer handling and running an event. Not: cooking the food, which is Cooking. Primary attribute: Cooperativeness.

Teaching.name: Teaching
Teaching.description: Covers: instructing, coaching and mentoring: lessons, drills, feedback, exams and helping a student improve. Not: looking after young children, which is Childcare. Primary attribute: Cooperativeness.

Childcare.name: Childcare
Childcare.description: Covers: looking after children: comfort, play, safety, routines and earning a frightened child's trust. Not: medical treatment, which is First Aid or Medicine. Primary attribute: Cooperativeness.

Hero Law.name: Hero Law
Hero Law.description: Covers: Quirk and hero law: licensing, permitted Quirk use, self-defense, jurisdiction, arrest powers, use of force, liability and police procedure. Not: the business of agencies, which is Hero Industry. Primary attribute: Intelligence.

Hero Industry.name: Hero Industry
Hero Industry.description: Covers: the hero world: rankings, agencies, famous heroes and their public Quirks, sidekick contracts, merchandise and hero history. Not: legal rules, which is Hero Law. Primary attribute: Intelligence.

Medicine.name: Medicine
Medicine.description: Covers: diagnosis, treatment, pharmacology, surgical support and recovery care in a clinic or hospital. Not: emergency field care, which is First Aid. Primary attribute: Intelligence.

Science.name: Science
Science.description: Covers: physics, chemistry, biology and Quirk science, including Quirk genetics and lab research. Not: building devices, which is Support Engineering. Primary attribute: Intelligence.

Academics.name: Academics
Academics.description: Covers: academy coursework: mathematics, literature, history, modern Japanese, study habits and written exams. Not: foreign languages, which is Languages. Primary attribute: Intelligence.

Business.name: Business
Business.description: Covers: running an agency or company: budgets, marketing, accounting, management and brand strategy. Not: bargaining a single deal, which is Negotiation. Primary attribute: Intelligence.

Navigation.name: Navigation
Navigation.description: Covers: finding the way: city layouts, trains and transfers, maps, shortcuts and orienting in unfamiliar places. Not: living in the wild, which is Survival. Primary attribute: Intelligence.

Psychology.name: Psychology
Psychology.description: Covers: counseling, trauma care, profiling and understanding behavior, from a guidance office to a villain profile. Not: reading someone in the moment, which is Insight. Primary attribute: Cooperativeness.

Languages.name: Languages
Languages.description: Covers: foreign languages, English classes, translation and talking with visitors from overseas. Not: Japanese coursework, which is Academics. Primary attribute: Intelligence.

Willpower.name: Willpower
Willpower.description: Covers: resisting fear, panic, intimidation, interrogation and mind-affecting Quirks, and holding to a decision under pressure. Not: physical endurance, which is Conditioning. Primary attribute: Endurance.

Support Engineering.name: Support Engineering
Support Engineering.description: Covers: designing, building, tuning and repairing support gear and hero-costume systems, and diagnosing faulty equipment. Not: hands-on metalwork and assembly, which is Fabrication. Primary attribute: Intelligence.

Fabrication.name: Fabrication
Fabrication.description: Covers: hands-on making and repair: machining, welding, wiring, sewing heavy materials and assembling parts. Not: designing the system, which is Support Engineering. Primary attribute: Technique.

Computing.name: Computing
Computing.description: Covers: software, networks, data recovery, security systems and intrusion. Not: building physical gadgets, which is Support Engineering. Primary attribute: Intelligence.

Driving.name: Driving
Driving.description: Covers: driving cars, vans, motorcycles and trucks, including pursuit and evasive driving. Not: moving under one's own Quirk, which is Quirk Mobility. Primary attribute: Speed.

Costume Design.name: Costume Design
Costume Design.description: Covers: designing hero costumes and outfits: materials, function, Quirk compatibility, image and the support-company request process. Not: building powered gear, which is Support Engineering. Primary attribute: Technique.

Media Production.name: Media Production
Media Production.description: Covers: filming, photography, editing, broadcasting and producing content. Not: appearing on camera, which is Media Presence. Primary attribute: Technique.

Demolition.name: Demolition
Demolition.description: Covers: explosives, breaching charges, controlled collapses, finding a structure's weak points and bomb disposal. Not: explosions made by a Quirk, which is Quirk Output. Primary attribute: Intelligence.

Infiltration.name: Infiltration
Infiltration.description: Covers: getting into places: locks, alarms, keycards, security routines and secured buildings. Not: moving unseen once inside, which is Stealth. Primary attribute: Technique.

Disguise.name: Disguise
Disguise.description: Covers: changing appearance: costumes, makeup, wigs, forged papers and holding a false look. Not: lying in conversation, which is Deception. Primary attribute: Technique.

Sleight of Hand.name: Sleight of Hand
Sleight of Hand.description: Covers: palming, pickpocketing, planting objects, card tricks and quick hidden hand work. Not: breaking into places, which is Infiltration. Primary attribute: Technique.

Performance.name: Performance
Performance.description: Covers: music, singing, dance, acting and stage shows. Not: hero interviews, which is Media Presence. Primary attribute: Technique.

Visual Arts.name: Visual Arts
Visual Arts.description: Covers: drawing, painting, graphic design and illustration. Not: designing hero costumes, which is Costume Design. Primary attribute: Technique.

Cooking.name: Cooking
Cooking.description: Covers: cooking and baking, from dorm meals to a restaurant kitchen. Not: serving customers, which is Hospitality. Primary attribute: Technique.

Writing.name: Writing
Writing.description: Covers: reports, essays, journalism, scripts, notes and persuasive writing. Not: coursework knowledge, which is Academics. Primary attribute: Intelligence.

Animal Handling.name: Animal Handling
Animal Handling.description: Covers: calming, handling, training and caring for animals, including police dogs and wildlife. Not: Quirks that command animals, which is Quirk Control. Primary attribute: Cooperativeness.

Survival.name: Survival
Survival.description: Covers: living in the wild: forests, mountains, camping, foraging, weather, shelter and finding water. Not: city routes, which is Navigation. Primary attribute: Endurance.

U.A. Academy.text: Japan's national hero academy: a three-year residential program for high-school graduates, who all live in the Heights Alliance dorms on its walled campus above Musutafu. Principal Nezu, a white-furred animal with a genius intellect, runs it, and its teachers are working pro heroes: Shota Aizawa (Eraser Head), Present Mic, Midnight, Cementoss, Ectoplasm, Thirteen, Power Loader, Recovery Girl and, from this April, All Might. It has four courses: Hero, General Studies, Support and Management. The Hero Course takes only two classes a year; at the televised Sports Festival, agencies scout students and General Studies students can earn a transfer. Outsiders see the country's best hero academy. The visible contradiction: the academy that trains the public's protectors locks the public out.

Hero Public Safety Commission.text: The government body that runs the hero system. It writes the rules for hero work, issues and revokes hero licenses, runs the Provisional Hero License Exam and coordinates heroes with the police. It also manages how the public sees heroes: it releases incident statistics, handles press relations and presents the twice-yearly Hero Billboard Chart JP, which ranks heroes by incidents resolved, public approval and social contribution. Its tower in central Tokyo is quiet, efficient and closed to visitors beyond the licensing counter. Heroes depend on it and rarely love it; to most citizens it is a seal on a license. The visible contradiction: a public-safety agency that worries about approval ratings as much as about safety.

Japanese Police.text: The prefectural police forces under the National Police Agency: patrol officers, detectives, traffic and riot units, custody officers and prisoner transport. They investigate crimes, secure scenes, take statements and make arrests, but officers do not use their Quirks as weapons, so they rely on licensed heroes to stop villains in a fight. A typical incident ends with a hero restraining someone and an officer snapping on the handcuffs. Detective Naomasa Tsukauchi is a familiar face around Musutafu. Most people trust the police and barely notice them. The visible contradiction: officers hold the legal power to arrest, question and detain, yet heroes get the headlines, the rankings and the credit.

League of Villains.text: A villain group so new and small that almost no one has heard of it. Its leader, Tomura Shigaraki, is a gaunt, restless young man who wears severed hands on his face and body, scratches his neck when frustrated and talks about villainy in video-game terms. Kurogiri, a polite man of dark mist whose Quirk opens warp gates, manages him, tends their hideout bar and moves people in and out. The rest are hired thugs found through brokers, and the man Shigaraki calls Sensei backs them all. Their aim is to kill All Might and bring down the hero society he holds up. The few brokers who deal with them see a strange client with money and big talk. The visible contradiction: a League with two real members at the start of the year, led by a man who has never led anyone.

Shie Hassaikai.text: One of the last yakuza houses in Japan, based in an old walled compound on the southeastern edge of Osaka. When heroes rose, they and the police broke the old crime families; the survivors were labeled designated villain groups and watched, and the Hassaikai has lasted by keeping its head down. Its old boss lies in a coma, and the house is run in his name by his young second, Kai Chisaki, called Overhaul: a cold, meticulous man in a beaked plague-doctor mask who cannot stand being touched and calls Quirks a sickness. His enforcers, the Eight Bullets, answer to him alone. Outsiders see a fading relic of the old underworld. The visible contradiction: everything is done in the boss's name, and the boss cannot speak.

Meta Liberation Army.text: A militant movement from the early years of the Quirk era. Led by a man called Destro, it demanded the right to use Quirks freely, calling every restriction an attack on a person's own body, and fought the government until it was crushed. Destro died in prison and the army was disbanded; today it shows up in documentaries and textbooks as a warning about Quirk extremism. Destro's writings still circulate among Quirk-rights activists and the curious. Officially it has had no members, no attacks and no leadership for decades, and most people file it under history. The visible contradiction: its central claim, that people should be free to use the power they were born with, still gets a sympathetic hearing on talk shows and online forums.

Wild Wild Pussycats.text: A team of four pro heroes specializing in mountain rescue: Mandalay, whose Quirk lets her speak into many people's minds at once; Pixie-Bob, who shapes earth into moving beasts; Ragdoll, who can locate up to a hundred people and read their condition; and Tiger, a hard-hitting martial artist who can bend his body freely. They wear matching cat-themed costumes, strike a team pose whenever they introduce themselves and have worked together for well over a decade. Their lodge sits on their own land, a huge stretch of the Japanese Alps northwest of Musutafu, which U.A. uses for summer training camps. Outsiders see a cheerful, slightly old-fashioned idol team. The visible contradiction: behind the cat ears and the pose, most of their work is grim searches for people lost in the mountains.

Endeavor Hero Agency.text: The agency of Endeavor (Enji Todoroki), the Number Two hero at the start of the year, run from a tower in central Tokyo. Endeavor holds the record for the most incidents resolved in Japan's history, and the agency is built for volume: dozens of sidekicks on rotating shifts, an operations floor that tracks incidents across the city in real time, and a training gym where everyone is expected to keep pace. Sidekicks such as Burnin, Kido and Onima work in his shadow and know that his standards do not bend. The public respects his results and does not much like him: he ignores fans, refuses interviews he considers pointless and treats second place as an insult. The visible contradiction: the country's most effective hero is also one of its least loved.

Shiketsu Academy.text: The great hero academy of western Japan and U.A.'s closest rival: people speak of U.A. in the east and Shiketsu in the west. It trains high-school graduates over three years and is nearly as hard to enter. Its students wear dark formal uniforms with peaked caps, keep strict manners in public and train in rescue, teamwork and public conduct as hard as in combat; Shiketsu teaches that a hero's image is part of the job. Its first-years include Inasa Yoarashi, a huge, loud young man with a powerful wind Quirk who turned down a place at U.A. Outsiders see polished, reliable future heroes. The visible contradiction: an academy built on composure and modesty puts real energy into proving it is better than U.A.

Villain Brokers.text: Not one organization but a trade: the middlemen of Japan's underworld. Brokers sell introductions between villains and clients, rent out safe rooms and hideouts, supply forged IDs, unregistered support gear and weapons, and find hired muscle for anyone who pays. They work by burner phone from bar back rooms and pawnshops in port and nightlife districts. The best known is Giran, a smooth, sharp-dressed broker who has outlasted most of his clients by never taking sides. The police know many brokers' names and can prove little. To the few outsiders aware of them, brokers are shady businessmen. The visible contradiction: brokers rarely commit a crime themselves, yet almost no villain operation happens without one.

Hawks Hero Agency.text: The agency of Hawks, the Number Three hero at the start of the year, based in Fukuoka. Hawks is the youngest hero ever to reach the top ten: a quick, easygoing man in his mid-twenties with large crimson wings whose feathers he can detach and steer one by one, fine enough to sense vibrations and strong enough to carry people. He is so fast that his own sidekicks often arrive only to file the paperwork. The agency is small and lean: a handful of sidekicks, a dispatch desk and a press office answering questions about cases he closed an hour ago. Fans love his relaxed manner and his line that he wants a world where heroes have free time. The visible contradiction: the hero who talks about slowing down is the fastest worker in the country.

The Age of Quirks.text: Generations ago, a baby was born in Qingqing City, China, glowing with a soft light. It was the first superhuman birth the world widely heard about, and within a few years similar reports came from everywhere. Children began manifesting powers that came to be called Quirks: flight, fire, extra limbs, strange senses. Laws, jobs, sports and insurance had all been built for ordinary bodies, and the old order cracked. Crime by people with powers grew faster than the police could answer it, governments struggled to keep control, and much of society's energy went into holding itself together. In that disorder some people used their powers to protect others with no legal right to do so. The state eventually answered with a system: Quirk registration, laws against public Quirk use and a licensed profession of heroes paid and regulated by the government. In Japan the Hero Public Safety Commission runs that system, and it has become the center of public life. Today about four in five people have a Quirk, and almost nobody alive remembers a world without them. Heroes are public servants, celebrities and the national ideal at once; children grow up with hero figures and ranking shows, and the hero academies are among the most competitive schools in the country. The chaotic early decades survive in textbooks and documentaries, and they remain the reason the rules exist: every restriction on Quirk use is the state's answer to the years when anyone with a dangerous power could do as they pleased.

Quirk Genetics and Inheritance.text: Quirks run in families. A child's Quirk usually takes after one parent's, mixes features of both, or turns out as something new that grows out of the family's traits. The child of a parent who hardens their skin and a parent who breathes underwater may inherit either power, a blend of the two or something neither parent has. Mutation happens too: parents with ordinary-looking bodies can have a heteromorph child, or a child with a power that has no clear family source, and doctors treat this as normal variation. Families with famous Quirks draw close attention from the press and from agencies watching for the next generation of talent. Choosing a partner for the power a child might inherit is called a Quirk marriage. It was common in the early generations and some old families still arrange them quietly, but the public now treats the practice as a scandal: marrying for a Quirk means treating a spouse and children as a breeding project, and any public figure suspected of it pays in reputation. Most families simply hope a child's Quirk turns out safe, useful and easy to live with. No test can promise a particular result before a child is born, and two siblings raised in the same house can have entirely different powers.

Quirk Singularity Theory.text: A fringe theory, discussed more often in pop-science books and late-night talk shows than in policy, holds that Quirks grow stronger, more complex and harder to control with each generation. Its supporters point to children whose powers outstrip both parents', to blended Quirks that combine several family traits, and to the number of young children who need specialist help to keep their Quirks in check. Their prediction is grim: at some point Quirks will outgrow the bodies that carry them, and a generation will be born that cannot control its own powers at all. Most scientists dismiss the theory as alarmism. They note that the data are thin, that strong Quirks are easier to notice than weak ones, and that better counseling and training have kept childhood accidents in check. The theory has no official standing: the government does not plan around it, hero academies do not teach it as fact, and its proponents carry little weight in their fields. It survives on online forums and in the occasional documentary, and people bring it up again whenever a child's Quirk causes a disaster on the evening news. For most people it is an unsettling idea that is easy to set aside.

Quirklessness.text: About one in five people have no Quirk, and the share is smaller among the young. Doctors can usually confirm it in early childhood with an X-ray of the foot: a little toe with a single joint is the common modern pattern and goes with a Quirk, while two joints is the older human pattern and almost always means no Quirk will ever appear. Families often take the diagnosis hard, because hero culture shapes childhood. A Quirkless child is pitied by adults and often teased or bullied by other children, and one who still wants to be a hero is usually told to give up the idea. No law bars Quirkless people from any job, school or exam, and most live ordinary lives as office workers, teachers, doctors, engineers, police officers and parents. Many grandparents are Quirkless and think nothing of it. The barriers are quieter: a teacher's lowered expectations, a sports club that assumes a power, a careless joke at a party, a job interview that drifts toward what the applicant cannot do. Hero work is the one field where the gap is real, since a professional hero has to face people with dangerous Quirks, and no Quirkless hero holds a high ranking. Quirkless adults who choose rescue, police or support work rely on training, gear and judgment, and they earn respect slowly.

Quirk Types.text: People sort Quirks into three broad types, and the words appear on school forms, in news reports and in everyday talk. Emitter Quirks produce or control something beyond the normal body: fire, electricity, ice, sound, force, a change in gravity, a substance released from the skin. Most Emitters switch on and off at will and work at a distance, and their limits show up as fuel, range or strain. Transformation Quirks change the body for a time: hardened skin, a larger size, a beast form, a body of liquid or metal. The user chooses when to change, and the change ends in fatigue, hunger or a vulnerable recovery period. Mutant Quirks are permanent features of the body: an animal head, gills, extra arms, a tail, wings, unusual eyes. They are always present, and any special function they carry comes from the body itself. The categories overlap at the edges and are rough tools, not a ranking. A weak-looking Quirk can be decisive in the right job, and a flashy one can be nearly useless indoors. Counselors, teachers and agencies care less about the category than about the specifics: what triggers a Quirk, what it costs, how long it lasts and how much of it the user's body can handle.

Heteromorphs and Prejudice.text: People whose Mutant Quirks give them visibly nonhuman bodies are called heteromorphs: animal heads, scales, stone skin, extra limbs, wings, tails. Cities have grown used to them. Some trains have wider doors and reinforced seats, clothing makers sell cuts for tails, wings and extra arms, and heteromorph pros can be national stars; Gang Orca, a top hero with the head and strength of an orca, is known across the country. Accommodation is still uneven: a uniform that does not fit, a helmet built only for a human head, a clinic without the right equipment, a public bath that turns away anyone with scales. Prejudice runs hardest in some isolated rural towns, where heteromorph children can be shunned, kept at home or blamed for bad luck, and adults who grew up that way often carry the scars long after they move away. In the cities the discrimination is quieter: an apartment that is suddenly taken when a heteromorph applicant arrives, a job interview that ends early, a stranger who changes seats on the train, an officer who questions the person with the frightening face first. Most heteromorphs want to be treated as individuals rather than as bodies. Many build ordinary lives, some turn their looks into an advantage in rescue or entertainment work, and a bitter few decide society will never accept them and stop trying. Activists push for better laws and design, and slurs that were common a generation ago now draw public criticism.

Quirk Registration and Counseling.text: Every Quirk in Japan is registered. When a child manifests a power, usually around age four, the family takes them to a doctor or a licensed Quirk counselor. The counselor examines the Quirk, gives it a working name and a description, notes its type, triggers and risks, and files it with the national registry. Children whose Quirk has not appeared by the usual age get a medical check, and the finding is recorded the same way. Counseling continues wherever a Quirk is dangerous to the child or to others: counselors teach control, safe habits and the law, and they advise parents and schools. Good counseling helps a child live with their power without shame; rigid counseling teaches a child to hide what they are, and some people resent it for life. Registry records follow a person into adulthood. A registered Quirk appears in school and hospital files, and employers may ask about it where safety depends on it. A Quirk that grows, changes or turns out to work differently than first thought should be updated, and updates for late developers are routine paperwork. The police and the Hero Public Safety Commission can consult the registry in an investigation, which is one reason Quirk criminals are often identified quickly. A private citizen cannot look up a stranger's Quirk, and the registry holds only what was reported to it.

Quirk Manifestation.text: Most Quirks appear in early childhood, usually by about age four. The first sign can be small: sparks from a fingertip, toys floating when a toddler cries, a sudden change in skin or hair. Mutant traits are often visible from birth and grow more pronounced over time. A first manifestation can be frightening and sometimes dangerous, and parents, preschools and pediatricians are trained to expect one. Late bloomers exist. A Quirk can stay hidden for years when its trigger never comes up, when it is too subtle to notice or when the body is not yet ready, and a rare few appear only in the teens or later. Doctors treat late onset as unusual but real, and the registry is updated when it happens. Quirks also grow. Strong emotion or sudden danger can push a Quirk past its usual limits for a moment, and everyone has heard stories of a power that doubled in a crisis. Those surges are real but costly and unreliable, and nobody builds a career on them. Steady growth comes from training, and it works at any age: control, range, output and endurance all improve with practice and a body conditioned to carry the power. Adults who begin serious training late can still make large gains, and hero academies expect every student's Quirk to change over three years of work.

Quirk Drawbacks and the Body.text: Every Quirk has a cost, because every Quirk runs through a body. Emitters strain whatever produces their effect: a fire user overheats, a sound user strains their throat, a user who burns body fat, sugar or water runs dry and has to eat or drink, an electric user who overloads is left dazed and slow. Transformations end in fatigue, soreness or a vulnerable recovery period. Mutant bodies can need more food, special care or gear built for them. Some Quirks have recoil: a power stronger than its user's frame can tear muscle or break bone with each use. Others come with conditions: a maximum duration, a cooldown, a trigger that needs line of sight, a sense lost while the Quirk is active. Pushing past a limit is possible and dangerous, and a hero who ignores the cost is called reckless, not brave. Bodies adapt. Repeated, careful use builds tolerance, and training the muscles, lungs and nerves around a Quirk raises its safe ceiling. Hero academies track each student's limits, and at U.A. Academy Recovery Girl heals injuries by drawing on the patient's own stamina, so even treatment costs something. Support gear manages many drawbacks with cooling layers, recoil-absorbing gauntlets and supply packs. No training or gear removes a drawback entirely, and the most respected pros are the ones who know exactly where their own limits lie.

Quirk Training and Technique.text: Professional heroes treat a Quirk as a skill. Training starts with control: switching the Quirk on and off cleanly, aiming it, holding it steady while moving and using it under stress without hurting allies. Then come output and endurance. Many heroes think of output as a dial rather than a switch and train to use exactly as much power as a situation needs; some measure it as a percentage of their maximum and drill holding fixed levels.
