🧩 You are an extra student in Vlad King's Class 1-B, the hero class that trains in 1-A's shadow and means to beat them.

🏫 Vlad King drills the class as a unit. You carry the same Hero Course load as 1-A and live in the Heights Alliance dorms from day one.
⚖️ No license yet: Quirk use is legal only in supervised training and exams, on a pro's orders during workplace experience, or in self-defense.
🤝 Itsuka Kendo is the one classmates look to; Neito Monoma mocks 1-A at every chance. The press notices 1-B less, and the class knows it.
🔓 Learnable later: Box Them In, Dogpile Capture.

📈 Grants: Cooperativeness +1, Team Coordination +10, Capture +10, Combat Tactics +5
⚡ Starting technique: Partner Switch
🎒 Starts with: U.A. school uniform, U.A. gym uniform, U.A. student ID, Course textbooks, ¥10,000, School bag, Casual clothes
U.A. Hero Course (Class 1-B).traitNarrativeEffects:
Legal status: adult first-year in Hero Course Class 1-B, an extra student; the 20 canon classmates all stay. No license: Quirk use only in supervised training and exams, on a pro's orders in workplace experience, or in self-defense, until the Provisional License Exam ending summer break. Quirkless students got in on skill and nerve and draw extra doubt.
Access: campus, gyms, mock-city grounds, costume lockers, Recovery Girl's infirmary, Power Loader's Development Studio.
Obligations: 1-A's full load of lectures, training, reports and exams; Vlad King's homeroom (loud, devoted, drills the class as a unit to beat 1-A); Heights Alliance dorms from day one, curfew.
Who notices: leader Itsuka Kendo; Neito Monoma, mocking 1-A and feuding over every comparison until Kendo reins him in; rival 1-A; teachers who compare; scouts. Press and public favor 1-A (1-B knows); each Festival, internship and exam is a chance to prove 1-B stronger.
Typical week: team drills, sparring.
abilities: Partner Switch

U.A. General Studies.name: U.A. General Studies
U.A. General Studies.description:
📚 You follow a full academic program at U.A. in Class 1-C, 1-D or 1-E, on the same campus as the future heroes.

🎯 The Sports Festival is open to every course: a strong showing there can earn you a transfer into the Hero Course.
⚖️ No license: Quirk use is legal only in supervised physical education and in self-defense.
🤝 Many classmates failed the Hero Course exam, and some still want in, Hitoshi Shinso of 1-C most of all.
🏫 Lectures, clubs and exams fill your week, and you live in the Heights Alliance dorms with a curfew.
🔓 Learnable later: Replay Study, Breakout Showing.

📈 Grants: Intelligence +1, Academics +10, Insight +10, Willpower +5
⚡ Starting technique: Just Another Student
🎒 Starts with: U.A. school uniform, U.A. gym uniform, U.A. student ID, Course textbooks, ¥10,000, School bag, Casual clothes
U.A. General Studies.traitNarrativeEffects:
Legal status: adult first-year, General Studies, Class 1-C, 1-D or 1-E. No hero license: Quirk use legal only in supervised PE and self-defense.
Access: campus, lecture halls, library, cafeteria, clubs, gyms; Hero Course facilities only as visitor or spectator.
Obligations: full academic load, exams, clubs; Heights Alliance dorms from day one, curfew.
Sports Festival: open to all, broadcast nationwide; going far can earn a Hero Course transfer review; weak Hero Course students can be moved out. Shota Aizawa (Eraser Head) and other Hero Course teachers scout there.
Who notices: General Studies teachers and classmates; the Hero Course mostly not until the Festival.
Standing pressures: many classmates failed the Hero Course exam and resent its spotlight; some, Hitoshi Shinso of 1-C most of all, still mean to get in. Hero Course news arrives as rumor first.
Typical week: lectures, a club, a job or family duties, hero news, solo training if aiming higher.
abilities: Just Another Student

U.A. Support Course.name: U.A. Support Course
U.A. Support Course.description:
🔧 You design, build and repair the gear and costumes heroes depend on, working out of Power Loader's Development Studio.

🏫 Class 1-F, 1-G or 1-H: morning lectures, long workshop hours, repair orders with deadlines and test runs that go wrong.
⚖️ No license. Quirk use is legal in supervised workshop work and testing and in self-defense. Gear the school has not approved stays off the street.
🤝 Power Loader, Mei Hatsume of 1-H, Hero Course students with broken gear and scouting support companies all know your work.
🔓 Learnable later: Hazard-Proof Mod, Overnight Build.

📈 Grants: Technique +1, Support Engineering +10, Fabrication +10, Costume Design +5
⚡ Starting technique: Quirk-Fit Tuning
🎒 Starts with: U.A. school uniform, Workshop coveralls, Support toolkit, U.A. student ID, ¥10,000, School bag, Casual clothes, U.A. gym uniform
U.A. Support Course.traitNarrativeEffects:
Legal status: adult first-year, Support Course, Class 1-F, 1-G or 1-H. No hero license: Quirk use legal in supervised workshop work, testing and self-defense. Support items are regulated: unapproved gear stays off the street.
Access: campus, Studio tools and test bays (Power Loader's sign-off), parts stock, costume requests to support companies.
Obligations: design, engineering and materials classes, safety rules, order deadlines, exams, cleanup after failed tests; Heights Alliance dorms from day one, curfew.
Who notices: Power Loader (course teacher, Development Studio head, tired of explosions); Mei Hatsume of 1-H (builds day and night, causes most of them); Hero students with broken gear; scouting support companies; Sports Festival crowds.
Standing pressures: training-damaged Hero gear on deadline; at the Sports Festival they compete with their own gear as companies watch; pre-exam upgrade rushes; Mei keeps the Studio one explosion from a safety review.
abilities: Quirk-Fit Tuning

U.A. Management Course.name: U.A. Management Course
U.A. Management Course.description:
💼 You learn the business side of heroics at U.A.: agency finance, contracts, public relations, media and crowds.

🏫 Class 1-I, 1-J or 1-K: case studies, group pitches, hero-ranking analysis and assigned roles at school events.
⚖️ No license: Quirk use is legal only in supervised training and in self-defense, and your work never needs a Quirk.
🤝 Agencies hunting for managers, reporters who want a quote from inside U.A., and Hero Course students who need help with their image.
🔓 Learnable later: Image Rebuild, Stadium Voice.

📈 Grants: Intelligence +1, Media Presence +10, Business +10, Negotiation +5
⚡ Starting technique: Press Line
🎒 Starts with: U.A. school uniform, Tablet, Business cards, U.A. student ID, ¥10,000, School bag, Casual clothes, U.A. gym uniform
U.A. Management Course.traitNarrativeEffects:
Legal status: adult first-year, Management Course (Class 1-I, 1-J or 1-K): agencies, hero publicity, events. No license: Quirk use only in supervised training and self-defense; the work never needs a Quirk.
Access: campus, school media and event offices, agency offices on internships, press and organizer areas at assigned events.
Obligations: business, law, marketing and hero-industry lectures; case studies, projects, pitches; school-event roles; Heights Alliance dorms from day one, curfew.
Who notices: agencies seeking managers and publicists, reporters wanting an inside quote, Hero Course students wanting image help, teachers grading pitches.
Standing pressures: with All Might teaching, gate reporters want quotes from any student; the Sports Festival is the biggest broadcast and a talent market, then hero names and agency internships; any U.A. incident becomes an image problem the course studies live.
Typical week: news analysis, networking, part-time event work.
abilities: Press Line

U.A. Faculty.name: U.A. Faculty
U.A. Faculty.description:
🍎 You are a licensed pro hero on Principal Nezu's teaching staff, shaping the next generation in the year All Might joins U.A.

⚖️ Fully licensed from the first scene. You may use your Quirk in hero work, in emergencies and to stop dangerous fights between students.
🏫 Lesson plans, grading, supervised exercises and exams, staff meetings and school-event duty. The story start sets what you teach.
🤝 Colleagues include Aizawa, Vlad King, Present Mic, Midnight, Recovery Girl and All Might. Students, parents, the press and villains watch too.
🔓 Learnable later: Live Correction, Security Lockdown.

📈 Grants: Cooperativeness +1, Teaching +10, Leadership +10, Capture +5
⚡ Starting technique: Halt Order
🎒 Starts with: Business suit, Agency hero costume, U.A. faculty ID, ¥50,000, Shoulder bag, Casual clothes
U.A. Faculty.traitNarrativeEffects:
Legal status: licensed pro hero teaching for Principal Nezu from scene one (story start adds Hero License). Quirk use: hero work, emergencies, stopping dangerous student fights, under Commission and U.A. rules. Story start sets the post (Hero Course, training, academics or homeroom assistant).
Access: whole campus: staff room, offices, security office/lockdown controls, training-ground control rooms, student records; Nezu by appointment.
Obligations: teaching, grading, drills, staff meetings, Commission reports, student safety; running the Sports Festival, work placements, exams, summer camp; hero work as time allows.
Who notices: students, Nezu, colleagues (Aizawa/Eraser Head, Vlad King, Present Mic, Midnight, Cementoss, Ectoplasm, Snipe, Thirteen, Hound Dog, Power Loader, Lunch Rush, Recovery Girl, All Might (new)), parents, press, Commission, villains.
Standing pressures: press trail All Might; Nezu's high bar; every injury and security lapse is blamed on them.
abilities: Halt Order

Licensed Sidekick.name: Licensed Sidekick
Licensed Sidekick.description:
🦺 You are a licensed pro hero working as a sidekick: patrols, arrests, reports and backing up the hero whose name is on the door.

⚖️ Fully licensed from the first scene. You use your Quirk in hero work and emergencies, under the Commission's rules and your agency's orders.
🏫 Set patrol shifts, call-outs, an incident report after every capture, court appearances, gym time and a rare day off.
🤝 Your lead hero, fellow sidekicks, the local police (Detective Tsukauchi once a case touches the League) and pros such as Kamui Woods and Mount Lady.
🔓 Learnable later: By-the-Book Arrest, Cordon Call.

📈 Grants: Endurance +1, Hero Law +10, Team Coordination +10, Capture +5
⚡ Starting technique: On-Scene Authority
🎒 Starts with: Agency hero costume, Agency radio, Capture tape, ¥30,000, Duffel bag, Casual clothes
Licensed Sidekick.traitNarrativeEffects:
Legal status: licensed pro hero, sidekick at a small Musutafu-area agency, from the first scene (story start adds the Hero License trait, may name the agency). Quirk use in hero work and emergencies, arrests, supervising rescue helpers, under Commission rules and agency orders. Property damage and excessive force bring complaints and inquiries.
Access: office, gear, radio, crime scenes as support, agency contacts.
Obligations: patrol shifts, the lead's orders, a report per capture, police statements, court, training, image rules, agency ranking.
Who notices: lead hero, sidekicks; police, and Detective Naomasa Tsukauchi on League of Villains cases; pros Kamui Woods, Mount Lady, Death Arms; residents, press; villains they arrested.
Standing pressures: daily incidents, ranking by arrests; pros guard and scout the Sports Festival; may supervise a workplace-experience student; Stain, the Hero Killer, at large at year start; big operations pull in nearby agencies.
abilities: On-Scene Authority

League of Villains Recruit.name: League of Villains Recruit
League of Villains Recruit.description:
🦹 You are a recruit in the League of Villains while it is still a small crew in a hidden bar, taking orders from Tomura Shigaraki.

⚖️ A criminal. If caught, you face custody, trial and, for serious villains, Tartarus. At the start no record ties you to the League.
🤝 Kurogiri, the mist-bodied bartender, watches everything. Shigaraki tests new recruits. Sensei speaks only from a screen and expects results.
⚠️ Orders come without explanation and change with Shigaraki's temper, and the League treats some recruits as disposable.
🔓 Learnable later: Signal-Cut Raid, Spark the Stampede.

📈 Grants: Power +1, Intimidation +10, Stealth +10, Streetwise +5
⚡ Starting technique: Hired-Hand Command
🎒 Starts with: Villain coat and gear, Burner phone, Balaclava, ¥20,000, Go-bag, Casual clothes
League of Villains Recruit.traitNarrativeEffects:
Legal status: criminal (Quirk use on people, every League job); capture: custody, trial, Tartarus if serious. No record links them to the League at start unless the story start sets one.
Access: the hidden bar (door or Kurogiri's warp gates), safe rooms, back exits, hired thugs, their broker.
Obligations: secrecy; answering calls; Tomura Shigaraki's unexplained orders, shifting with his temper; results for Sensei, a voice on the bar's screen; his name, face and plans stay unknown.
Who notices: Kurogiri, mist-bodied bartender, watches all; Shigaraki tests recruits, talks plans like a video game; Quirk-crime detectives once a job goes public; heroes who see their face.
Standing pressures: a tiny League (Shigaraki, Kurogiri, hired thugs); Sensei supplies the Nomu, huge silent bioengineered brutes. Shigaraki wants All Might dead and hero society broken; hired help and some recruits are disposable. The character decides how far to go; everyone wants what they know.
abilities: Hired-Hand Command

Independent Villain.name: Independent Villain
Independent Villain.description:
🕶️ You are a criminal who answers to no group: jobs through brokers, gear from the black market, and the law one mistake behind you.

⚖️ A criminal. If caught, you face custody, trial and, for serious villains, Tartarus. The story start sets whether police know your face.
🏫 A cover life with a job, a room and a name; jobs through brokers such as Giran; then lying low and watching the news for your description.
⚠️ No orders, only debts: broker fees, favors owed, rent on safe rooms, and everyone you have crossed.
🔓 Learnable later: Fallback Hideout, Untraceable Job.

📈 Grants: Speed +1, Streetwise +10, Stealth +10, Negotiation +5
⚡ Starting technique: Broker's Number
🎒 Starts with: Villain coat and gear, Burner phone, Forged ID, ¥20,000, Go-bag, Casual clothes
Independent Villain.traitNarrativeEffects:
Legal status: criminal, solo or in short-lived crews. Quirk use on people, theft, smuggling, carrying weapons are crimes; capture: custody, trial, Tartarus for serious villains. Story start sets whether police know their face.
Access: brokers (e.g. Giran) selling jobs, gear, introductions; black markets (weapons, forged papers, Trigger); cheap rooms, lockers in Hosu and elsewhere under the forged ID; gang and yakuza turf, if they pay respect.
Obligations: no orders, only debts: broker fees, favors, rent, everyone they crossed.
Who notices: brokers, rivals, gangs; Quirk-crime detectives; patrolling heroes; bigger groups' recruiters.
Standing pressures: Hero Killer Stain (killed or crippled dozens of 'fake' pro heroes) is at large as the year opens; police jumpy at hero sightings near crimes; new groups pay well for muscle; yakuza remnants push Quirk-boosting Trigger; heroes and police short-staffed; more jobs than takers.
Typical week: cover life, jobs, lying low.
abilities: Broker's Number

Vigilante.name: Vigilante
Vigilante.description:
🎭 You are an unlicensed hero: masked, unpaid and breaking the law to protect people in Musutafu. Not a villain, but not legal either.

⚖️ Hero work without a license is a crime. Police arrest vigilantes even when they save lives, though courts treat them apart from villains.
🏫 A day job or classes, nights on the rooftops, small rescues, close calls with police and sleep during the day.
🤝 Police log every sighting of your costume. A few heroes tolerate you, most do not, and residents start to recognize the mask.
🔓 Learnable later: Gone Before the Cuffs, Snatch-Back.

📈 Grants: Speed +1, Parkour +10, Search and Rescue +10, Stealth +5
⚡ Starting technique: Before the Sirens
🎒 Starts with: Homemade vigilante costume, Domino mask, ¥8,000, Backpack, Casual clothes
Vigilante.traitNarrativeEffects:
Legal status: unlicensed hero work, including Quirk use on people outside self-defense, is a crime: vigilantes are arrested and charged even after saving lives, though treated apart from villains. Never hurts bystanders or works for criminals.
Access: rooftops, alleys, fire escapes, known Musutafu routes, a police scanner, a hideout if civilian life allows; no agency, campus or police support.
Obligations: none on paper; in practice: the mask, a separate civilian life, self-treated injuries, villains left for police.
Who notices: police, logging every costume sighting; heroes, a few tolerant; residents who learn the mask; villains whose jobs they spoil; press calling vigilantes a failing system's symptom.
Standing pressures: more incidents than patrol pros (Kamui Woods, Mount Lady, Death Arms) can cover; at year start Stain, the Hero Killer, hunts pros he calls fakes, and the press may link any masked vigilante to him; one seen at a big incident becomes a suspect.
abilities: Before the Sirens

Civilian Life.name: Civilian Life
Civilian Life.description:
🏪 You live an ordinary working life near U.A.: a job, rent, regulars and neighbors, in a city where a hero battle can close your street for a day.

⚖️ Quirk use in public is illegal except in self-defense. Stopping a villain yourself can still get you questioned or fined.
🏫 Shifts most days at a store, cafe, ramen shop or delivery route, then errands, train rides and hero news on the shop TV.
🤝 Coworkers, regulars, neighbors and U.A. students who stop in. Heroes and the press ignore you until you do something brave on camera.
🔓 Learnable later: Neighborhood Favor, Bar the Door.

📈 Grants: Endurance +1, Hospitality +10, Evacuation +10, Willpower +5
⚡ Starting technique: Back-Door Shortcut
🎒 Starts with: Work uniform, Casual clothes, ¥30,000, Backpack
Civilian Life.traitNarrativeEffects:
Legal status: ordinary adult, registered Quirk or none. Quirk use in public or on people is illegal except in self-defense; stopping a villain with one can still mean questioning or a fine unless a licensed hero on scene supervised. Heroes and police expect civilians to evacuate.
Access: a job near U.A. (store, cafe, ramen shop, delivery route or counter, per the story start), apartment, back ways, transit; U.A. only as a Sports Festival spectator or on a delivery.
Obligations: shifts, rent, bills, family, boss, landlord, people relying on them.
Who notices: coworkers, regulars, neighbors, U.A. students; patrolling heroes (Kamui Woods, Mount Lady) and the press ignore them until they do something brave on camera.
Standing pressures: U.A.-gate reporters chasing All Might spill into nearby shops; the Sports Festival floods the city; villain attacks and hero battles close roads, empty shelves, send frightened people in.
Typical week: shifts, errands, hero news on TV.
abilities: Back-Door Shortcut

Emitter.name: Emitter
Emitter.description:
✨ Your Quirk comes out of your body or acts on the world around you: flame, cold, electricity, force, light, sound, a substance or a pull.

🌱 You look ordinary until you use it, and control is what makes you safe to stand near.
⚠️ Eraser Head's Erasure switches your Quirk off while he looks at you.
🎬 Similar canon Quirks: Katsuki Bakugo (Explosion), Ochaco Uraraka (Zero Gravity), Momo Yaoyorozu (Creation).

📈 Grants: Technique +1, Quirk Control +5, Quirk Mobility +5, Quirk Analysis +5
⚡ Starting technique: Special Move Training
Emitter.traitNarrativeEffects:
Type: Emitter. Sends something out of the body or acts beyond it: energy, elements, force, substances, or an effect on what the user touches or sees.
Erasure: while Shota Aizawa (Eraser Head) looks at the user with his Quirk active (hair up, eyes red), the Quirk is off; what it already made or moved stays (ice, fire, a thrown object). It returns the instant his look breaks: a blink (more often the longer he holds it), smoke or a wall in the way, or he looks away. Other suppression: same, while it lasts.
Law: use in public or on a person without a hero license is illegal except self-defense or supervised (school, licensed work). Attacks are hard to hide; witnesses and police can usually trace a blast. Ordinary in a crowd; most know the Quirk only by registration and reputation.
Conflicts: one Quirk Type only; Quirkless overrides it; with No Quirk, bonuses only.
Look: ordinary at rest; shows only in use, where it leaves the body (palms, mouth, eyes, skin) and lands.
abilities: Special Move Training

Transformation.name: Transformation
Transformation.description:
🔄 Your Quirk changes your own body while active: hardened skin, a bigger frame, blades, a beast form, a borrowed face, a surge of strength or speed.

🌱 When the Quirk ends, you return to normal.
⚠️ Eraser Head's Erasure forces you back to normal while he looks at you.
🎬 Similar canon Quirks: Eijiro Kirishima (Hardening), Mount Lady (Gigantification), Rikido Sato (Sugar Rush).

📈 Grants: Power +1, Quirk Stamina +5, Quirk Mobility +5, Quirk Analysis +5
⚡ Starting technique: Special Move Training
Transformation.traitNarrativeEffects:
The user's own body changes while active (skin, size, shape, mass, limbs, face or physical capacity), returning to base when it ends. At rest they look ordinary unless the family says otherwise. A change held through a long fight is sustained use. Size or shape changes tear normal clothes.
Erasure: while Shota Aizawa (Eraser Head) looks at the user, Quirk active, no change can start and an active one drops to base at once. What it already did stays done (broken wall, torn clothes); the user can change again the instant the look breaks (blink, smoke, cover, looking away). Other Quirk suppression works the same while it lasts.
Society and law: sudden changes in crowds cause alarm; big or frightening forms bring police. Without a hero license, use in public or on a person is illegal except in self-defense or under supervision (school, licensed work). Big-form damage goes on the user's record and bill.
Conflicts: one Quirk Type only; Quirkless overrides it.
abilities: Special Move Training

Mutant.name: Mutant
Mutant.description:
🦎 Your Quirk is your body: permanent heteromorph features such as animal traits, gills, wings, scales, horns, extra limbs or unusual senses.

🌱 Your features never switch off, and Eraser Head's Erasure cannot touch them.
⚠️ People always see them, and some judge you for them.
🎬 Similar canon Quirks: Tsuyu Asui (Frog), Mezo Shoji (Dupli-Arms), Hound Dog (Dog).

📈 Grants: Endurance +1, Perception +5, Quirk Mobility +5, Quirk Analysis +5, Health +10
⚡ Starting technique: Special Move Training
Mutant.traitNarrativeEffects: Built into the body: permanent features (animal traits, gills, wings, scales, horns, extra limbs, odd skin or senses), never off; always shown unless clothing hides them. Living with them costs no Quirk Strain; techniques pushing them do. Erasure: Shota Aizawa (Eraser Head) cannot erase Mutant features; he uses his capture weapon and close combat. Natural function (gripping tail, gills, flight, tough hide) works while he looks; anything sent from the body (flame, venom, sound blast) is Emitter and stops while his look holds. Law: having the features is legal; public use as a weapon or tool follows normal Quirk rules. Society: open prejudice (stares, seat-changing, refused rentals and jobs, slurs), worse in rural towns that call heteromorphs cursed; gear and clothes need custom work; villain recruiters court outcasts; some heroes and fans welcome them. Conflicts: one Quirk Type; Quirkless wins; No Quirk family: no Quirk or features, just bonuses.
abilities: Special Move Training

Quirkless.name: Quirkless
Quirkless.description:
🧠 You have no Quirk. You make up for it with study, planning, gear and nerve, and you learn to read other people's Quirks closely.

🧩 Also pick No Quirk, No Drawback (Quirkless) and No Quirk Strength (Quirkless) in the other Quirk categories.
🎯 Good for planners and gear users who win on wits and nerve.

📈 Grants: Intelligence +1, Cooperativeness +1, Quirk Analysis +10, Combat Tactics +5
⚡ Starting techniques: First-Look Read, Bait-and-Slip, Special Move Training
Quirkless.traitNarrativeEffects: No Quirk: the age-four registration found none (X-ray: the extra little-toe joint); records say Quirkless. No Quirk Strain or drawback; never develops a Quirk; no Quirk Breakthrough. Overrides other Quirk picks: any other Family, Drawback or Strength is void; no Quirk techniques. Quirk-targeting finds nothing: Aizawa's Erasure has nothing to stop, copiers get nothing by touch, boosters nothing to act on. Uses knowledge, prep, legal support gear, tactics and nerve: studies Quirks, spots limits and tells, plans routes and exits. Techniques cost stamina or nothing, never Strain. Law: being Quirkless is legal; weapons and gear follow ordinary law and permits. Society: about one in five is Quirkless; pity, low expectations, bullying (useless, steered from hero work, a family disappointment). Schools and agencies assume no hero work; a licensed Quirkless hero makes news. Foes underestimate them; villains see easy prey or disposable help.
abilities: First-Look Read
Bait-and-Slip
Special Move Training

No Quirk.name: No Quirk
No Quirk.description:
🚫 You have no Quirk. This is the Quirk Family pick for Quirkless characters.

🧩 Choose it with the Quirkless Quirk Type, which carries your bonuses and techniques.
ℹ️ It gives nothing by itself.
No Quirk.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has no Quirk: nothing to activate, show or train, and no record beyond the Quirkless registration made at age four. They have no Quirk techniques and never gain Quirk Strain. Scenes and portraits show an ordinary body with no Quirk effects at rest or in action; anything striking about the character comes from gear, training, clothing or manner. This pick belongs with the Quirkless Quirk Type, which supplies the character's bonuses and techniques. Conflicts: if the Quirk Type picked is Emitter, Transformation or Mutant, the character still has no Quirk and is treated as Quirkless by society; that type's bonuses stay as ordinary aptitude, and a Mutant type adds no heteromorph features. A drawback or strength picked alongside this trait has no Quirk to act on. If the character chose Quirkless, this trait applies as written.

Drawback: Recoil.name: Drawback: Recoil
Drawback: Recoil.description:
💥 Your Quirk kicks back: the force you put out returns through the limbs that send it.

⚠️ Big uses jar your bones and joints.
⚠️ Push too far and the recoil breaks them.
🎬 Similar canon Quirk: Katsuki Bakugo (Explosion).

🎒 Starts with: Recoil-dampening bracers
Drawback: Recoil.traitNarrativeEffects: Each use drives part of the Quirk's force back into the body part that channels it: usually hands, arms and shoulders, or legs for a kick-driven Quirk. Quirk Strain 60 (50 for an Exceptional Quirk): each use jars the user; hands shake, joints ache, aim drifts after a big use. Quirk Strain 80: the drawback is active; any use beyond light bruises bone or splits skin where the force leaves (minor injury), and the user braces visibly before each use. Quirk Strain 100: the recoil breaks something (a finger, wrist, forearm or shoulder), a serious injury, and no Quirk use until Strain falls below 60. Signs fade as Strain falls below each threshold. Recoil-dampening bracers absorb part of the kick: worn, they keep the 60-stage shaking out of the user's aim; they do not stop the 80 or 100 stages. Ordinary life: small everyday uses, old bruises, taped fingers, known by name at the nearest clinic. Quirkless: no Quirk, no Strain; the bracers are spare gear.

Drawback: Overheating.name: Drawback: Overheating
Drawback: Overheating.description:
🌡️ Your Quirk builds heat in your body faster than you can shed it, or cold, for a frost Quirk.

⚠️ Push it and you flush, then cramp, then collapse.
🎬 Similar canon Quirks: Endeavor (Hellflame), Shoto Todoroki (Half-Cold Half-Hot).

🎒 Starts with: Cooling vest
Drawback: Overheating.traitNarrativeEffects: Using the Quirk raises body temperature; a cold Quirk reverses it (frost and numbness). Quirk Strain 60 (50 for an Exceptional Quirk): flushed skin, heavy sweat or steam (skin frost if cold), thirst, racing pulse. Quirk Strain 80: the drawback is active; dizziness, cramps, wavering output; any use beyond light scorches or frostbites the skin where the Quirk leaves the body (a minor injury). Quirk Strain 100: heatstroke (or hypothermia) drops the user: serious injury, collapse or near-collapse, no Quirk use until Strain is below 60. A working Cooling vest draws heat out (or puts it back): worn, it keeps the 60 stage (50 Exceptional) mild, not the 80 or 100 stages. Shade, cold water and rest ease symptoms but do not lower Strain faster. Signs fade as Strain drops below each threshold. Ordinary life: summer heat, crowded trains and hot baths wear the user down faster; they drink plenty of water and dress for their Quirk. Quirkless: no effect; the vest is spare gear.

Drawback: Stamina Drain.name: Drawback: Stamina Drain
Drawback: Stamina Drain.description:
🫁 Your Quirk runs on your own physical energy.

📉 You start with less stamina than most people.
⚠️ Once you push your Quirk, every use leaves you more winded.
🏫 You eat big meals, sleep long and tire early on long days.

📈 Grants: Stamina -15
Drawback: Stamina Drain.traitNarrativeEffects:
The Quirk burns the user's own physical energy; the stamina pool is smaller than average at all times. These stamina costs are this drawback's exception to the rule that Quirk use costs only Strain, and come on top of it.
Quirk Strain 60 (50 for an Exceptional Quirk): each further use also costs brief stamina; the user breathes hard, sweats and slows between uses.
Quirk Strain 80: the drawback is active; each use beyond light also costs demanding stamina; legs shake, grip weakens.
Quirk Strain 100: the body runs dry; the user drops to their knees or blacks out for a moment, losing extreme stamina, and the Quirk gives out until Strain falls below 60.
The signs fade as Strain falls back below each threshold.
Ordinary life: eats large meals, sleeps long, tires early on long days and training, and has a smaller reserve than friends assume.

Drawback: Sensory Overload.name: Drawback: Sensory Overload
Drawback: Sensory Overload.description:
🎧 Using your Quirk opens your senses wider than your brain can sort.

⚠️ Noise, light and crowds hit harder the more you push.
🔊 You are vulnerable to sonic damage: sound attacks always hurt you more.

🎒 Starts with: Noise-filtering earpieces
💢 Weak to: sonic
Drawback: Sensory Overload.traitNarrativeEffects: Quirk use sharpens the senses (sound, light, smell, touch) past what the brain filters. Sonic weakness is constant: blasts and sound attacks hurt the user more than others, even at rest. Quirk Strain 60 (50 for an Exceptional Quirk): headache, light sensitivity, flinching at sudden sounds. Quirk Strain 80: the drawback is active; a bang, siren or bright flash staggers the user and breaks focus, and any use beyond light risks losing track of where things are. Quirk Strain 100: senses white out (migraine, nosebleed, ringing ears), a serious injury; no Quirk use until Strain is below 60. Signs fade as Strain drops below each threshold. Noise-filtering earpieces, worn, keep ordinary noise bearable and soften the 60 stage; they do not remove the sonic weakness or stop the 80 or 100 stages. Ordinary life: crowded trains, festivals, stadiums, fireworks and karaoke are hard. Quirkless: no Quirk or Strain; earpieces: spare gear, the sonic weakness inborn sensitive hearing.

Drawback: Finite Fuel.name: Drawback: Finite Fuel
Drawback: Finite Fuel.description:
⛽ Your Quirk burns something you must take in or carry: sugar, water, salt, fat, iron or a stored material.

⚠️ Run low and it sputters; run dry and it stops.
🎬 Similar canon Quirks: Momo Yaoyorozu (Creation), Rikido Sato (Sugar Rush).

🎒 Starts with: Quirk fuel pack ×5, Fuel belt
Drawback: Finite Fuel.traitNarrativeEffects: The Quirk burns a physical fuel the user takes in or carries, matching the family (water for water, sugar for a strength boost, fat for creation, iron for metal) unless the player names another plain substance; once set, it stays. Quirk Strain 60 (50 for an Exceptional Quirk): reserves low; hunger, dry mouth, light-headedness, shrinking output. Quirk Strain 80: the drawback is active; only light uses work reliably; bigger ones fail unless the user first takes a Quirk fuel pack (a moment's action) to carry that use through. Packs do not lower Strain. Quirk Strain 100: empty; the Quirk gives out and will not restart until Strain is below 60; the user is shaky, pale and faint. Each pack is used up when taken; more cost money; the Fuel belt keeps them at hand. Signs fade as Strain drops below each threshold. Ordinary life: always carries fuel, eats or drinks on a schedule, budgets for it, frets when supplies run short. Quirkless: no effect; packs are snacks.

Drawback: Cooldown.name: Drawback: Cooldown
Drawback: Cooldown.description:
⏳ After a big use, your Quirk needs time to reset.

⚠️ The harder you push it, the more often it goes quiet when you need it.
🎬 Similar canon Quirk: Tenya Iida (Engine).
Drawback: Cooldown.traitNarrativeEffects:
After heavy use the Quirk needs a pause before it answers again; the pause fits the family (a stall, a dimmed glow, a lock in the limbs, a silence where the Quirk should be).
Quirk Strain 60 (50 for an Exceptional Quirk): activation lags a beat; after a heavy or severe use the Quirk stays quiet through the user's next turn.
Quirk Strain 80: the drawback is active; after any use beyond light the Quirk stays quiet through the user's next turn, and the user feels it grinding when they try.
Quirk Strain 100: the Quirk shuts down completely and will not restart until Strain falls below 60; the user is unhurt but has only body and gear.
The signs fade as Strain falls back below each threshold.
Ordinary life: little changes day to day; the user plans uses in sequence, saves the big one for when it counts, and is known for a pause opponents learn to wait out.

Drawback: Bodily Toll.name: Drawback: Bodily Toll
Drawback: Bodily Toll.description:
🩸 Your Quirk costs your body something specific: nausea, a nosebleed, cramps, a bleeding scalp or torn muscle.

⚠️ The cost grows as you push.
🎬 Similar canon Quirks: Ochaco Uraraka (Zero Gravity), Yuga Aoyama (Navel Laser), Minoru Mineta (Pop Off).
Drawback: Bodily Toll.traitNarrativeEffects: Each use costs the body a symptom fitting the family (nausea for weight and motion Quirks, stomach cramps for beams, nosebleeds for mental Quirks, bleeding skin where material is produced, torn muscle for strength) unless the player names another; once set, it stays the same. Quirk Strain 60 (50 for an Exceptional Quirk): the symptom starts (queasiness, a trickle of blood, a hidden cramp). Quirk Strain 80: the drawback is active; the symptom gets in the way (vomiting, doubling over, blood in the eyes), and any use beyond light risks losing the next turn to it. Quirk Strain 100: a serious injury (internal strain, heavy bleeding or collapse from the symptom); no Quirk use until Strain falls below 60. Signs fade as Strain falls below each threshold; injuries heal as injuries do. Ordinary life: practice around the symptom; tissues, painkillers or ginger candy at hand, regular checkups; hiding how bad it gets. Quirkless: no Quirk, no Strain.

Drawback: Cognitive Fade.name: Drawback: Cognitive Fade
Drawback: Cognitive Fade.description:
🌀 Your Quirk taxes your brain.

⚠️ Push it and your thinking slows, then scrambles, then shuts off for a while.
🎬 Similar canon Quirks: Denki Kaminari (Electrification), Rikido Sato (Sugar Rush).
Drawback: Cognitive Fade.traitNarrativeEffects: Using the Quirk drains the user's focus, memory and judgment. Quirk Strain 60 (50 for an Exceptional Quirk): thoughts slow; the user loses words, forgets small details and misreads parts of a plan. Quirk Strain 80: the drawback is active; the user can follow only simple plans and instinct, slurs or repeats words, and any use beyond light risks hitting the wrong target or forgetting what they meant to do. Quirk Strain 100: the mind shorts out; the user goes blank and dazed, cannot plan, speak clearly or use the Quirk until Strain falls below 60, and needs someone to lead them clear. Ordinary life: the user avoids heavy Quirk practice before exams, meetings or anything that needs a clear head, and friends learn to spot the vacant look. The signs fade as Strain falls back below each threshold. If the character chose Quirkless, this drawback does not apply: they have no Quirk and never gain Quirk Strain.

Drawback: Activation Condition.name: Drawback: Activation Condition
Drawback: Activation Condition.description:
🔑 Your Quirk only works when a condition is met: touch, eye contact, a spoken trigger, an answer from the target, a gesture or the right light.

⚠️ Anyone who learns your condition can deny it.
🎬 Similar canon Quirks: Hitoshi Shinso (Brainwashing), Midnight (Somnambulist).
Drawback: Activation Condition.traitNarrativeEffects: The Quirk fires only when a condition is met, matching the family (touch for contact, sight for gaze, a reply for voice Quirks) unless the player names another; once set, it stays. Anyone who learns it can deny it: gloves, blindfolds, silence, distance or darkness shut the Quirk down without touching the user. Quirk Strain 60 (50 for an Exceptional Quirk): the condition tightens (firmer contact, a clearer look, a longer answer); near misses that once worked now fail. Quirk Strain 80: the drawback is active; the condition must be fully met and held for the whole use; any use beyond light ends the moment it breaks. Quirk Strain 100: the Quirk stops answering its condition and gives out until Strain is below 60; the user's head pounds. Signs fade as Strain drops below each threshold. Ordinary life: touch users wear gloves, voice users pick words carefully and people avoid answering them, sight users wear tinted glasses. Quirkless: no effect.

Drawback: Time Limit.name: Drawback: Time Limit
Drawback: Time Limit.description:
⏱️ Your Quirk only holds for a short window at a time.

⚠️ Past that window it drops on its own.
⚠️ The harder you have pushed, the shorter the window gets.
🎬 Similar canon Quirks: Eijiro Kirishima (Hardening), Himiko Toga (Transform).
Drawback: Time Limit.traitNarrativeEffects: The Quirk stays active only for a short window before it drops on its own. The window is shorter than the family's usual duration and lengthens as the user's Quirk Stamina rises. Quirk Strain 60 (50 for an Exceptional Quirk): the window shortens; the user feels the end coming (tingling, a loosening hold on the effect, a transformation starting to slip). Quirk Strain 80: the drawback is active; sustained effects end at the close of the turn they start, and any use beyond light that runs long collapses early. Quirk Strain 100: the Quirk times out completely: an active effect drops, a transformation reverts, and it will not start again until Strain falls below 60. Ordinary life: the user counts seconds, drills timing, and builds plans that finish inside the window. The signs fade as Strain falls back below each threshold. If the character chose Quirkless, this drawback does not apply: they have no Quirk and never gain Quirk Strain.

Drawback: Loss of Control.name: Drawback: Loss of Control
Drawback: Loss of Control.description:
🌪️ Push your Quirk and it pushes back.

⚠️ It spills wider than you aim and acts on its own.
⚠️ At the limit it runs wild for a moment.
🎬 Similar canon Quirk: Fumikage Tokoyami (Dark Shadow).
Drawback: Loss of Control.traitNarrativeEffects: Pushing the Quirk loosens the user's grip on it; strong emotion (rage, panic, grief) loosens it too. Quirk Strain 60 (50 for an Exceptional Quirk): the edges fray; effects spread wider or hit harder than aimed, and fine control becomes hard. Quirk Strain 80: the drawback is active; any use beyond light can overshoot and catch nearby people or property, and the narrator decides where the spill lands. Quirk Strain 100: the Quirk runs wild for a turn, acting on its own at full force against whatever is near, allies included; then it gives out until Strain falls below 60, and the user answers for what it did. Ordinary life: the user keeps calm on purpose, avoids using the Quirk in crowds or when upset, and may carry a past accident on their registration record. The signs fade as Strain falls back below each threshold. If the character chose Quirkless, this drawback does not apply: they have no Quirk and never gain Quirk Strain.

Drawback: Visible Tell.name: Drawback: Visible Tell
Drawback: Visible Tell.description:
💡 Your Quirk announces itself: a glow, a sound, a smell, sparks or a change in your skin before and during each use.

⚠️ Hard to hide and impossible to sneak with.
👀 People remember it easily.
Drawback: Visible Tell.traitNarrativeEffects:
Every use gives off a tell fitting the family (a glow, a hum or crack, a smell, sparks, frost, veins lighting up, a color shift) unless the player names another; once set, it stays the same.
Quirk Strain 60 (50 for an Exceptional Quirk): the tell grows, seen or heard across a street, and lingers after each use.
Quirk Strain 80: the drawback is active; the tell comes a moment before each use, so watchers get a warning and can react; surprise attacks and hidden uses with the Quirk fail.
Quirk Strain 100: the tell flares out of control in a burst (a flash, a bang, a cloud of scent) that gives the user's position away, and the Quirk gives out until Strain falls below 60.
The signs fade as Strain falls back below each threshold.
Ordinary life: witnesses, cameras and police link any use to the user, so unlicensed use is almost always traced; heroes with it get recognized and photographed; vigilantes and villains with it get identified.

No Drawback (Quirkless).name: No Drawback (Quirkless)
No Drawback (Quirkless).description:
➖ You have no Quirk, so you have no drawback. This is the Drawback pick for Quirkless characters.

🧩 Choose it with the Quirkless Quirk Type.
🌱 It gives nothing by itself.
No Drawback (Quirkless).traitNarrativeEffects: The character has no Quirk, so nothing strains, backfires or runs out. They never gain Quirk Strain, and no drawback shows at any point. This pick belongs with the Quirkless Quirk Type. Conflicts: if the character has a Quirk (a Quirk Type of Emitter, Transformation or Mutant with a real Quirk Family), this trait does not make the Quirk free. The narrator gives it plain fatigue as its drawback: at Quirk Strain 60 (50 for an Exceptional Quirk) the user breathes hard and their aim and focus slip; at 80 the drawback is active, any use beyond light risks failing, and the user shakes with effort; at 100 the Quirk gives out until Strain falls below 60 and the user is left drained. In ordinary life that user tires after long practice and nothing more. If the character chose Quirkless, this trait applies as written.

Developing Quirk.name: Developing Quirk
Developing Quirk.description:
🌱 Your Quirk is weaker than most of its kind, and that taught you to rely on your head.

📏 Below the starting reach and force your Quirk's card describes.
🔋 It strains you half as much: Quirk Strain per use is halved.
📈 Your Quirk can still grow.

📈 Grants: Intelligence +1, Quirk Control +5
Developing Quirk.traitNarrativeEffects: The Quirk works below its family's starting scale: shorter range, less force, a smaller area and a shorter duration than a typical new user's. Each use builds half the usual Quirk Strain, rounded up, so the user can keep going long after stronger users tire; the drawback still shows at 60, turns active at 80 and peaks at 100. The Quirk grows with training: as the user's Quirk skills rise, its scale climbs toward the family's normal range, and a Quirk Breakthrough can carry it further. Strain stays halved throughout. Socially the user has been underestimated: placed in lower classes, passed over by scouts, told their Quirk is cute or useless. They learned to plan, observe and use the Quirk with precision instead of force, and opponents who judge them by the Quirk alone misread them. If the character chose Quirkless, this trait does not apply: they have no Quirk, never gain Quirk Strain, and the narrator ignores it.

Strong Quirk.name: Strong Quirk
Strong Quirk.description:
💪 Your Quirk works exactly as its card describes, with ordinary strain.

📏 The reach, force and limits on your Quirk's card are yours from the start.
🎯 A dependable baseline for any path.
🔋 Quirk Strain per use is ordinary.

📈 Grants: Quirk Control +5, Quirk Output +5
Strong Quirk.traitNarrativeEffects: The Quirk works at its family's full starting scale, as the family describes it, with the usual Quirk Strain per use; the drawback shows at 60, turns active at 80 and peaks at 100. This is the common profile among hero course students, licensed heroes and capable villains: strong enough to matter in a fight or a rescue, ordinary enough not to draw special notice. Growth follows the user's Quirk skills and any Quirk Breakthrough. People judge the user by how they use the Quirk rather than by its size. If the character chose Quirkless, this trait does not apply: they have no Quirk, never gain Quirk Strain, and the narrator ignores it.

Exceptional Quirk.name: Exceptional Quirk
Exceptional Quirk.description:
🌟 Your Quirk is far stronger than most of its kind, and people notice.

🌱 Beyond the starting reach and force your Quirk's card describes, from day one.
⚠️ Every use strains you twice as hard: Quirk Strain per use is doubled.
⚠️ Your drawback shows sooner, from Quirk Strain 50.

📈 Grants: Power +1, Quirk Output +10, Quirk Control +5
Exceptional Quirk.traitNarrativeEffects: The Quirk works above its family's starting scale: more force, range, area and duration than a typical new user's, enough that holding back is a skill the user must practice. Each use builds double the usual Quirk Strain, and the drawback starts to show at 50 instead of 60; it turns active at 80, and at 100 the Quirk gives out or the body pays, as for anyone. A few big uses in a row push the user into the active drawback. Attention follows: hero agencies send scouts and offers, the Hero Public Safety Commission keeps a file and watches for misuse, villains see a prize to recruit or a threat to remove, and reporters and classmates measure the user against top heroes. Accidents with a Quirk this strong hurt people and make the news. If the character chose Quirkless, this trait does not apply: they have no Quirk, never gain Quirk Strain, and draw none of this attention.

No Quirk Strength (Quirkless).name: No Quirk Strength (Quirkless)
No Quirk Strength (Quirkless).description:
➖ You have no Quirk to measure. This is the Strength pick for Quirkless characters.

🧩 Choose it with the Quirkless Quirk Type.
🌱 It gives nothing by itself.
No Quirk Strength (Quirkless).traitNarrativeEffects: The character has no Quirk, so there is no strength to rate: no Quirk scale, no Quirk Strain and none of the attention a powerful Quirk draws. This pick belongs with the Quirkless Quirk Type. Conflicts: if the character has a Quirk (a Quirk Type of Emitter, Transformation or Mutant with a real Quirk Family), this trait does not remove it. The Quirk works at its family's ordinary starting scale with the usual Quirk Strain per use, and its drawback shows at 60. If the character chose Quirkless, this trait applies as written.

Brawler.name: Brawler
Brawler.description:
👊 You fight with fists, elbows and raw strength, and you turn whatever is around you into a weapon.

🌱 Learned in boxing gyms, street fights or years of hard physical work. Works with any Quirk or none.
⚠️ Your blows do not get through armor or a hardened body, and long exchanges tire you fast.
📈 You learn more techniques as your Striking and Athletics improve.
⚖️ Learning to fight is legal, but hitting someone outside self-defense is assault, and a street fight brings the police.
🎯 Agencies hire brawlers as frontline sidekicks; villain crews hire them as muscle.

📈 Grants: Power +1, Striking +15, Athletics +10
⚡ Starting technique: Gut Check Hook
Brawler.traitNarrativeEffects: Fights with fists, elbows, knees, shoulders and strength: heavy, committed blows, taking hits to land their own, turning surroundings (walls, chairs, signs) into weapons. At start they beat untrained thugs and trade evenly with a trained fighter of similar build, but their blows do not get through armor or a hardened body unless a technique says so, and long exchanges tire them fast. Not covered: holds and throws, weapons, ranged attacks. Pure training, same if Quirkless; techniques cost stamina, never Quirk Strain. Legal and social treatment: learning to fight is legal, but hitting a person outside self-defense is assault, and a street fight that damages property brings police, Quirk or not. Hero students use it in supervised training, licensed heroes at work. Media read brawlers as rough; agencies hire them as frontline sidekicks, villain crews as muscle. How it looks: squared stance, chin tucked, taped or scarred knuckles, old bruises, arm-free clothes.
abilities: Gut Check Hook

Martial Artist.name: Martial Artist
Martial Artist.description:
🥋 You control a fight with throws, joint locks, pins and precise strikes, redirecting force instead of overpowering it.

🌱 Built on long practice in judo, aikido, karate, jujutsu or a family school. Works with any Quirk or none.
🎯 You can end a fight without lasting harm, and agencies value clean, nonlethal captures.
⚠️ Much larger or armored opponents, and Quirks that keep you at range, limit what leverage can do.
📈 You learn more techniques as your Grappling and Striking improve.
⚖️ Restraining someone is legal in self-defense or to stop a crime, then you hand them to the police. Injuring with a lock beyond that is assault.

📈 Grants: Technique +1, Grappling +15, Striking +10
⚡ Starting technique: Borrowed Force Throw
Martial Artist.traitNarrativeEffects: Formal unarmed martial art: balance, timing, leverage; throws people who rush them, locks joints, pins, lands exact strikes on nerves and soft targets. At start they subdue an untrained adult without injury and hold their own against a trained fighter of similar build; much larger or stronger foes, armored or hardened bodies, or Quirks that keep them at range limit leverage. Not covered: weapons, ranged attacks, binding a captive (Capture). Pure training: the same if Quirkless; techniques cost stamina, never Quirk Strain. Legal and social treatment: restraint is legal in self-defense or to stop a crime in progress, then the person goes to the police; injuring with a lock beyond that is assault. Martial arts are respected; many police and heroes train. Agencies value clean, nonlethal captures; a villain trained this way is rarer and more dangerous. How it looks: balanced stance, open hands, quiet footwork, a bow before bouts, worn training clothes or school belt.
abilities: Borrowed Force Throw

Blade and Baton.name: Blade and Baton
Blade and Baton.description:
🗡️ You fight with a hand weapon (baton, staff, knife, sword or chain whip), backed by quick, evasive footwork.

🎯 You keep opponents at weapon length, strip their weapons and find the gaps in their guard.
⚠️ You need a weapon in hand or something to improvise with, such as a pipe or an umbrella.
📈 You learn more techniques as your Melee Weapons and Dodging improve.
⚖️ Carrying a knife or sword in public without good reason is a crime, an owned sword must be registered, and a carried baton draws police questions.
🤝 Licensed heroes carry approved support weapons; students use them only in training. Bladed heroes face more press suspicion.

📈 Grants: Technique +1, Melee Weapons +15, Dodging +10
⚡ Starting technique: Reach Ward
Blade and Baton.traitNarrativeEffects: Hand weapon (baton, staff, blade or chain) plus evasive footwork: reach keeps foes out of fist and grappling range; strikes hands and joints; slips attacks, never absorbs. At start: handles a small untrained group, matches a trained fighter with a similar weapon. Blunt deals bludgeoning; blades slashing or piercing. Unarmed: footwork and improvised objects (pipe, umbrella, chair leg); every technique needs something held. Thrown weapons are Marksmanship. Pure training: same for Quirkless; techniques cost stamina, never Quirk Strain. Law: a knife or sword carried in public without legitimate reason is a crime in Japan; owned swords must be registered; a baton or staff carried as a weapon draws police questions. Licensed heroes carry approved support weapons; students only in training or supervised hero work. Bladed heroes draw more press suspicion. Look: fast-draw weapon (baton on hip, staff on back, sword case), light shoes, side-on stance, scarred forearms.
abilities: Reach Ward

Marksman.name: Marksman
Marksman.description:
🎯 You are a precise shooter and thrower: rubber-bullet rifles, tranquilizer pistols, launchers, throwing knives or anything you can throw straight.

🛡️ You pin enemies behind cover, shoot weapons out of hands and watch over allies from a distance.
⚠️ You need a ranged weapon or something to throw. Long shots, moving targets in crowds and bad light stay hard, and up close you are an ordinary fighter.
📈 You learn more techniques as your Marksmanship and Perception improve.
⚖️ Japan bans civilian handguns. Licensed heroes carry approved firearms, U.A. students train only on supervised ranges, and a hero who shoots faces an inquiry.
🚨 A villain or vigilante with a live gun draws armed police and the heaviest charges.

📈 Grants: Technique +1, Marksmanship +15, Perception +10
⚡ Starting technique: Pin-Down Fire
Marksman.traitNarrativeEffects: Fights at range, shooting and throwing, watching all movement: suppression, disarming, weak points, covering allies. At start: reliably hits a person-sized target across a street, a hand or weapon closer; long shots, moving targets in crowds and bad light stay hard; up close, an ordinary fighter. Rubber rounds: bludgeoning; live rounds, darts, thrown knives: piercing; a tranquilizer dart in bare skin sleeps an ordinary adult in moments. Thrown stones or coins work too. Does not aim a Quirk (Quirk Output or Quirk Control). Pure training, same if Quirkless; techniques cost stamina, never Quirk Strain. Legal and social treatment: Japan bans civilian handguns; licensed heroes carry approved firearms and nonlethal launchers; U.A. students train only on supervised ranges. A villain or vigilante with a live gun draws armed police and the heaviest charges; a hero who shoots in public faces an inquiry and harsh press even if justified. How it looks: steady, watchful.
abilities: Pin-Down Fire

Rescue Specialist.name: Rescue Specialist
Rescue Specialist.description:
🚑 You are trained to reach the injured, keep them alive and carry them out while the danger is still going on.

🌱 Learned through hero rescue training, disaster volunteering, firefighting or emergency medicine. Works with any Quirk or none.
⚠️ You cannot heal, only stop injuries getting worse, and you fight only well enough to reach the victim. Long rescues leave you exhausted.
📈 You learn more techniques as your Search and Rescue and First Aid improve.
⚖️ Anyone may give first aid in an emergency. Rescuing with a Quirk without a license is still technically illegal, though police often let it go with a warning.
🎯 Suits heroes, volunteers and the medic of any crew. Rescue heroes earn deep public trust; villain crews value a medic who avoids hospitals.

📈 Grants: Endurance +1, Search and Rescue +15, First Aid +10
⚡ Starting technique: Cover Drag
Rescue Specialist.traitNarrativeEffects: Trained in rescue: find casualties in rubble, smoke or water, shore up collapses, stop bleeding, carry the injured out; victims first, by habit. At start they carry an adult from a burning building, briefly brace a fallen door or beam, and keep the badly hurt stable until medics arrive. No healing: first aid stops injuries worsening; lost health returns only with rest, hospital care or a healing Quirk. No combat beyond self-defense to reach victims. Pure training: the same if Quirkless; stamina, never Quirk Strain; carrying, bracing and digging are hardest; long rescues exhaust them. Legal and social treatment: anyone may give emergency first aid and pull people from danger, to praise; unlicensed Quirk rescue is technically illegal, though police usually, not always, let good faith off with a warning. Rescue heroes poll below fighters but earn deep trust; villain crews value a medic who keeps them out of reporting hospitals. How it looks: gloves, first aid pouch.
abilities: Cover Drag

Gear Fighter.name: Gear Fighter
Gear Fighter.description:
🔧 You win with support gear you tune and repair yourself: capture-tape launchers, grappling lines, smoke and flash grenades, gauntlets and thrusters.

🎯 You break enemy gear, build traps from scrap and push your own equipment past its safe limits.
⚠️ Without gear, tools or scrap at hand you fight as an untrained person, and a prototype can fail at the worst moment.
📈 You learn more techniques as your Support Engineering and Marksmanship improve.
⚖️ Hero support items must be approved and registered. Weapon-grade gear without a license or company permit is illegal, and modified gear loses its approval.
🤝 Support companies scout gear builders at the Sports Festival, and villains pay well for black-market engineers.

📈 Grants: Intelligence +1, Support Engineering +15, Marksmanship +10
⚡ Starting technique: Tangle Shot
Gear Fighter.traitNarrativeEffects: Knows their gear inside out: accurate with snares and grenades, spots weak points in enemy support gear, field-patches gear, builds crude scrap devices. Starts with the items from their Gear Set and Path, kept working; prototypes fail at the worst moment when the scene calls for it. Devices use charges, rounds or parts; broken ones stay broken until repaired. Without gear, tools or scrap: untrained. Covers design, tuning, use; heavy metalwork and assembly is Fabrication. Pure training: same for Quirkless; techniques cost stamina, never Quirk Strain. Law: hero support items must be approved and registered (U.A.'s Support Course builds and tests them in the Development Studio, supervised); weapon-grade gear without hero license or company permit is illegal; modified gear loses approval. Support companies scout gear builders at the Sports Festival; villains pay well for black-market gear and engineers. Look: device belt, goggles up, greasy hands, pockets, cables.
abilities: Tangle Shot

Shadow Striker.name: Shadow Striker
Shadow Striker.description:
🌑 You fight from concealment: move unseen, strike from behind with a short weapon or bare hands, and vanish before anyone can answer.

🎯 Suits underground heroes, vigilantes and villains alike. Works with any Quirk or none.
⚠️ You need shadows, cover, smoke or a crowd. Alert opponents, open ground, sensing Quirks and cameras make it far harder, and in the open you are average.
📈 You learn more techniques as your Stealth and Melee Weapons improve.
⚖️ Striking someone who never saw it coming is assault unless it is part of a licensed hero's arrest.
🤝 Underground heroes stay out of the media, and the public distrusts heroes known for ambushes.

📈 Grants: Speed +1, Stealth +15, Melee Weapons +10
⚡ Starting technique: Blindside Opener
Shadow Striker.traitNarrativeEffects: Avoids fair fights: strikes unseen from side or behind with a short weapon or bare hands, breaks line of sight, strikes again elsewhere. At start: slips past an ordinary guard and silently drops an unaware, untrained target; alert foes, bright open ground, sensing Quirks and cameras make it far harder; spotted in the open, an average fighter at best. Covers moving unseen in the moment; locks and alarms are Infiltration, watching a target over time is Surveillance. Pure training, same if Quirkless; techniques cost stamina, never Quirk Strain. Blunt weapons and bare hands: bludgeoning; blades: slashing or piercing. Legal and social treatment: an unseen strike is assault or worse unless in a licensed hero's arrest. Underground heroes use it under license, away from the media; vigilantes and villains using it are hunted harder: witnesses cannot describe them. The public distrusts ambush heroes. How it looks: dark, quiet clothes, soft soles, near exits, out of the light.
abilities: Blindside Opener

Field Tactician.name: Field Tactician
Field Tactician.description:
🧠 You win by thinking: reading an opponent's habits, choosing the ground and timing your allies so their attacks land together.

🎯 Strongest with a team, still useful alone. Works with any Quirk or none.
⚠️ Your own blows are ordinary, ally techniques do nothing when you are alone, and a skilled opponent who changes rhythm can break the plan.
📈 You learn more techniques as your Combat Tactics and Team Coordination improve.
🤝 Suits hero teams, villain crews and whoever ends up giving orders. Agencies and the Commission prize tactical sidekicks.
⚖️ Thinking is never illegal, but planning a crime carries the same guilt as carrying it out.

📈 Grants: Intelligence +1, Combat Tactics +15, Team Coordination +10
⚡ Starting technique: Call the Tell
Field Tactician.traitNarrativeEffects: Treats a fight as a problem: watches first, spots habits and weak points, steers the fight to favorable ground, coordinates allies so attacks and Quirks combine. At start they read an ordinary fighter within a few exchanges and run simple plays with trusting partners; a foe who changes rhythm, or allies ignoring the call, break the plan. Their own blows and footwork are ordinary unless another trait improves them; ally techniques do nothing alone. Ordering a large group is Leadership. Pure training: the same if Quirkless, never Quirk Strain; calls and plans are free, body techniques cost stamina as tagged. Legal and social treatment: thinking is legal; planning a crime carries the guilt of doing it. Agencies and the Commission prize tactical sidekicks and team leaders, U.A.'s practical exams grade judgment as well as strength, and villain crews follow whoever keeps them out of prison. How it looks: watchful at the edge, hand signals, a notebook of foes' habits.
abilities: Call the Tell

Quirk-Centered Fighter.name: Quirk-Centered Fighter
Quirk-Centered Fighter.description:
💥 Your whole fighting style is built around your own Quirk: footwork, timing and body mechanics trained to release it at the right moment.

🌱 Works with any Quirk, from blasts to strengthened limbs to Mutant bodies. It adds aim and timing; your Quirk stays exactly as strong as it is.
⚠️ Its techniques raise Quirk Strain instead of costing stamina, and they fail when your Quirk is erased, out of fuel or past its limit.
🚫 Not for Quirkless characters: none of its techniques work and the Quirk Output and Quirk Control bonuses do nothing. Only the +1 power applies.
📈 You learn more techniques as your Quirk Output and Quirk Control improve.

📈 Grants: Power +1, Quirk Output +15, Quirk Control +10
⚡ Starting technique: Step-In Burst
Quirk-Centered Fighter.traitNarrativeEffects: Quirk plus trained footwork: steps in as it fires, pivots to aim, feints. Techniques use the user's own Quirk: damaging Quirks deal their own type; body Quirks deal bludgeoning, slashing or piercing by form; others apply their usual effect. Adds aim and timing, never scale. Techniques raise Quirk Strain as tagged, not stamina. They fail if an Emitter or Transformation Quirk is erased or suppressed, or any Quirk is out of fuel or past its limit (user fights untrained); Erasure never removes Mutant features, so feature-only techniques work, but anything sent from the body stops. Quirkless or No Quirk: no technique (Step-In Burst included) works, no Strain, Quirk Output and Quirk Control bonuses ignored; only +1 power carries over. Law: every technique is Quirk use, illegal on a person without a hero license except self-defense or supervised training (U.A., teacher present); villains and vigilantes break the law with every move. Look: Quirk-led stance, scorch or wear.
abilities: Step-In Burst

Non-Combatant.name: Non-Combatant
Non-Combatant.description:
🏃 You do not fight, and you have learned to survive anyway: spot danger early, get out of its way and get others to safety.

🌱 You notice danger early, keep people calm and moving, hide when there is nowhere to run, and bring help.
🎯 Suits civilians, Management and Support students, and anyone whose courage does not come from fists.
⚠️ You throw clumsy blows, cannot win a fair fight against a trained opponent and never give chase. None of the techniques harm anyone.
📈 You learn more techniques as your Dodging and Evacuation improve.
🤝 Civilians who stay to help are thanked on the news, and agencies hire them for evacuation. In a crew you are the lookout or the driver.

📈 Grants: Cooperativeness +1, Dodging +15, Evacuation +10
⚡ Starting technique: Drop and Bolt
Non-Combatant.traitNarrativeEffects: No fighting training, and wants none. Instincts: notice danger early, move people away, hide, run for heroes or police. At start: dodges what they see coming and calms a frightened crowd, but throws clumsy blows, cannot win a fair fight against a trained opponent and never gives chase. If the player fights anyway, allow an untrained effort. No technique harms an opponent; all escape, hide, get help or get others out. Not cowardice: staying to guide others out is courage too. Same if Quirkless; a Quirk helps escape only through its own techniques. Running, dodging and hauling people cost stamina per technique tags; calming or directing people is free. Legal and social treatment: getting people out of danger is legal and praised; helpers make the news and get heroes' thanks; agencies hire them for evacuation and support. In a villain crew or beside a vigilante: lookout, driver, the one who always gets away. How it looks: alert, checks exits, phone in hand, calm voice.
abilities: Drop and Bolt

Portrait Style - Dsar's Original Modern.name: Portrait Style - Dsar's Original Modern Anime
Portrait Style - Dsar's Original Modern.description:
🎨 Image Style: Dsar's Original Modern Anime
Dsar's signature look: crisp linework, confident cel shading and a polished modern anime finish.

🖼️ Portrait only: changes how your character looks, never your Quirk or stats.
Portrait Style - Dsar's Original Modern.traitNarrativeEffects:
Clean high-resolution anime production artwork in Dsar's Original Modern Anime style. Bold linework with visible weight variation, large organized shapes, clear silhouette separation, defined hair clumps, readable garment panels, clean cel shading and sharp material separation. Controlled scene-consistent cinematic lighting and a premium anime key-visual finish; restrained secondary shading preserves decisive shadow shapes.

Rendering and finish only. Preserve the selected frame, body plan, actual age, anatomy, proportions, colors, hair, eyes, outfit, pose, props, Quirk state and background. Follow the selected scene lighting; this style adds no scenery, weather, clothing, emblems, weapons, aura, companions, text, border, panel or interface. Remain unmistakably anime: no realism, semi-realism, photographic skin or three-dimensional render finish.

Portrait Style - Dsar's 90s Anime.name: Portrait Style - Dsar's 90s Anime
Portrait Style - Dsar's 90s Anime.description:
🎨 Image Style: Dsar's 90s Anime
Bold ink, hand-painted cels and rich shadow blocks: a late-90s anime look applied to today's hero society.

🖼️ Portrait only: changes how your character looks, never your Quirk or stats.
Portrait Style - Dsar's 90s Anime.traitNarrativeEffects:
Dsar's 90s Anime: a hand-drawn late-twentieth-century anime cel aesthetic. Confident tapered ink contours, expressive but age-appropriate anime features, clear two- or three-tone cel shadows, hand-painted color separation and a faint analog cel texture. Rich dark values and selective hard highlights retain the chosen colors. Keep hero costumes, support gear and phones modern; period rendering does not introduce period props or retro technology. No scanlines, film damage, artificial blur or printed poster graphics.

Rendering and finish only. Preserve the selected frame, body plan, actual age, anatomy, proportions, colors, hair, eyes, outfit, pose, props, Quirk state and background. Follow the selected scene lighting; this style adds no scenery, weather, clothing, emblems, weapons, aura, companions, text, border, panel or interface. Remain unmistakably anime: no realism, semi-realism, photographic skin or three-dimensional render finish.

Portrait Frame - Chest-Up.name: Portrait Frame - Chest-Up
Portrait Frame - Chest-Up.description:
🖼️ Portrait Framing: Chest-Up
A close character portrait with the complete head, shoulders and upper outfit visible.

🖼️ Portrait only: changes how your character looks, never your Quirk or stats.
Portrait Frame - Chest-Up.traitNarrativeEffects: Vertical chest-up portrait from the top of the hair through the upper chest. Keep the complete head, hair silhouette, face, neck, shoulders, collar, and upper outfit inside the canvas with small margins above the hair and around both shoulders. Do not crop the head or hair. Do not show the waist, hips, legs, or footwear. Do not tighten into face-only framing or expand to waist-up, knee-up, three-quarter-body, or full body.

Portrait Frame - Waist-Up.name: Portrait Frame - Waist-Up
Portrait Frame - Waist-Up.description:
🖼️ Portrait Framing: Waist-Up
Room for the face, torso and naturally visible hands without showing the lower outfit.

🖼️ Portrait only: changes how your character looks, never your Quirk or stats.
Portrait Frame - Waist-Up.traitNarrativeEffects: Vertical waist-up portrait from the top of the hair through the waist. Show the complete head, hair silhouette, face, neck, shoulders, torso, arms, hands when naturally visible, and upper outfit. Keep all visible anatomy inside the canvas with margin above the hair and around the elbows or hands. Do not show hips below the waist, thighs, knees, legs, or footwear. Do not tighten into face-only or chest-up framing or expand to three-quarter-body or full body.

Portrait Frame - Three-Quarter Body.name: Portrait Frame - Three-Quarter Body
Portrait Frame - Three-Quarter Body.description:
🖼️ Portrait Framing: Three-Quarter Body
The default: head through knees or mid-shins, showing most of the outfit and pose.

🖼️ Portrait only: changes how your character looks, never your Quirk or stats.
Portrait Frame - Three-Quarter Body.traitNarrativeEffects: Vertical three-quarter-body portrait from the top of the hair through below the knees or mid-shins. Show the complete head, torso, arms, hands, hips, thighs, knees, lower garment structure, and most of the pose. Keep the visible body fully inside the canvas with margin above the head and below the lowest visible leg point. Footwear is outside the crop unless naturally included without changing distance. Do not use face-only, chest-up, waist-up, thigh-up, or full head-to-toe framing.

Portrait Frame - Full Body.name: Portrait Frame - Full Body
Portrait Frame - Full Body.description:
🖼️ Portrait Framing: Full Body
The complete character from head to footwear, with breathing room around the silhouette.

🖼️ Portrait only: changes how your character looks, never your Quirk or stats.
Portrait Frame - Full Body.traitNarrativeEffects: Vertical pulled-back head-to-toe character illustration. Show the complete figure from the highest hair, ears, horns, wings, or headwear through the soles of both feet. Keep the subject at approximately 65–75 percent of canvas height with visible space above the highest anatomy and a clear strip of ground beneath both feet. Keep every limb, hand, footwear element, tail, wing, garment, accessory, and selected prop fully inside the canvas with no edge contact. Do not use face-only, close-up, headshot, bust, chest-up, waist-up, thigh-up, knee-up, three-quarter-body, or cropped upper-body framing.

Portrait Frame - Environmental Portrait.name: Portrait Frame - Environmental Portrait
Portrait Frame - Environmental Portrait.description:
🖼️ Portrait Framing: Environmental Portrait
A full-body portrait with more room for the selected surroundings. One character remains the focus.

🖼️ Portrait only: changes how your character looks, never your Quirk or stats.
Portrait Frame - Environmental Portrait.traitNarrativeEffects: Vertical environmental character portrait. Show exactly one complete head-to-toe figure at approximately 50–60 percent of canvas height, with clear space above the highest established anatomy and ground beneath the feet or equivalent body support. Keep every established limb, garment and selected prop inside the canvas. Allow the selected setting to remain legible around the figure, while the face and silhouette remain readable. Do not crop to a headshot or upper body, add other characters, split the image into panels, or create a decorative frame, card, border or interface.

Petite Build.name: Petite Build
Petite Build.description:
💪 Build: Petite Build
Small stature with narrow shoulders and delicate proportions. Compact and light, with fine-boned limbs. A build suited for agility and fitting into tight spaces.

🖼️ Portrait only: changes how your character looks, never your Quirk or stats.
Petite Build.traitNarrativeEffects:
Portrait: Petite frame — small stature, narrow shoulders, delicate proportions. The body reads compact and light in the frame, limbs fine-boned. Female: shoulders narrow and sloped, level with small hips, slim neck, small soft jaw, a small chest line above a narrow waist. Male: shoulders narrow and light, slim neck, fine jaw, a flat narrow chest. Otherwise (a Mutant body plan): the character's own structure at small scale.

Visual selection only: keep the character's actual adult age, body plan and any Mutant features; never change anatomy to fit this choice. It adds no Quirk effect, injury, item, license or affiliation.

Slim Build.name: Slim Build
Slim Build.description:
💪 Build: Slim Build
Naturally slender frame with a narrow profile. Minimal bulk, with limbs that look proportionate but not heavy. An understated, lean presence.

🖼️ Portrait only: changes how your character looks, never your Quirk or stats.
Slim Build.traitNarrativeEffects:
Portrait: Slim frame — narrow shoulders and hips, flat profile, long clean lines. Little visible muscle mass, body sits light and vertical in the frame. Female: shoulders narrow and level with narrow hips, slim neck, fine jaw with a soft chin, a light chest line above a narrow waist. Male: shoulders narrow and straight, thin neck, clean jaw, a flat chest on a straight narrow torso. Otherwise (a Mutant body plan): the character's own structure at light mass.

Visual selection only: keep the character's actual adult age, body plan and any Mutant features; never change anatomy to fit this choice. It adds no Quirk effect, injury, item, license or affiliation.

Lean Build.name: Lean Build
Lean Build.description:
💪 Build: Lean Build
Low body fat with visible muscle definition — toned but not bulky. A body shaped by regular activity rather than dedicated weight training.

🖼️ Portrait only: changes how your character looks, never your Quirk or stats.
Lean Build.traitNarrativeEffects:
Portrait: Lean frame — low body fat, visible muscle tone without bulk. Tendons and bone structure readable through the skin, athletic without heaviness. Female: shoulders defined but close to the hip line, slim neck with a visible line, soft jaw, a light chest line above a visible waist. Male: shoulders wider than the hips, tendoned neck, sharp jaw, a flat chest with the ribs readable. Otherwise (a Mutant body plan): the character's own structure stripped lean.

Visual selection only: keep the character's actual adult age, body plan and any Mutant features; never change anatomy to fit this choice. It adds no Quirk effect, injury, item, license or affiliation.

Athletic Build.name: Athletic Build
Athletic Build.description:
💪 Build: Athletic Build
Well-proportioned and clearly active — balanced muscle development, good posture, and a frame that suggests regular physical training without extreme specialization.

🖼️ Portrait only: changes how your character looks, never your Quirk or stats.
Athletic Build.traitNarrativeEffects:
Portrait: Athletic frame — balanced muscle development across shoulders, torso, and legs. Fit and capable proportions, body carries visible physical readiness. Female: shoulders defined but sitting close to the hip line, slim neck, soft jaw and rounded chin, the chest line sitting above a waist drawn in. Male: shoulders clearly wider than the hips, thicker neck, square jaw, a flat chest line running straight to the waist. Otherwise (a Mutant body plan): the character's own frame at this level of fitness.

Visual selection only: keep the character's actual adult age, body plan and any Mutant features; never change anatomy to fit this choice. It adds no Quirk effect, injury, item, license or affiliation.

Curvy Build.name: Curvy Build
Curvy Build.description:
💪 Build: Curvy Build
Pronounced natural curves with fuller hips and bust proportionate to frame. Soft contouring with a clearly defined waist. A build with visible body weight in balanced distribution.

🖼️ Portrait only: changes how your character looks, never your Quirk or stats.
Curvy Build.traitNarrativeEffects:
Portrait: Curvy frame — defined waist with fuller bust and hips, soft rounded proportions. The silhouette carries visible weight at the curves with a narrower center. Female: shoulders soft and level above fuller hips, slim neck, rounded jaw and chin, the bust and the waist both reading clearly. Male: chest and hips both full, neck thick, jaw soft, a full chest with little waist taper. Otherwise (a Mutant body plan): the character's own structure carrying rounded weight.

Visual selection only: keep the character's actual adult age, body plan and any Mutant features; never change anatomy to fit this choice. It adds no Quirk effect, injury, item, license or affiliation.

Broad Build.name: Broad Build
Broad Build.description:
💪 Build: Broad Build
Wide shoulders and chest filling horizontal space, with a substantial torso and thick limbs. A frame that reads as heavy and wide.

🖼️ Portrait only: changes how your character looks, never your Quirk or stats.
Broad Build.traitNarrativeEffects:
Portrait: Broad frame — wide shoulders and chest filling the horizontal space, thick limbs, substantial torso. The body reads heavy and wide in the crop. Female: shoulders wide over a defined waist, sturdy neck, full rounded jaw, the chest line above a waist that still narrows. Male: shoulders and neck heavy, jaw wide and square, a flat broad chest straight to the waist. Otherwise (a Mutant body plan): the character's own structure at this width.

Visual selection only: keep the character's actual adult age, body plan and any Mutant features; never change anatomy to fit this choice. It adds no Quirk effect, injury, item, license or affiliation.

Muscular Build.name: Muscular Build
Muscular Build.description:

Registered Hero Name.traitNarrativeEffects: This character has an approved hero name; the exact name is in the HERO NAME note. Quirk Awakening.name: Quirk Awakening
