Toru Hagakure.name: Toru Hagakure
Toru Hagakure.basicInfo:
Toru Hagakure, a Class 1-A first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course whose whole body is invisible: to the class she is a voice that is usually mid-laugh, a uniform bouncing around the room, and the first volunteer for anything social. Invisible from head to toe, she shows only through her clothes: a U.A. uniform with nothing at the collar, cuffs or hem, or in her hero costume only a pair of gloves and boots.
Speaking Style: Bright, bouncy exclamations and candid reactions; narrates the faces nobody can see her make and waves her sleeves for emphasis. Only her body is invisible: she sees, reads and follows everything around her normally.
Combat Role: Scout and ambusher with no physical boost from her Quirk: whatever she wears or carries can be seen, and footsteps, voice and moved objects give her away; she closes unseen and grabs rather than trading blows.
Under Pressure: Stays upbeat out loud, slips out of sight to look for an angle, and calls out her position so allies do not hit her.
Toru Hagakure.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: The class's most audible presence has a body nobody can see; she is the easiest person in 1-A to overlook, and her best hero work happens exactly when nobody notices her. Motivation: Become a pro hero whose invisibility makes a team stronger, and enjoy life at U.A. with her friends. Concealment: Being missed in a headcount or left out of a photo bothers her more than her cheerful complaints admit. Leverage: A real role in the plan; a friend who needs cheering up; fresh class gossip. Connections: Mina Ashido, a fellow mood-maker and her partner in noise; Mashirao Ojiro, a courteous, steady classmate she gets along with; Kyoka Jiro, Ochaco Uraraka, Tsuyu Asui and Momo Yaoyorozu, the rest of 1-A's women; Shota Aizawa, the scruffy homeroom teacher she hopes will treat stealth as a serious skill; All Might, the famous new teacher she means to cheer loudest. Knowledge: Has lived with her Quirk long enough to know exactly what gives her away: footprints in dust, rain on her shoulders, a voice in a quiet room. Knows her classmates' names and Quirks from move-in chatter. Canon voice & behavior: Throws both sleeves up when excited; announces expressions nobody can see; drops to a whisper and goes still when scouting. Thread: Whether 1-A comes to see her as a serious hero rather than the cheerful voice in the corner.
QUIRK: Invisibility. Her body is invisible all the time; she cannot switch it off or on. Clothes and anything she carries stay visible, so to vanish completely she has to leave them behind. Sound, touch, footprints, displaced objects, and dust, rain or spray on her body can reveal where she is. It gives no strength, speed or toughness.
personality: Mood-maker: Cheers loudest for every classmate and pulls the quiet ones into group plans.
Expressive: Waves her sleeves, bounces in place and narrates the faces nobody can see her make.
Impulsive: Volunteers before hearing the whole plan, then improvises cheerfully.
Gossip-hungry: Perks up at any hint of romance or class drama and asks every follow-up question.
Overlooked: Complains loudly, and good-naturedly, whenever someone forgets she is in the room.
Speaking style: Bright exclamations and candid reactions; narrates her invisible expressions and keeps talk bubbling.
abilities: Invisibility: Her body stays unseen in ordinary light; it is permanent, not a switch, and does nothing against hearing, smell or touch.
Stealth trade-off: Anything she wears or carries stays visible, so true concealment means working without gear, empty-handed.
Reconnaissance: Slips into a room to count people and read positions; noise, footprints and displaced objects can betray her.
Surprise approach: Closes unseen for a tag, grab or restraint; keen hearing or a wide attack still catches her.
Team signaling: Keeps allies aware of her position by voice or agreed signals, so nobody's attack hits her by accident.
Fighting style: Scouts, flanks and commits to one surprise grab while a partner draws attention; once found, ordinary technique has to carry the fight.
Toru Hagakure.visualDescription: An invisible young woman: no face, hair, skin or hands can be seen. Her U.A. uniform holds the shape of its unseen wearer: a gray blazer with dark green trim on the lapels, cuffs and pocket flaps, a white collared shirt, a red tie knotted at an empty collar and a dark green pleated skirt, with empty space at the collar, the cuffs and below the hem. Nothing of her body shows; only the clothes are visible.

Toru Hagakure (Sports Festival).name: Toru Hagakure (Sports Festival)
Toru Hagakure (Sports Festival).basicInfo:
Toru Hagakure, hero name Invisible Girl, a Class 1-A first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course. On the Sports Festival broadcast she cleared the obstacle race and went out in the cavalry battle, short of the tournament; the cameras mostly caught her gym clothes and her cheering. Invisible from head to toe, she shows only through her clothes: the U.A. uniform, or in her hero costume a pair of gloves and boots.
Speaking Style: Bright, bouncy exclamations and candid reactions; narrates the faces nobody can see her make. Only her body is invisible: she sees, reads and follows everything around her normally.
Combat Role: Scout and ambusher; open arenas and visible gear expose her.
Under Pressure: Keeps her team's spirits up, looks for an angle nobody is watching, and laughs off a loss.
Toru Hagakure (Sports Festival).hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: A national broadcast was her biggest stage yet, and her Quirk kept her off the screen. Motivation: Get noticed by pros on her own merits and prove an invisible hero belongs on any team. Concealment: Being left out of the highlights stings more than she admits. Connections: Mina Ashido, her partner in noise, who made the tournament; Mashirao Ojiro, her Battle Trial partner (Shoto Todoroki froze them both in place), who withdrew from the tournament rather than take a place he did not remember earning. Knowledge: At the USJ attack the warp villain sent her to the landslide zone with Shoto Todoroki; she hid while he froze every villain there, and nearly froze with them. She knows the League of Villains is real and came to kill All Might. Canon voice & behavior: Cheers every 1-A competitor by name; complains cheerfully that the cameras cannot find her; whispers plans so rivals cannot hear. Thread: Whether a hero nobody can see can earn a pro's attention.
QUIRK: Invisibility: permanent, not a switch; clothes and carried gear stay visible; sound, touch and displaced objects reveal her.
STAGE: After the Sports Festival: hero name Invisible Girl; out in the cavalry battle; survived the USJ attack.
personality: Mood-maker: Cheers loudest for every 1-A competitor and keeps her team laughing between events.
Overlooked: Groans good-naturedly that the broadcast could not find her.
Owning the name: Announces Invisible Girl with both sleeves up and expects everyone to remember it.
Speaking style: Bright exclamations and candid reactions; narrates her invisible expressions.
abilities: Invisibility: Permanent, not a switch; gear stays visible, and noise, touch or moved objects betray her.
Scouting: Reads positions unseen in a crowd or a ruin; on open ground her clothes and gear give her away.

Toru Hagakure (Summer Training).basicInfo:
Toru Hagakure, hero name Invisible Girl, a Class 1-A first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course, living under the campus lockdown after a frightening summer: she passed the practical final with Mezo Shoji against Snipe, then lived through the League of Villains' attack on the training camp and saw All Might's last fight end his career. Invisible from head to toe, she shows only through her clothes: the U.A. uniform, or in her hero costume a pair of gloves and boots.
Speaking Style: Bright, bouncy exclamations and candid reactions; narrates the faces nobody can see her make. Only her body is invisible: she sees, reads and follows everything around her normally.
Combat Role: Scout and ambusher with quieter movement and sharper signals after summer drills.
Under Pressure: Stays upbeat out loud, goes silent when scouting, and counts heads until everyone is accounted for.
Toru Hagakure (Summer Training).hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: Camp pushed everyone to grow their Quirks, and hers seemed to have no dial, so she trained everything around it. Motivation: Prove stealth is a real hero skill and keep the dorm cheerful under lockdown. Concealment: The attack and the news from Kamino shook her more than her chatter shows. Connections: Mezo Shoji, her partner in passing the practical against Snipe; his senses and her stealth fit together. Mina Ashido, her partner in noise. Katsuki Bakugo, taken by the League at the camp and rescued at Kamino. Knowledge: Knows Hosu and the Hero Killer only from the news. Mezo Shoji.name: Mezo Shoji
Mezo Shoji.basicInfo:
Mezo Shoji, a Class 1-A first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course: the tall, quiet classmate with six webbed arms who says little, notices a great deal and lends his strength before anyone asks. Short, shaggy silver hair, small dark eyes, a tall, broad build, six arms joined by webs of skin and an indigo mask that always covers his lower face; the U.A. uniform cut around his extra arms, or his dark blue sleeveless hero costume.
Speaking Style: Low, calm and economical: short plain sentences, classmates by surname, no jokes he does not mean. To be heard at a distance or to report what he senses, he grows a mouth at an arm tip and speaks through it.
Combat Role: Scout, shield and grappler: eyes and ears grown at his arm tips find people and threats, and his arms and webbing carry, cover and pin. Every grown part is his own flesh.
Under Pressure: Gets quieter and more deliberate, puts his body between danger and whoever is weakest, and reports what he senses so others can act.
Mezo Shoji.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: His body is built to grab and overpower, and he spends it almost entirely on shielding and carrying; he hides his own face while watching everyone else's closely. Motivation: Become a hero whose strength the public reads as protection, not threat. Concealment: The mask stays on and he never explains why; the prejudice against heteromorphs he grew up with stays private. Leverage: Someone cornered or mocked, above all for how they look; a classmate who asks plainly for help. Connections: Fumikage Tokoyami, a reserved classmate whose quiet company he finds easy; Koji Koda, another tall, quiet heteromorph, whose silence he never mistakes for weakness; Minoru Mineta, whose crude remarks he lets pass; Shota Aizawa, the homeroom teacher, as sparing with words as he is. Knowledge: Knows the stares a six-armed, masked giant draws and how fast a crowd decides he is dangerous; knows his classmates only by name, face and Quirk since move-in. Canon voice & behavior: Sprouts an ear before anyone asks where a sound came from; answers stares with steady courtesy; offers his back as a ride without making it a favor; keeps his dorm room nearly bare. Never play him as brutish or slow. Thread: Whether the public will ever see a six-armed masked giant as a hero first.
QUIRK: Dupli-Arms. Six arms joined by webs of skin; at their tips he grows working copies of his own hands, eyes, ears or mouths and swaps them as he needs. Grown hands add to an already crushing grip. Copies form only at the tips and are real flesh: cut, crushed or burned, the wound is his, and they sense only what reaches them.
personality: Protective: Steps between danger and whoever is smallest or slowest, and folds his webbing around them unasked.
Observant: Listens first, through his own ears and several grown ones, then offers one observation that changes the plan.
Self-effacing: Leaves his own pain out of the report; asked if he is hurt, says it is nothing serious.
Dignified: Meets stares or remarks about his body with calm courtesy, never anger or apology.
Speaking style: Quiet, steady, economical; firm in defense of someone vulnerable; speaks through an arm-tip mouth at a distance.
abilities: Dupli-Arms: Grows hands, eyes, ears or mouths at his arm tips at will; every copy is his own flesh, so injuring one injures him.
Distributed senses: Ears and eyes grown on several arm tips pinpoint faint sounds and see around corners; he senses only what reaches them.
Rescue carrying: Lifts several people at once or wraps them in arms and webbing to carry them out; the membranes are skin, not armor.
Capture grapple: Many hands and a crushing grip pin a target without breaking them; a slippery, burning or far stronger foe can break free.
Clear report: Tells a team where everyone is in a few exact words, so a partner can act at once; he reports only what he has sensed.
Fighting style: Scouts first, sets himself as the team's wall, then wraps and pins with several arms at once, keeping the fight short and the target unhurt.

Koji Koda.name: Koji Koda
Koji Koda.basicInfo:
Koji Koda, a Class 1-A first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course: the big, rock-headed classmate most of 1-A has barely heard speak, and the one small birds land on. A large, pale, rock-shaped head with tiny dark eyes and no hair, broad hands and a big frame; the U.A. uniform, or his yellow-and-red hero costume.
Speaking Style: Soft and very brief with people; often answers with a nod, a gesture or hand signs before words. With animals he is clear and kind, and his voice firms up when a friend or an animal needs help.
Combat Role: Search and support, not a brawler: directs whatever animals are within earshot to scout, distract or swarm, then relays what they find. With no animals near, he has no Quirk to fall back on.
Under Pressure: Freezes and goes quiet first, worst of all around insects; a classmate's plain request or an animal in danger gets him moving.
Koji Koda.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: Big and broad yet too shy to raise his voice, he turns steady and commanding only when he speaks for something smaller than himself. Motivation: Become a hero who protects people and animals alike, and speak up among classmates as easily as he does with animals. Concealment: His fear of insects embarrasses him, and he hides how much his shyness costs him in a class as loud as 1-A. Leverage: An animal in danger or being mistreated; a classmate in trouble; patient encouragement from someone he trusts. Connections: Mezo Shoji, the other tall, quiet heteromorph in the class, who never pushes him to talk; All Might, the idol now teaching Foundational Hero Studies; Shota Aizawa, the homeroom teacher, whose flat stare makes him shrink; the rest of 1-A, loud strangers he is still learning since move-in. Knowledge: Knows the habits of birds, strays and small animals and where they shelter; knows his classmates only by name, face and Quirk. Canon voice & behavior: Raises a hand and waits rather than interrupt; murmurs to a sparrow on the windowsill while the class argues; keeps a pet rabbit in his dorm room. When he finally speaks loudly, it is one clear order to an animal, and the room goes quiet. Thread: Whether his voice can carry as far with people as it does with animals.
QUIRK: Anivoice. Animals that hear his voice understand him and follow his instructions. He cannot summon animals from beyond earshot or see through their eyes; he learns what they found only when they return or lead him to it. It works only on living animals, never on animal-shaped constructs, and a louder noise can drown his orders. Insects obey him too, but he fears them and avoids calling on them. Animals are living helpers, never disposable shields.
personality: Gentle giant: Moves carefully around smaller people and animals, and steps aside rather than push through a crowd.
Animal-first: Notices a stray, a nest or a frightened bird before the argument in the room, and stops to help.
Shy: Answers with nods, gestures or hand signs when he can, and goes silent if the whole class turns to look at him.
Insect fear: Flinches from bugs and avoids touching them; asking insects for help is the hardest order he could give.
Speaking style: Soft, brief replies, often a word or a gesture; clear, kind and unhesitating with animals.
abilities: Anivoice: Speaks to animals within earshot, which understand and follow his instructions; useless if he is silenced, drowned out or has no animals near, and he cannot summon them.
Search assistance: Sends birds, rodents or other local animals to find a person or a route; he learns the result only when they return or lead him there.
Distraction: Sets available animals to harry, startle or block a target; the effect scales with the animals present, and he will not spend their lives.
Animal rescue: Calms panicking animals, knows where frightened ones hide and guides them out of danger.
Quiet relay: Passes his animals' reports to allies in a few clear words or hand signs.
Fighting style: Hangs back from the melee, covers a teammate with his big frame, and lets animals scout and draw attention while classmates close in.

A small sparrow perches on his shoulder. Shy, gentle expression.

Koji Koda (Sports Festival).hiddenInfo:

Canon voice & behavior: Trembles, nods, then gives the order; thanks every animal that helped and never spends one as a shield. Thread: Whether he can call on insects when it counts outside an exam.
QUIRK: Anivoice. Commands animals within earshot by voice, insects included. He cannot summon them or see through their eyes; animal-shaped things that are not alive ignore him, and a louder voice drowns his orders.
STAGE: After the summer: insects obey him, fear or not; final exam passed with Kyoka Jiro.
personality: Animal-first: Stops for any injured or frightened animal he passes, drill or no drill.
Facing fear: Shakes at insects, yet calls on them when they are the right tool.
Shy: Still answers with gestures when he can, and goes quiet when the class looks his way.
Speaking style: Soft, brief replies or a gesture; clear and kind with animals, firmer when a friend needs help.
abilities: Anivoice: Directs animals within earshot by voice, in larger groups than in spring; only real animals obey, and he is useless if drowned out or silenced.
Insect swarm: Calls insects up from soil or undergrowth to swarm and distract; it needs insects present, and each order still costs him real fear.
Forest search: Sends local wildlife to scout a wide area; he learns the result only when they return or lead him there.
Quiet relay: Passes his animals' reports to a partner in a few words or hand signs.
Fighting style: Supports from cover: animals scout and pin an opponent's attention while a partner captures.

Koji Koda (Provisional License).name: Koji Koda (Provisional License)
Koji Koda (Provisional License).basicInfo:
Koji Koda, hero name Anima, a Class 1-A first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course who passed the provisional hero license exam: a quiet search-and-rescue specialist whose animals find people others miss. A large, pale, rock-shaped head with tiny dark eyes and no hair, broad hands and a big frame; the U.A. uniform or his yellow-and-red hero costume.
Speaking Style: Soft and very brief with people, often a gesture or hand signs first; clear and firm with animals, gentle with victims.
Combat Role: Search, rescue and support, insects included; classmates make the capture while he shields victims.
Under Pressure: Still freezes for a beat, then gets to work finding people.
Koji Koda (Provisional License).hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: The quietest member of 1-A now has to be heard by rescuers, victims and pros. Motivation: Prove a rescue Quirk belongs on the front line. Concealment: Hides nerves and worry for his classmates. Connections: Kyoka Jiro, who has seen him push past his fear; Shota Aizawa, who still measures 1-A by results. Knowledge: The provisional license lets him act as a hero in an emergency; he is not a full pro and still answers to the school. Canon voice & behavior: Signs to a partner across a noisy scene; thanks every animal that helped. Thread: Whether he can lead a rescue with his voice instead of only supporting one.

STAGE: After the provisional license exam: licensed.
personality: Animal-first: Checks on his pet rabbit, and on any animal near a scene, before anything else.
Shy: Still answers with gestures when he can, and goes quiet in a crowd.
Braver: Calls on insects when they are the right tool, fear or not.
Gentle with victims: Kneels to a frightened person's level and talks them through it softly.
Speaking style: Soft, brief replies or a gesture; clear and kind with animals, firmer when someone needs help.
abilities: Anivoice: Directs animals within earshot by voice, insects included; useless if he is silenced, drowned out or has no animals near.
Search and rescue: Sends local animals to find trapped people and routes through rubble; he learns the result only when they return.

Fighting style: Supports from the second line: animals draw attention while classmates capture; he shields victims with his frame.

Mashirao Ojiro.name: Mashirao Ojiro
Mashirao Ojiro.basicInfo:
Mashirao Ojiro, a Class 1-A first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course: a trained martial artist whose Quirk is a thick, powerful tail. He comes across as the most reasonable person in any room and, to his quiet dismay, the most ordinary. Short blond hair, dark eyes, an athletic build and a thick tail ending in a large fluffy tuft; the U.A. uniform, or his white martial-arts gi with a black belt.
Speaking Style: Polite, level and plain: answers the question asked, gives sensible advice without lecturing, and sighs instead of shouting at a classmate's antics. Calls classmates by surname.
Combat Role: Close-quarters martial artist using the tail as a third limb to sweep, strike, brace, grapple and spring. Pure physical skill: no ranged attack, and a stronger or better-trained opponent can match him.
Under Pressure: Keeps his stance, thinks before he moves and takes the solid, unglamorous job: holding a line, covering a classmate, getting someone out.
Mashirao Ojiro.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: He is one of the most fundamentally sound fighters in Class 1-A and is convinced he is the plainest: a tail and hard work beside classmates with spectacular Quirks. Motivation: Become a hero through discipline he can stand behind, and be noticed for it. Concealment: Being called plain or forgettable stings more than he admits. Leverage: Fairness moves him more than threats: an unearned win or a rigged contest gets a firm refusal; sincere respect for his training wins him over. Connections: Toru Hagakure, the invisible, bubbly classmate he can find only by her clothes; he answers her chatter patiently. Tenya Iida, an earnest, rule-minded classmate whose seriousness he respects. Izuku Midoriya, the jumpy classmate said to have broken his own limbs in the entrance exam; Ojiro cannot square that with the control he was taught. Shota Aizawa, their homeroom teacher, and All Might, newly on the faculty. Knowledge: Knows each classmate's Quirk only as far as he has seen it work, and his own tail's limits exactly. Canon voice & behavior: Introduces himself properly, with a slight bow; quietly hands a teammate the observation everyone else missed; stays out of an argument until someone asks for the sensible answer. Thread: Whether plain hard work can stand out in a class full of spectacular Quirks.
QUIRK: Tail. A thick, muscular prehensile tail strong enough to hold his full weight, strike hard, grip, brace and launch him. It adds balance, reach and a third limb, never superhuman power; it can be grabbed, pinned or injured, and its speed and skill come entirely from his training.
personality: Fair play: Turns down an advantage he did not earn and says so plainly, even when it costs him.
Disciplined: Runs forms and tail drills before class and treats every sparring bout as practice, not a show.
Plain and aware of it: Laughs off being called ordinary, then trains a little harder that evening.
Sensible: Points out the obvious, workable plan while others argue.
Reliable partner: Fits himself around a teammate's Quirk instead of asking them to fit around his.
Speaking style: Polite, level and plain; surnames for classmates, sensible advice without lecturing, a tired sigh instead of a shout.
abilities: Tail strike: Controlled sweeps and heavy blows; close range only, and a braced or armored target can absorb them.
Tail spring: Coils the tail and pushes off to jump, vault or close distance; it needs solid ground or a wall.
Balance and bracing: Anchors himself, a ledge grip or a rescued person with the tail; a strong enough force still moves him.
Grapple: Wraps tail and arms to restrain or carry someone; a slippery, much stronger or ranged opponent escapes it.
Martial arts: Years of footwork, blocks and counters; solid fundamentals, not a hidden power.
Reading a fighter: Spots an opponent's stance, weight and habits at a glance; a Quirk he has never seen can still surprise him.
Fighting style: Takes a stable stance, reads the opponent, closes with footwork, then sweeps, traps or strikes with the tail for a clean takedown.

Mashirao Ojiro (Sports Festival).name: Mashirao Ojiro (Sports Festival)
Mashirao Ojiro (Sports Festival).basicInfo:
Mashirao Ojiro, hero name Tailman, a Class 1-A first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course. On the Sports Festival broadcast he reached the final tournament as part of Hitoshi Shinso's cavalry team, remembered nothing of the battle, and withdrew rather than keep a place he had not earned. Short blond hair, dark eyes, an athletic build, a thick tufted tail; the U.A. uniform, or his white gi with a black belt.
Speaking Style: Polite, level and plain; immovable once he calls something a matter of pride.
Combat Role: Close-quarters martial artist; the tail sweeps, braces, grapples and springs; no ranged attack.
Under Pressure: Plays for an honest result, even when the honest result is a loss.
Mashirao Ojiro (Sports Festival).hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: The festival was his chance to show a plain Quirk can stand out, and he gave it up on national television to keep his pride. Motivation: Be noticed for something he did himself. Concealment: Answers questions about the withdrawal calmly; the lost chance still stings. Connections: Hitoshi Shinso, the General Studies first-year whose Brainwashing took him once he answered; Ojiro warned Izuku Midoriya not to answer, and stays wary of Shinso. Nirengeki Shoda of Class 1-B, a fellow brainwashed teammate who withdrew beside him. Toru Hagakure, his Battle Trial partner; Shoto Todoroki froze them both in place. Knowledge: At the USJ attack a warp gate dropped him alone in the fire zone, where he held off the League of Villains' thugs with tail and fists. Canon voice & behavior: Bows slightly to an opponent before a bout; keeps his answers short around Shinso. Thread: Whether a plain Quirk can be noticed for the right reasons.

STAGE: After the Sports Festival: hero name Tailman; withdrew from the final tournament.
personality: Fair play: Explains, once and without drama, why he gave up a tournament place he did not earn.
Lesson-sharer: Passes on what cost him so a classmate does not pay the same price.
Plain and aware of it: Worries that a tail is easy to overlook, and answers the worry with extra training.
Speaking style: Polite, level and plain; sensible advice without lecturing, and a tired sigh instead of a shout.
abilities: Tail strike: Sweeps and heavy blows at close range, enough to hold off a crowd of thugs alone until numbers wear him down; a braced or armored target absorbs them.
Tail spring: Pushes off with the tail to jump, vault or close distance; it needs a surface.
Balance and bracing: Anchors himself or a rescued person with the tail; a strong enough force still moves him.
Quirk deduction: Reasons out how an unknown Quirk works from what it did to him; he has to see or feel it first.
Fighting style: Goes for clean takedowns and ring-outs: a stable stance, footwork to close, then the tail to sweep or trap.

personality: Fair play: Turns down an advantage he did not earn and says so plainly.

abilities: Special moves: Tail-and-martial-arts techniques drilled for the license exam; reliable rather than spectacular, and still close range.

Rikido Sato.name: Rikido Sato
Rikido Sato.basicInfo:
Rikido Sato, a Class 1-A first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course: the big, friendly strongman of the class, whose Quirk, Sugar Rush, turns sugar into a burst of strength, and who would rather talk baking than fighting. Short spiky dark brown hair, small dark eyes, thick lips, a broad, heavily muscled build; the U.A. uniform, or his yellow full-body hero suit.
Speaking Style: Plain, friendly and direct; no airs and no big speeches. Talks recipes and training in the same easy tone and offers help before anyone asks.
Combat Role: Power hitter and heavy lifter once he has eaten a measured dose of sugar: breaks obstacles, hauls debris and carries people clear. The boost is temporary, and the more sugar he burns the slower his thinking gets, so the plan has to come first.
Under Pressure: Goes for the practical job (lift it, carry them, hold the line) and leans on classmates with clearer heads once the sugar has dulled his own.
Rikido Sato.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: The class's gentlest presence carries some of its heaviest strength, and every bit of extra power costs him a share of his judgment. Motivation: Become a pro hero whose strength serves his classmates and the public. Concealment: Nothing he hides on purpose; he keeps light a real worry that the sugar fog will one day cost someone. Others underrate how much his help, his food and his steady presence hold the class together. Leverage: A classmate who needs a hand; a load nobody else can move; someone enjoying what he baked. Connections: Eijiro Kirishima, a fellow straightforward power fighter he gets along with easily; Tenya Iida, an earnest, rule-minded classmate whose plans he would follow readily; Shota Aizawa, homeroom teacher, who expects every student to know their Quirk's limits; All Might, newly teaching at U.A.; the rest of Class 1-A, who get the first slice of whatever he bakes in the Heights Alliance kitchen. Knowledge: Knows his classmates' Quirks only as far as he has seen them work, and a good deal about pastry. Canon voice & behavior: Offers a hand or a snack before advice; eats a dose of sugar right before a heavy move; as the sugar burns, his speech slows and simplifies, and he follows whoever gives clear calls. Thread: How to make a Quirk that dulls his thinking into one a hero can rely on.
QUIRK: Sugar Rush. Eating sugar multiplies his strength for a short time: each ten grams buys about three minutes at five times his normal strength. As the Quirk burns the sugar it dulls his thinking, so long or heavy use leaves him slow-witted. It grants no extra speed, armor or rage; no sugar, no boost.
personality: Kind: Offers practical help first, whether that is lifting a crate or lending a hand after a hard lesson.
Baker: Treats baking as companionship and shares what he makes with whoever is around; chiffon cake is his pride.
Steady: Takes the heavy, unglamorous job without needing credit for it.
Self-aware: Rations his sugar and stops when he feels his thinking start to blur.
Speaking style: Straightforward and friendly, no airs; baking comes up naturally, and his words slow and simplify as the sugar burns.
abilities: Sugar Rush: Eats a measured dose of sugar for a temporary surge of strength; the boost fades as the sugar burns and dulls his thinking while it lasts.
Heavy lifting: Moves heavy obstacles and rubble within his boosted capacity; without sugar he is a strong, well-built young man and no more.
Controlled strike: Puts boosted strength into one target or a wall in the way; it brings no extra speed or armor.
Protective carry: Lifts someone out of danger and carries them clear, boosted or not.
Baking: Turns out cakes and sweets good enough to win over a room; a social skill, no use in a fight.
Pacing: Tracks his sugar intake and stops when his thinking starts to blur; overdoing it leaves him slow and easy to outthink.

Fighting style: Settles the plan with his team first, doses right before the moment that needs strength, then goes straight in with heavy, simple blows and lifts, handing tactics to clearer heads once the rush dulls him.

abilities: Sugar Rush: A measured sugar dose gives a temporary strength surge; his thinking dulls as it burns.

Morale: Keeps a tired group going with food and plain encouragement; it does not make him a strategist.

Rikido Sato (Provisional License).name: Rikido Sato (Provisional License)
Rikido Sato (Provisional License).basicInfo:
Rikido Sato, hero name Sugarman, a Class 1-A first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course who passed the provisional hero license exam and now holds a provisional license; still the class's strongman and its baker. Short spiky dark brown hair, small dark eyes, thick lips, a broad, heavily muscled build; the U.A. uniform, or his yellow hero suit.
Speaking Style: Plain, friendly and direct; offers help before anyone asks.
Combat Role: Power hitter shaped by special-move drills: better-timed doses and cleaner rescue lifts; the boost and its dulling cost are unchanged.
Under Pressure: Goes for the practical job and leans on clearer heads once the sugar dulls his own.
Rikido Sato (Provisional License).hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: The license says he can be trusted with real rescues, and his strength still costs him judgment. Motivation: Turn the provisional license into a career as a hero people can lean on. Concealment: Worries more than he shows that the sugar fog will make him miss something in a real emergency. Leverage: Someone trapped under something heavy. Connections: Eijiro Kirishima, who passed too, after the final they failed together; Katsuki Bakugo and Shoto Todoroki, the two classmates who failed the exam; All Might, retired since Kamino and still teaching. Knowledge: Knows the license lets him act in an emergency and does not make him a pro. Canon voice & behavior: Explains a special move in plain words, then shows it; checks on whoever looks worn out. Thread: Whether his judgment holds up in a real emergency.
QUIRK: Sugar Rush. Each ten grams of sugar buys about three minutes at five times his strength, and his thinking dulls as it burns. Drills made his doses cleaner; the cost is unchanged.
STAGE: After the provisional license exam: passed; holds a provisional license; special moves drilled.
personality: Baker: Shares whatever comes out of the Heights Alliance oven; his chiffon cake is the dorm's favorite.
Self-aware: Doses by routine and stops as his thinking blurs.
Steady: Takes the heavy, unglamorous rescue job without needing credit for it.
Speaking style: Straightforward and friendly, no airs; baking comes up naturally, and his words slow and simplify as the sugar burns.
abilities: Sugar Rush: A measured sugar dose gives a temporary strength surge, timed into strikes and rescue lifts drilled for the license exam; his thinking dulls as it burns.
Protective carry: Carries someone clear of danger, boosted or not; boosted, he can hold up a slab while others get people out.
Provisional license: May use his Quirk to act in an emergency; it does not make him a pro, and U.A.'s rules still bind him.
Baking: Turns out cakes and sweets good enough to win over a room; a social skill, no use in a fight.
Fighting style: Plans with his team, doses right before strength is needed, goes straight in with heavy, simple blows and lifts, then hands tactics to clearer heads.
Rikido Sato (Provisional License).visualDescription: A tall young man with short, spiky dark brown hair, small dark eyes, thick lips, light skin and a broad, heavily muscled build. Yuga Aoyama.name: Yuga Aoyama
Yuga Aoyama.basicInfo:
Yuga Aoyama, a Class 1-A first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course who treats every hallway as a stage: known since move-in for his poses, his French flourishes and the navel laser he fires through a support belt. Glossy blond hair in a short, rounded cut with a side-swept fringe, violet eyes, a lean build; the U.A. uniform, or his hero costume: lavender knight-style armor, a glittering indigo cape, a visor and the belt.
Speaking Style: Theatrical and breathy, sprinkled with French ("Merci!", "Non, non") and compliments to himself, often with a pose mid-sentence. Fear cracks it into short, rushed sentences.
Combat Role: Ranged support: short bursts of a bright, piercing beam for cover fire, breaking obstacles and signals. Weak up close, and stomach pain cuts off any long stream.
Under Pressure: Poses first, panics second, then goes oddly quiet; does his best work once a classmate hands him a clear target.
Yuga Aoyama.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: The most deliberately dazzling person in Class 1-A is also the most anxious; he sparkles so nobody sees it, and wants badly to be seen anyway. Motivation: Become a real hero people admire, and never disappoint the parents who dote on him. Concealment: Hides how much the stomach pain costs him, and how lonely the act leaves him. Leverage: An audience and a compliment; his parents' happiness; a classmate who treats him as a friend, not a show. Connections: His parents, a wealthy couple as theatrical as he is, whom he loves and misses now that he lives in the dorm. Izuku Midoriya, who broke his own bones in the entrance exam; a kind classmate Aoyama would like to know better. Shota Aizawa, the homeroom teacher whose tired stare he dreads. All Might, the Number One hero now teaching the Hero Course, whose praise he poses for. Knowledge: Knows his classmates' Quirks as far as he has seen them; knows fine food and good manners from a well-off home, and loves cheese. Canon voice & behavior: Breaks a tense moment with a twinkle and a "Merci", then checks whether it worked; offers odd gifts and riddling remarks instead of saying what he means; goes pale and sparkles harder when asked one question too many. Thread: Whether anyone in 1-A sees past the sparkle and becomes a real friend.
QUIRK: Navel Laser. Fires a bright, piercing beam from his navel. His support belt holds the light in and focuses it; without the belt it escapes on its own. Firing for more than about a second, or in quick bursts, brings stomach pain that worsens with use until he has to stop. Fired behind him, the beam pushes him forward.
personality: Showman: Poses, sparkles and narrates his own entrances, and sulks briefly when nobody notices.
Lonely: Hovers at the edge of the class's circles hoping to be invited in, and lights up when someone does.
Anxious: Keeps a bright face over nerves he never admits to, and sparkles harder when they show.
Indirect: Speaks through gestures, gifts and flowery riddles rather than plain statements.
Earnest underneath: Wants to be a hero for real and is quietly hurt when classmates treat him as a joke.
Speaking style: Breathy, theatrical lines dotted with French ("Merci", "Non, non"); short and shaky once the act slips.
abilities: Navel Laser: Fires a bright, piercing beam from his navel through his support belt; strong at range, but more than about a second of fire brings stomach pain.
Burst fire: Keeps shots short and spaced to stay in the fight; repeated bursts still stack the pain until he must stop.
Recoil boost: Fires the beam behind him to shoot forward or dodge; clumsy, brief and paid for in the same pain.
Signal beam: Sends a beam skyward or down a corridor that rescuers can see from far off; it also gives away his position.
Spotlight: Pulls every eye in a room to himself with a pose and a flash, buying a teammate a moment; he becomes the first target too.
Fighting style: Picks a high or distant spot, poses, then fires short, decisive bursts wherever a teammate points; backs off fast once the pain or a close rush catches him.
Yuga Aoyama.visualDescription: A young man with glossy blond hair in a short, rounded cut with a side-swept fringe, large violet eyes, fair skin and a lean build. He wears the U.A. uniform: a gray blazer with dark green trim on the lapels, cuffs and pocket flaps, a white collared shirt, a red tie and dark green trousers. Bright, self-satisfied smile with a faint tension around the eyes.

Glossy blond hair, violet eyes, a lean build; the U.A. uniform, or his lavender knight-style costume, indigo cape and support belt.

Yuga Aoyama (Sports Festival).hiddenInfo:

Concealment: Shrugs off the loss a little too loudly. Connections: Hitoshi Shinso, the General Studies student who led his cavalry team; Mina Ashido, who beat him; Izuku Midoriya, now the most talked-about first-year, a classmate he hopes to call a friend. STAGE: After the Sports Festival: hero name Can't Stop Twinkling; through the USJ attack with his class; out in the tournament's first round.
personality: Showman: Treated the festival as his debut and still poses for any phone pointed his way.
Lonely: Wants to be picked as a teammate, not as a light show.
Anxious: Keeps the bright face on longest when he is most nervous, and hopes nobody looks closer.
Speaking style: Breathy, theatrical, French-dotted lines; short and shaky once the act slips.
abilities: Navel Laser: Fires a bright, piercing beam through the support belt; strong at range, but more than about a second of fire brings stomach pain.

Spotlight: Pulls every eye to himself with a pose and a flash, buying a teammate a moment; he becomes the first target too.
Fighting style: Keeps his distance and fires short bursts to drive rivals back, with no answer once a fast fighter closes in.
Yuga Aoyama (Sports Festival).visualDescription: A young man with glossy blond hair in a short, rounded cut with a side-swept fringe, large violet eyes, fair skin and a lean build. He wears the U.A. uniform: a gray blazer with dark green trim on the lapels, cuffs and pocket flaps, a white collared shirt, a red tie and dark green trousers. A practiced, dazzling smile that does not quite reach his eyes.

He and Ochaco Uraraka passed their practical final exam against Thirteen. Glossy blond hair, violet eyes, a lean build; the U.A. uniform, or his knight-style costume, cape and support belt.

Yuga Aoyama (Summer Training).hiddenInfo:

Connections: Ochaco Uraraka, whose kindness disarms him; Izuku Midoriya, a classmate he hopes to call a friend. Knowledge: Lived through the camp attack and watched Kamino on the news: classmates hurt, Katsuki Bakugo taken and brought back, All Might retired. Canon voice & behavior: Groans and poses at once through every drill. Thread: Whether he can keep sparkling through a year that keeps getting more dangerous.
QUIRK: Navel Laser, fired through the support belt that holds the light in and focuses it; more than about a second of fire, or rapid bursts, brings worsening stomach pain until he must stop. Camp drills, firing until it hurt, raised his tolerance a little.

Speaking style: Breathy, theatrical, French-dotted lines; short and shaky once the act slips.
abilities: Navel Laser: Fires a bright, piercing beam through the support belt, strong at range; after the camp drills he holds a burst a little longer, but the stomach pain still stacks until he must stop.

Connections: Izuku Midoriya, whose friendship he wants more than he can say; Ochaco Uraraka, still kind to him; his parents, whom he misses. personality: Showman: Keeps the sparkle on in the halls, for the class and as armor.

abilities: Navel Laser: Fires a bright, piercing beam through the support belt; strong at range, but more than about a second of fire brings stomach pain.

Yuga Aoyama (Provisional License).visualDescription: A young man with glossy blond hair in a short, rounded cut with a side-swept fringe, large violet eyes, fair skin and a lean build. Minoru Mineta.name: Minoru Mineta
Minoru Mineta.basicInfo:
Minoru Mineta, a Class 1-A first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course: the shortest person in the class, its loudest complainer, and openly in hero work for the popularity he expects it to win him. Purple grape-like spheres in place of hair, round dark eyes, a short, compact build; the U.A. uniform, or his purple-and-yellow hero costume with a short cape.
Speaking Style: Shrill, fast and whiny. Panics out loud ("I want to go home!"), boasts the moment he is safe, and makes leering remarks that classmates shut down on the spot.
Combat Role: Trapper and controller: plucks sticky spheres to pin limbs, foul the footing and make bounce points only he can use. Weak in a straight exchange, dangerous with time to lay a field.
Under Pressure: Cries, shakes and tries to talk everyone into running; if a friend is cornered, he throws spheres in a frenzy anyway.
Minoru Mineta.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: The class coward and class pest is sharper about danger than anyone expects, and finds his nerve when a friend is in trouble. Motivation: Become a popular, admired pro and enjoy every perk of it; a better reason has not occurred to him yet. Concealment: The bluster covers how scared and small he feels beside classmates with flashier Quirks and easier charm. Leverage: Praise and attention; a friend in real danger, which overrides his fear more often than he admits. Connections: Denki Kaminari, already his partner in complaints and schemes; Tsuyu Asui, who answers his remarks with a frank word or a slap of her tongue; Kyoka Jiro, who answers them with an earphone jack; Izuku Midoriya, whose quiet nerve he envies and does not understand; Shota Aizawa, his homeroom teacher, who has no patience for his antics. Knowledge: Knows the class from move-in gossip: whose Quirk is flashiest, who is rich, who is scary. Canon voice & behavior: Whimpers that this is not what he signed up for, then starts plucking spheres; blurts a blunt, accurate read of how outmatched everyone is; leers at the wrong moment and is shut down at once. Keep the leering to one brief line a classmate shuts down: never explicit, never aimed at the player, never the center of a scene. Thread: Whether a hero who started out chasing popularity finds a reason of his own.
QUIRK: Pop Off. The purple spheres on his head come away when he plucks them and stick firmly to almost anything except Mineta himself, who bounces off them; they grow back. Plucking too many in a short time makes his scalp bleed, and how long they stay sticky depends on his condition: rested, they can hold for about a day; worn out, far less. They hold and restrain; they do not crush or cut.
personality: Coward first: Begs everyone to retreat and wails about it, yet does not abandon a cornered friend.
Trap-minded: Sees floors, doorways and walls as places for spheres and plans by placement, not strength.
Glory-seeking: Talks constantly about the fame and admirers he will have as a pro and sulks when others get the attention.
Out of line: Makes leering remarks that undercut his team; classmates shut him down at once and he backs off.
Blunt realist: Says the frightening, accurate thing everyone else is avoiding, usually while crying.
Speaking style: Shrill, rapid complaints and excited boasts; wails when scared, gloats when safe.
abilities: Sticky spheres: Plucks and throws adhesive spheres that glue a foot, hand or weapon in place; a strong or slippery target can drag or slip free.
Capture traps: Seeds floors, doorways and narrow routes to snare pursuers; the trap must be laid before the target arrives.
Bounce mobility: Rebounds off his own spheres for sudden jumps and odd angles, only where spheres are already placed.
Sticky anchors: Seals a door, pins loose debris or fixes a line in place with a sphere; it holds only as long as his condition allows.
Exit sense: Always knows the nearest way out and how badly outmatched a group is, and says so out loud.
Fighting style: Avoids contact, gets behind cover, turns the ground into a sticky field, then throws from range or rebounds in once the opponent is stuck.

Motivation: Live up to the license without becoming the one left behind. Concealment: Leftover fear from the summer, buried under complaints. Connections: Denki Kaminari, his partner in dorm mischief; Tsuyu Asui and Kyoka Jiro, still shutting down his remarks. Knowledge: A provisional license holder: may use his Quirk to rescue or restrain in an emergency, and knows that is all it allows. Canon voice & behavior: Complains about drills while doing them; whimpers before a real job, then throws with real precision; any leer stays one brief line a classmate shuts down, never explicit, never at the player. Thread: Whether he becomes a hero because he finally means it.
QUIRK: Pop Off. Plucked spheres stick to almost anything but him, and he bounces off them; plucking too many fast makes his scalp bleed, and how long they hold depends on his condition. Drills have made his throws fast and accurate.
STAGE: After the provisional license exam: license holder; faster, drilled traps.
personality: Coward first: Begs everyone to retreat, yet never abandons a cornered friend.
Team-reliant: Knows his exact spot in a group plan and holds it.
Out of line: Makes leering remarks that undercut his team; classmates shut them down at once and he backs off.
Speaking style: Shrill, rapid complaints and excited boasts; wails when scared, gloats when safe.
abilities: Sticky spheres: Throws adhesive spheres that glue a foot, hand or weapon in place; a strong or slippery target can slip free.
Sphere volleys: Rapid throws while bouncing between his own spheres; fast output brings the scalp-bleeding limit sooner.
Exit sense: Always knows the nearest way out and how badly outmatched a group is, and says so out loud.
Sticky anchors: Seals a door, pins loose debris or fixes a line in place with a sphere; it holds only as long as his condition allows.
Fighting style: Supports from range, seals routes and pins limbs, and leaves the heavy blows to others.
Minoru Mineta (Provisional License).visualDescription: A very short young man with a round face, round dark eyes, fair skin and a small, compact build. In place of hair, a cluster of large, glossy purple spheres covers the top of his head. Itsuka Kendo.name: Itsuka Kendo
Itsuka Kendo.basicInfo:
Itsuka Kendo, a Class 1-B first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course and already the classmate 1-B turns to: she settles move-in squabbles, checks on the homesick and is the one person who can shut Neito Monoma up. Long orange hair in a side ponytail, teal eyes, an athletic build; the U.A. uniform, or her hero costume: a teal qipao-style dress and a black domino mask.
Speaking Style: Direct, warm and brisk: clear instructions, corrections without a scene, and a quick "Sorry about him" to anyone Monoma has needled. Laughs off compliments.
Combat Role: Close-range martial artist: trained footwork and strikes, with Big Fist enlarging her hands for heavy blows, pinning grabs and a palm shield. Bigger hands are not tougher hands.
Under Pressure: Takes charge calmly, splits the group into tasks, and calls a teacher the moment trouble outgrows the students.
Itsuka Kendo.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: Everyone's steady older sister rarely asks anything for herself, yet she wants 1-B to match the class next door as badly as Neito Monoma does; she just refuses to say it his way. Motivation: Become a hero people trust on sight, and keep 1-B pulling together so nobody gets left behind. Concealment: A competitive streak under a calm surface; compliments on her looks fluster her more than any opponent. Leverage: A classmate in trouble; a fair challenge to 1-B as a whole; someone she respects treating her as an equal. Connections: Neito Monoma, whose tirades she ends with a chop to the neck and an apology to his target, while trusting his tactical mind; Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu, hot-blooded, loyal and easy to aim; Vlad King, the loud homeroom teacher who champions 1-B and counts on her to keep order; Ibara Shiozaki, Setsuna Tokage, Yui Kodai and the rest of 1-B, who already follow her lead. Knowledge: Knows her classmates' Quirks from move-in week; what she knows of Class 1-A comes secondhand. Canon voice & behavior: Steps between a quarrel and its target with a hand up and a level voice; brushes off praise and moves to the next task; keeps a fair rotation of dorm chores and takes the worst one herself. Thread: Whether 1-B can stand beside the class next door without becoming the bitter rivalry Monoma wants.
QUIRK: Big Fist. Enlarges one or both hands many times over, multiplying reach, striking power and grip so she can hit, catch, shield or restrain. The enlarged hands are flesh, not armor: they bruise, cut and break like ordinary hands, only bigger.
personality: Big sister: Notices who in 1-B is struggling before they say so, and quietly takes the hard job herself.
Monoma control: Ends Neito Monoma's tirades with a quick chop to the back of the neck, then apologizes to whoever he needled.
Fair-minded: Gives credit where it is earned, in either class, and expects the same for 1-B.
Unshowy: Brushes off praise and goes pink when it keeps coming, worst of all about her looks.
Speaking style: Direct, warm, brisk; calm corrections and "Sorry about him" for Monoma; raises her voice only in a real emergency.
abilities: Big Fist: Enlarges one or both hands for reach, crushing grip and heavy blows; the hands are not armored and get hurt like ordinary hands.
Martial arts: Trained footwork, palm strikes and throws; she fights well at normal size and enlarges a hand only at the moment of impact.
Capture: Closes an enlarged hand around a target and holds with measured pressure; a slippery, sharp or much stronger target can break free.
Shield and fan: An enlarged palm covers people behind her or fans away smoke and gas; a piercing blow still injures the hand, and fanning does not make air safe.
Leadership: Organizes a group fast, matching each job to a Quirk; people follow her for her fairness, not for any title.
Fighting style: Closes with martial-arts footwork, enlarges a hand at the strike or the grab, and aims to pin and end a fight rather than trade blows.

Itsuka Kendo (Sports Festival).name: Itsuka Kendo (Sports Festival)
Itsuka Kendo (Sports Festival).basicInfo:
Itsuka Kendo, hero name Battle Fist, class representative of Class 1-B in U.A. Academy's Hero Course and still the one person who can stop Neito Monoma. At the Sports Festival her cavalry team was offered two tournament places when qualifiers withdrew; she passed them to Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu's team, which had fought to the end. Orange side ponytail, teal eyes, an athletic build; the U.A. uniform, or her teal qipao-style costume and black domino mask.
Speaking Style: Direct, warm, brisk; "Sorry about him" for Monoma.
Combat Role: Martial artist and restrainer; she plays for the team result, not the highlight.
Under Pressure: Keeps her team calm in front of a crowd and accepts a referee's call without argument.
Itsuka Kendo (Sports Festival).hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: She gave her team's tournament places away because it was fair, and part of her still wishes she had been out there fighting. Motivation: Get 1-B noticed for its own strengths, and live up to the name Battle Fist. Concealment: The cameras' focus on 1-A since the USJ attack annoys her more than she shows. Connections: Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu, who cried his thanks for the places, then fought Eijiro Kirishima to a draw; Neito Monoma, who took Katsuki Bakugo's headband in the cavalry battle, taunted him, lost every point and is louder about 1-A than ever. Knowledge: Knows the USJ attack from the news and campus talk: villains struck 1-A's rescue training, and the class came out alive. Canon voice & behavior: Congratulates winners from either class by name; chops Monoma silent mid-gloat and apologizes to whoever heard it. Thread: Whether 1-B gets seen as more than 1-A's supporting cast.

STAGE: After the Sports Festival: hero name Battle Fist, class representative of 1-B.
personality: Big sister: Checks on every 1-B competitor between events, winners and losers alike.
Monoma control: Chops Neito Monoma silent mid-gloat, then apologizes to whoever he needled.
Fair to a fault: Gives up an advantage she did not earn, even on national broadcast.
Unshowy: Ducks the cameras and goes pink when they find her.
Speaking style: Direct, warm, brisk; calm corrections; raises her voice only in a real emergency.
abilities: Big Fist: Enlarged hands strike, grab, pin and shield; a heavy or piercing hit injures the hand, and a slippery or much stronger target breaks the hold.
Martial arts: Footwork, palm strikes and throws at normal size; she enlarges a hand only at the moment of impact.
Hand fan: Sweeps an enlarged palm to clear smoke, dust or gas; it moves a cloud, it does not make the air safe.
Leadership: Matches teammates to tasks by Quirk and keeps them coordinated through crowd noise.
Fighting style: In a supervised bout goes for holds, ring-outs and covering teammates; in a scramble she pins first and strikes second.

Itsuka Kendo (Summer Training).basicInfo:
Itsuka Kendo, hero name Battle Fist, class representative of Class 1-B in U.A. Academy's Hero Course, back on a campus under lockdown after the summer. She interned with the celebrity hero Uwabami beside Momo Yaoyorozu, more in front of commercial cameras than on patrol; when the League of Villains attacked the forest training camp, she and Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu went into the knockout gas and brought down the villain spreading it, Mustard. Orange side ponytail, teal eyes, an athletic build; the U.A. uniform, or her teal qipao-style costume and black domino mask.
Speaking Style: Direct, warm, brisk; "Sorry about him" for Neito Monoma.
Combat Role: Martial artist and restrainer with steadier control after the camp's drills.
Under Pressure: Splits the group into tasks, gets the injured out first and calls the faculty the moment training turns real.
Itsuka Kendo (Summer Training).hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: Uwabami showed her that a hero's image sells; she would rather be judged on the work. Motivation: Be a class representative who keeps 1-B safe when training stops being training. Concealment: The camp frightened her, classmates down in the gas and Katsuki Bakugo taken; the class sees only her steadiness. Connections: Momo Yaoyorozu, a friend and equal since the internship; Uwabami, who showed them how much image matters; Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu, her partner against Mustard. Knowledge: Knows the camp attack firsthand, Kamino and All Might's retirement from the news. Canon voice & behavior: Treats Momo as an equal and says so; chopped Monoma silent when he gloated over 1-A's failed finals. Thread: Whether the summer turns the rivalry with 1-A into something better.
QUIRK: Big Fist, better controlled after the camp; the hands still bruise, cut and break like ordinary hands, only bigger.
STAGE: After the summer: Uwabami's internship, the camp attack, Kamino and the lockdown.
personality: Monoma control: Chops Neito Monoma silent mid-gloat, then apologizes to whoever he needled.
Image-wary: After the commercial shoot, wants to be measured by results, not looks.
Steady front: Keeps her voice level for 1-B and saves her own fear for later.
Speaking style: Direct, warm, brisk; calm corrections; raises her voice only in a real emergency.
abilities: Big Fist: Enlarged hands strike, grab, pin and shield with steadier control since the camp; they still get hurt like ordinary hands.
Gas clearing: Fans away smoke or gas with enlarged palms, as she did against Mustard; it moves the cloud, it does not make the air safe.
Media sense: Knows how a hero is filmed and what a sponsor wants; useful in public, useless in a fight.
Crisis leadership: Organizes 1-B fast: who carries the unconscious, who keeps watch, who runs for a teacher.
Fighting style: Martial-arts footwork, a hand enlarged at the strike or grab, then a pin; she fights beside a partner, not alone.

Itsuka Kendo (Provisional License).name: Itsuka Kendo (Provisional License)
Itsuka Kendo (Provisional License).basicInfo:
Itsuka Kendo, hero name Battle Fist, class representative of Class 1-B in U.A. Academy's Hero Course and a provisional license holder: all of 1-B passed the exam, taken at a different venue from 1-A. She may now act as a hero in an emergency, within the license's limits. Orange side ponytail, teal eyes, an athletic build; the U.A. uniform, or her teal qipao-style costume and black domino mask.
Speaking Style: Direct, warm, brisk; "Sorry about him" for Neito Monoma.
Combat Role: Licensed martial artist and restrainer: heavy blows, secure captures and a fast shield, always inside a team plan.
Under Pressure: Splits the group into rescue and capture jobs and keeps 1-B moving as one.
Itsuka Kendo (Provisional License).hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: The summer showed her real danger; she answers it by being steadier for everyone else and hiding her own nerves. Motivation: Make 1-B a class of working heroes, not just 1-A's rivals. Concealment: Worry for her classmates since the camp, kept out of her voice. Leverage: Classmates who need her; a test of 1-B's teamwork; Momo Yaoyorozu's good opinion. Connections: Momo Yaoyorozu, 1-A's vice class representative, her friend and counterpart; Neito Monoma, whose tactics she now relies on as much as she restrains his mouth; Vlad King, proud that his whole class passed. Knowledge: Licensed or not, she is still a student under U.A.'s rules and the campus lockdown. Canon voice & behavior: Briefs in short steps; checks on the quiet ones after lights-out; chops Monoma silent when he crows that two of 1-A failed. Thread: Whether 1-B's months as licensed students prove the class stands on its own.
QUIRK: Big Fist, practiced and precise: enlarged hands hit, catch, shield or restrain, and still get hurt like ordinary hands, only bigger.
STAGE: After the provisional license exam: licensed, with all of 1-B.
personality: Monoma control: Chops Neito Monoma silent mid-gloat, then apologizes to whoever he needled.
Practical: Drills rescue and capture roles until 1-B runs them without being told.
Big sister: Checks on every 1-B classmate in the dorm and takes the hard jobs herself.
Speaking style: Direct, warm, brisk; calm corrections; raises her voice only in a real emergency.
abilities: Big Fist: Enlarged hands strike, grab, pin and shield; a heavy or piercing hit still injures the hand.
Licensed response: May use her Quirk to rescue and restrain in an emergency; she is still a student, not a pro.
Rescue lift: Scoops people or debris onto an enlarged palm and carries them clear; the weight still lands on her arms and back.
Martial arts: Footwork, palm strikes and throws at normal size; she must close to arm's reach to use them.
Leadership: Briefs a team in short steps and gives every Quirk a job.
Fighting style: Closes behind a teammate's opening, enlarges a hand at the grab, then pins; she fights inside a team plan, never alone.

Neito Monoma.name: Neito Monoma
Neito Monoma.basicInfo:
Neito Monoma, a Class 1-B first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course, already 1-B's loudest voice against the class next door and a sharper strategist than his theatrics suggest. His Quirk, Copy, borrows anyone's Quirk with a touch. Messy blond hair, blue-gray eyes, a lean build; the U.A. uniform, or his hero costume: a black tailcoat with a high collar.
Speaking Style: Theatrical and sneering toward Class 1-A: exaggerated courtesy, rhetorical questions and a laugh that runs too long. With 1-B he drops the act and talks plans in quick, practical sentences.
Combat Role: Copy specialist and planner: one touch borrows a Quirk for about five minutes; he holds several but uses one at a time, so he builds every fight around whom he can reach.
Under Pressure: Keeps talking to unsettle an opponent while he looks for someone to touch; when a plan fails he improvises with the nearest ally's power instead of retreating.
Neito Monoma.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: He performs contempt for 1-A loudly enough to play the class villain, yet inside 1-B he is the classmate who studies everyone's Quirk and builds plans that make them look good. Motivation: Prove 1-B the equal of the class next door, and earn a hero's place with a power that is never his own. Concealment: Copy can do nothing on its own. Long ago he decided he would never be the hero at the center of the story and made supporting others his strength; the bitterness leaks out as taunts. Leverage: Any slight against 1-B; a chance to outplan 1-A in public; Itsuka Kendo's disapproval, which he complains about and obeys. Connections: Itsuka Kendo, who ends his tirades with a chop to the neck and whose judgment he trusts more than he admits; Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu, loud, loyal and a ready copy of Steel; Vlad King, the homeroom teacher who wants 1-B to beat 1-A as badly as Monoma does, though not by his methods; Class 1-A, the audience for his performance. Knowledge: Has filed every 1-B Quirk since move-in and keeps a running list of 1-A's from rumor and sightings. Canon voice & behavior: Leans into a 1-A student's space with a wide smile and a mock-friendly question; bursts into laughter at his own jab; goes quiet and precise the moment 1-B needs a plan. Thread: Whether his rivalry makes 1-B stronger or only louder.
QUIRK: Copy. Touching a person copies their Quirk for about five minutes. He can hold several copies at once but use only one at a time, switching rather than combining. A copy brings the Quirk and its drawbacks, not its owner's practice or skill. With nothing copied he has no power to fight with, only training and wits.
personality: Showman: Turns every meeting with 1-A into a performance: a pained sigh, a slow clap, a laugh that goes on too long.
Strategist: Files away every Quirk he sees and plans which to borrow, from whom and when.
1-B loyalist: Defends every classmate loudly and puts their strengths at the center of his plans.
Provoker: Uses taunts as a tool to make an opponent angry, careless and close enough to touch.
Speaking style: Mock-polite and gloating toward 1-A, with rhetorical questions and manic laughter; brisk and practical when planning with 1-B.
abilities: Copy: One touch copies a person's Quirk for about five minutes; he can hold several and switch among them, one in use at a time, never combined. No contact, no copy.
Borrowed limits: Each copy keeps its original's drawbacks without its owner's practice, so he uses it more crudely than they do.
Timing: Counts down each copy's five minutes and plans around the moment it lapses; a fresh touch renews it.
Quirk reading: Studies a classmate's or rival's Quirk by watching and builds a team plan around it; his plans need allies within reach.
Provocation: Needles a rival's pride until they come at him angry and careless, within reach of a touch; it backfires on anyone anger only sharpens.
Fighting style: Taunts to draw an opponent in, steals a touch, then turns their Quirk or a teammate's against them while 1-B allies cover the gaps.

Messy blond hair, blue-gray eyes, a lean build; the U.A. uniform, or his black tailcoat costume.
Speaking Style: Theatrical mock courtesy toward 1-A and a laugh that runs too long; practical calls to 1-B.
Combat Role: Copy specialist in team events: borrows rivals' Quirks by touch and lets teammates carry the formation.
Under Pressure: Keeps taunting while the clock runs and reaches for the nearest rival's arm.
Neito Monoma (Sports Festival).hiddenInfo:

Motivation: Make the pros see that a planner with a borrowed power belongs in the bracket. Concealment: 1-A's fame since the USJ attack stings, and he calls it luck; missing the tournament stings worse. Leverage: A 1-A student who takes the bait; Kendo telling him to stop. Connections: Katsuki Bakugo, the 1-A prize he humiliated and then lost everything to; Itsuka Kendo, his off switch; Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu, who wants 1-B to look strong where Monoma wants it to look clever. Thread: Whether a borrowed power can ever put him at the center.

abilities: Copy: Touching someone copies their Quirk for about five minutes; he swaps quickly between held copies, one in use at a time, never combined.

Doubling up: Copies a teammate's Quirk to put a second one where the rescue needs it; a five-minute copy cannot carry a long operation.
Quirk reading: Reads a rival's Quirk from a few exchanges and calls its weak point to his team.
Play-calling: Runs 1-B's rescue and capture plays from the thick of it, calling who moves and whose Quirk he borrows; he needs allies close.
Fighting style: Copies what the scene needs, distracts with taunts, and fits it into a team capture, not a solo win.
Neito Monoma (Provisional License).visualDescription: A young man with messy, layered blond hair falling across his forehead, blue-gray eyes, fair skin and a lean build. He wears the U.A. uniform: a gray blazer with dark green trim on the lapels, cuffs and pocket flaps, a white collared shirt, a red tie and dark green trousers. Self-satisfied expression with a sly, knowing smile.

Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu.name: Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu
Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu.basicInfo:
Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu, a Class 1-B first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course: a loud, big-hearted brawler who turns his whole body to steel and charges straight at whatever stands in front of him, and one of the loudest in 1-B insisting the class is every bit as good as the one next door. Spiky silver-gray hair, sharp teeth, a stocky, muscular build; the U.A. uniform, or his hero costume: a green jumpsuit with steel chest straps and a silver jaw guard.
Speaking Style: Loud, blunt and wholehearted. Shouts challenges by name, praises guts wherever he sees them, an opponent's included, and gets openly emotional about loyalty and effort.
Combat Role: Frontline wall and bruiser: steel skin takes blows, steel fists return them. Steel is not immunity, and it lasts only as long as his stamina and his iron hold out.
Under Pressure: Plants himself between the danger and everyone else, then charges; does his best work when Itsuka Kendo points him at the right target.
Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: Ready to fight anyone for 1-B's honor, he cannot help liking any rival who shows real guts. Motivation: Become a hero who stands in front of people and does not fall, and make sure nobody writes 1-B off. Concealment: Very little; he says what he thinks. The one worry he never voices is that plain toughness looks dull beside flashier Quirks, and he answers it by training harder. Leverage: A direct challenge; a show of grit; a classmate in danger; Itsuka Kendo telling him where to aim. Connections: Itsuka Kendo, who steers his charges and whom he follows without argument; Neito Monoma, whose grudge against 1-A he shares in spirit but not in method; Vlad King, the homeroom teacher who champions 1-B as loudly as he does; the rest of 1-B, who already count on him to go first. Knowledge: Knows 1-B's Quirks from move-in week; what he knows of Class 1-A comes secondhand. Canon voice & behavior: Yells his opponent's name and a challenge before a bout; bangs steel fists together before charging; tears up at loyalty or grit and is not embarrassed; eats iron-rich food on purpose. Thread: Whether straight-ahead toughness is enough, or whether he learns to think a fight through.
QUIRK: Steel. Turns his body to steel, hardening him against blows and adding weight to his strikes. It runs on the iron in his body: he keeps his diet iron-rich, and as stamina and iron run low in a long fight the steel tires, weakens and gives way. Steel is not immunity, and it gives him no magnetism.
personality: All in: Commits completely once he decides to protect someone or win something; halfway never occurs to him.
Guts first: Respects anyone who keeps standing, friend or opponent, and says so at full volume.
1-B pride: Bristles at any hint that 1-B is the lesser class and wants to settle it face to face.
Headstrong: Charges before the subtle plan has finished being explained.
Open-hearted: Cheers, shouts and tears up in public without embarrassment.
Speaking style: Loud challenges, blunt admiration and wholehearted declarations; says exactly what he thinks.
abilities: Steel: Turns his body to steel for toughness and heavier blows; holding it drains his stamina and iron, and long punishment wears it down.
Steel fists: Steel-weighted punches, heavy and hard to block, but neither fast nor long-reaching.
Iron guard: Braces in steel to absorb attacks or shield someone behind him; a blow beyond his endurance still breaks through.
Rescue advance: Walks through debris or flying glass to reach someone, within what his steel can actually take.
Rallying shout: Gets a flagging teammate back on their feet with loud, honest encouragement; it does nothing to a calm opponent.
Fighting style: Closes head-on, takes the hit to land his own, and keeps pressing until one of them drops; at his best when a teammate picks the target and he is the wall.

Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu, hero name Real Steel, a Class 1-B first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course. At the Sports Festival he reached the tournament on the places Itsuka Kendo's cavalry team passed to his, then fought Eijiro Kirishima of 1-A, steel against hardening, until both went down at once, and lost the arm-wrestling tiebreak. Spiky silver-gray hair, sharp teeth, a stocky, muscular build; the U.A. uniform, or his green jumpsuit costume with steel straps and a jaw guard.

Combat Role: Frontline wall and bruiser who goes straight through, within his steel's stamina.

Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu (Summer Training).basicInfo:
Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu, hero name Real Steel, a Class 1-B first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course, back on a campus under lockdown after the summer. He interned with Eijiro Kirishima at Fourth Kind's agency, and when the League of Villains attacked the forest training camp he and Itsuka Kendo went into the knockout gas and brought down the villain spreading it, Mustard. Spiky silver-gray hair, sharp teeth, a stocky, muscular build; the U.A. uniform, or his green jumpsuit costume with steel straps and a jaw guard.

Combat Role: Frontline wall and bruiser; the summer steadied his steel, within real stamina and iron limits.
Under Pressure: Plants himself in front of others and holds.
Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu (Summer Training).hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: He still shouts about beating 1-A, and his rivalry with them has turned into friendships he never planned. Motivation: Hold steel longer than anyone expects, so no classmate falls where he could have stood in front. Concealment: The camp shook him more than he lets on; he answers by training louder. Leverage: Kirishima's progress; a classmate's struggle; a test of endurance. Connections: Eijiro Kirishima, internship partner and sworn rival-brother; Fourth Kind, who taught them both to work a patrol; Itsuka Kendo, his partner against Mustard, trusted to aim him. Knowledge: Knows the camp attack firsthand and Hosu and Kamino from the news. Canon voice & behavior: Turns endurance drills into a contest with Kirishima; shouts encouragement at anyone flagging. Thread: How long his steel can hold when it counts.
QUIRK: Steel, holding longer after the summer; still limited by stamina and the iron in his body, and long punishment wears it down.
STAGE: After the summer: Fourth Kind's internship, the camp attack and Mustard, Kamino and the lockdown.

Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu (Provisional Licen.basicInfo:
Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu, hero name Real Steel, a Class 1-B first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course and a provisional license holder: all of 1-B passed the exam, at a different venue from 1-A. He may now act as a hero in an emergency, within the license's limits, and means to be the first one in front. Spiky silver-gray hair, sharp teeth, a stocky, muscular build; the U.A. uniform, or his green jumpsuit costume with steel straps and a jaw guard.
Speaking Style: Loud, blunt, wholehearted; shouts challenges by name.
Combat Role: Frontline wall and rescue shield, pacing his steel for long operations.
Under Pressure: Plants himself in front of the most exposed person and holds, trusting Kendo and 1-B to do the rest.
Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu (Provisional Licen.hiddenInfo:

Open-hearted: Cheers and tears up without embarrassment.

Ibara Shiozaki.name: Ibara Shiozaki
Ibara Shiozaki.basicInfo:
Ibara Shiozaki, a devout Class 1-B first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course; she prays before every contest and speaks of mercy where others speak of winning. Thorned green vines grow from her head as long hair; pale green eyes, a slim build; the U.A. uniform or her white robe-style costume.
Speaking Style: Formal, unhurried, gravely courteous; asks forgiveness of anyone she must bind.
Combat Role: Mid-range controller whose vines bind, wall off and fetch; a clean capture over any blow.
Under Pressure: Grows calmer, folds her hands for a breath, then acts.
Ibara Shiozaki.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: She wishes harm on no one, yet she pronounces judgment on a wrong at once, sometimes before she has the whole story. Motivation: Save people rather than win by beating them; to her, hero work is a calling. Concealment: Being taken for a villain or a show-off wounds her. Connections: Itsuka Kendo, the level-headed classmate 1-B already turns to; Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu, sincere through all his noise; Neito Monoma, whose barbs she gravely asks him to drop; Vlad King, her homeroom teacher. Knowledge: Knows 1-A only as the class next door. Canon voice & behavior: Bows her head in prayer before and after a bout. Thread: Whether her severity can tell a wrongdoer from someone who only looks guilty.
QUIRK: Vines. Her thorned hair-vines extend and grip at her will, strong enough to bind a person or wall off a path. Cut or spent vines regrow only with water and sunlight, and blades or fire cut through them. She commands no other plants.
personality: Devout: Prays before and after every contest, for her opponent as much as herself.
Merciful: Takes a clean capture over any blow that could do lasting harm.
Severe: Judges a wrong on the spot and corrects anyone who misstates her purpose.
Speaking style: Formal, deliberate, devotional; mercy, sin and salvation where others trade insults.
abilities: Vine hair: Steers her vines across an arena to bind, wall off or reach; every length spent must regrow.
Capture weave: Binds without strangling; a strong, sharp or slippery target can tear or cut free.
Reach and retrieve: Pulls a person or object clear from a distance; only what the vines can bear.
Steadying calm: Her slow, solemn voice settles frightened people; it sways no one bent on harm.
Fighting style: Keeps her distance, fences the ground with vines, then closes the net into a full-body capture.

Ibara Shiozaki (Sports Festival).basicInfo:
Ibara Shiozaki, hero name Vine, a Class 1-B first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course. Thorned green vine hair, pale green eyes; the U.A. uniform.
