For once everyone is out of costume, in party clothes: Principal Nezu with a speech on cards, Shota Aizawa near the door, All Might in a suit that finally fits his new frame, Cementoss, Ectoplasm, Snipe, Hound Dog, Recovery Girl, Thirteen and Vlad King.

The default course, as pressure the player can change: Nezu's toast runs long and wanders into the state of his fur, then lands on the year: the USJ, the camp, Kamino, All Might's retirement, a festival held behind walls, the first chart without All Might at the top, and a whole first year that made it to December. Midnight runs a party game of questions that Hound Dog refuses and Snipe wins without saying a word. Present Mic gets the room singing. Vlad King and Aizawa argue the Joint Training result again. All Might tells a story at his own expense and the room laughs with him, not at him. Aizawa tries to leave three times, and Mic and Midnight catch him twice. If the raid freed Eri, he has a better excuse than anyone: she is asleep in the teachers' quarters and he wants to be there if she wakes.

Late in the evening someone goes quiet over what the year cost, and the party can sit with them or let the music cover it. A teacher party can give a toast of its own, start a rivalry over the karaoke list or help Aizawa escape. Between colleagues, romance stays at most a hint.

The event is complete when Nezu's last toast is drunk and the lounge empties, or Aizawa finally gets out the door with the party's help.

civ_moving_day.title: Moving Day
civ_moving_day.beats:
The first days of April and of the new fiscal year, a weekday from morning into evening. Cherry trees bloom, new hires in stiff suits pack the trains, and reporters still camp at U.A. Academy's gate for a glimpse of All Might. Today the player moves into a new apartment in their own city, a short ride from work, wherever the Background puts home. If the Background has the player settled for years, the move belongs to a new neighbor across the hall who has buried the corridor in boxes, and the player is the helper.

Who is there: the landlord, Mrs. Setsuko Haraguchi, a brisk retired bookkeeper on the ground floor who carries the garbage calendar in a plastic sleeve; two tired movers; the upstairs neighbor, Daichi Ono, a night-shift nurse whose Quirk lets him hear a dropped coin through two floors and who wants quiet above all; down the hall, Mrs. Kinue Abe, whose mild magnetic Quirk keeps teaspoons stuck to her palm, bringing tea unasked. Mr. Tatsuya Moriwaki runs the corner store at the end of the block and knows every resident's complaints.

The default course, as pressure the player can change: the truck arrives an hour early while the keys are still with Mrs. Haraguchi, the stairs are the only way up, and the box with the kettle and the bedding went onto the wrong truck. The landlord walks through burnable, non-burnable and bottle days and mentions that the last tenant left over noise. At noon Daichi comes down, sleepless, about the stairs. Neighbors expect a small greeting gift, and Moriwaki sells boxed towels and soba for exactly that. A Quirk inside the building is a private matter; one used on the street out front can still bring a fine. In Tokyo the room is smaller, the rent higher and the landlord a management company on the phone.

The event is complete when the last box is inside, the missing box is found or written off, and the player has met the landlord and at least one neighbor, or leaves the unpacking for another day.

civ_festival_fever.title: Festival Fever
civ_festival_fever.beats:
Golden Week, the days after the U.A. Sports Festival. The scene reaches the player wherever the day goes. Replays loop on station boards, shop televisions and phones. By canon default, unless the story changed it, the whole country watched Katsuki Bakugo win the first-year tournament and rage on the podium in chains and a muzzle because Shoto Todoroki held back his fire in the final; Izuku Midoriya win the obstacle race and wreck his own fingers against Todoroki; Ochaco Uraraka refuse to quit against Bakugo; Fumikage Tokoyami take third, and Tenya Iida, also third, leave before the ceremony when word came that his brother Ingenium had been attacked in Hosu by the Hero Killer.

Who is there: at work, Kenji Watabe, a coworker who has rewatched the final eleven times and calls that podium honest; the manager, Ms. Yumiko Hosaka, who wants the screen off because people stop to watch and block the aisle; Mr. Shiraishi, a retired regular, who says a hero who snarls on a podium should never be licensed.

The default course, as pressure the player can change: Kenji and Mr. Shiraishi start a loud argument over the podium, a line forms behind them, and Ms. Hosaka asks the player to end it. Later a first-year in a U.A. tracksuit, a Support Course student seen for half a minute in the obstacle race, comes in for a drink; three customers recognize her at once, one wants a photo, and she only wants out. If the player sat in the stands on festival day, a regular swears the player was in a crowd shot behind the food stalls.

At a cafe the replay plays on one phone at a table of six; at a ramen shop it runs above the counter between orders; on a delivery route every door asks about the final; near Tokyo's scramble crossing the giant screens loop the podium while the crowd stalls on the crosswalk.

The event is complete when the argument at work is settled or broken up and the recognized student has her drink and leaves, with or without a photo, or the player's shift ends.

civ_after_kamino.title: After Kamino
civ_after_kamino.beats:
Mid-August, the days after Kamino. Every screen still carries the footage: a block of Kamino Ward flattened, All Might's body giving out on live television, a thin, wounded man in the rubble, then one last blow and a finger pointed at the camera. Unless the story changed it, the kidnapped U.A. student Katsuki Bakugo is home, Best Jeanist is recovering from his injuries, the masked man the news calls Shigaraki's Sensei is in custody, and All Might has retired from hero work. Endeavor is now the highest-ranked active hero, and talk shows argue whether he can stand for anything. Obon has begun and the trains are packed.

Who is there: the manager has set a Kamino relief box by the register; a coworker, Saki Nomura, has not slept since the broadcast and talks about moving home to the countryside; a neighbor has set All Might figures and incense on her balcony; at the station, Hiroshi Tanigawa, a volunteer coordinator in an armband, signs people up for a morning bus to Kamino to sweep, sort salvage and hand out water behind police tape; licensed crews do the heavy lifting.

The default course, as pressure the player can change: the day runs on short tempers and small fears. Customers buy water and batteries. In the afternoon a man with a speed Quirk grabs an armful of goods and bolts, and a sidekick from a small local agency catches him two blocks away, out of breath, saying the agency's calls have tripled since Kamino. A civilian who stops him with a Quirk risks a fine, unless it was self-defense. Saki asks the player to cover her shift so she can catch a train home.

In Musutafu, reporters crowd U.A. Academy's gate again, and new walls rise around the campus. In Tokyo the giant screens replay the retirement announcement while crowds stand still to watch.

The event is complete when the player has made one choice about the mood around them (to volunteer, give, comfort, cover a shift or keep their head down) and the day's shift or volunteer run ends.

civ_fan_convention.title: Hero Fan Convention
civ_fan_convention.beats:
A weekend in early autumn: the Hero Fan Expo fills the exhibition halls of the nearest big city, Musutafu's or Tokyo's, as the player's life sets it. The player comes as a fan, on a friend's spare ticket, or behind a booth the workplace rented.

Who is there: convention staff in orange vests under a floor manager with a headset, Ms. Haruna Ando; Tidewater, a sidekick from a mid-sized agency, signing photos at a folding table, joking about her short line; Doorstop, the stocky pro the expo hired for security, whose Quirk pins whatever he touches to the floor. All Might goods are everywhere and different now: a Symbol of Peace retirement line sells out in an hour, fans tie denim armbands for Best Jeanist's recovery, and cosplayers in Sports Festival tracksuits pose as Bakugo and Todoroki.

The default course, as pressure the player can change: the main-stage panel, Who Is Number One Now, argues the first Hero Billboard Chart without All Might, due before winter. Endeavor is the highest-ranked active hero and the room's least loved; Hawks is fast and popular; a panelist insists Best Jeanist would hold the top if he were healthy. The open mic waits for a question. Midafternoon a man in a cheap All Might costume sweeps a box of signed cards off a booth and runs for the exit; Doorstop pins him to the carpet in one move and calls security. The player can be the one robbed, the one who points, or the one in the runner's path; a Quirk used outside self-defense is still illegal here, and Doorstop says so politely. Tidewater's line grows for the rest of the day.

A booth worker sells out early or sits beside a stack of unsold stock; a fan chases one signature or one rare figure; a friend who bought the tickets wants a cosplay photo with the player in it.

The event is complete when the theft is handled and the player has done one thing at the expo that matters to them (a signature, a purchase, a question at the panel, a booth sold out), or leaves the hall.

civ_holiday_rush.title: Holiday Rush
civ_holiday_rush.beats:
Mid to late December, the year-end rush, afternoon into closing. The city is lit, bonus season fills the shops, Christmas cake orders stack up and year-end parties fill every izakaya. Unless the story changed it, November's Hero Billboard Chart named Endeavor Number One and Hawks Number Two, and the replay of Endeavor's fight with a flying Nomu over Fukuoka, his fist raised at the end, still runs between ads.

Who is there: the manager, Mr. Masaru Iwata, short-staffed and apologizing in advance; a part-timer, Ayumi Kuroda, saving for a trip; a stream of customers; a local hero on patrol, Snapline, whose Quirk fires a taut cord from either wrist.

The default course, as pressure the player can change: a coworker calls in sick and Mr. Iwata asks the player to stay two extra hours. The cake preorders are mixed up and two customers claim the same box. Near dusk a man with a Quirk that fogs glass clouds the front window and the register camera, grabs a stack of gift cards and the cash tray, and runs; Snapline, passing outside, has him wrapped on the sidewalk in seconds, poses for one phone, and leaves the statements to a police officer. Any civilian who uses a Quirk on the thief risks a fine, unless it was self-defense. The rush resumes.

At a convenience store it is cakes and fried chicken; at a cafe, seasonal drinks and couples at every table; at a ramen shop, party groups ordering one more round; on a delivery route, three times the packages and dark stairwells; at a shop counter, gift wrapping until the tape runs out. Near Tokyo's scramble crossing the stores overflow under the giant screens.

After closing the shutters come down and the noise stops. Mr. Iwata hands out leftover cake and thanks everyone in turn; Ayumi buys hot canned coffee from the vending machine and asks what the player plans for the New Year.

The event is complete when the shop closes for the night after the robbery is handled and the player has shared the quiet after closing or gone home.

b1_day_after_usj.title: The Day After the USJ
b1_day_after_usj.beats:
The day after the attack on the USJ, at U.A. Academy. Classes are called off across campus while the faculty meet, and the Class 1-B Dorm Lounge fills early. Every channel runs the same aerial shot of the dome and the police tape across the road, and the anchors repeat what the school has confirmed: a group calling itself the League of Villains broke into Class 1-A's rescue lesson, two teachers are hurt, All Might drove the attackers off, police hold dozens of thugs, and the ringleaders got away. No student died. The Class 1-A side of the building is very quiet.

Itsuka Kendo has made tea for anyone who wants it and makes sure every worried family on the phone gets an answer. Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu paces and wants to go next door and do something. Ibara Shiozaki prays for the injured. Pony Tsunotori asks what "villain alliance" means in the anchor's fast Japanese, and Setsuna Tokage explains it at speed.

Default course, as pressure the player can change: Neito Monoma watches with folded arms and announces that 1-A is now famous for being attacked, that the cameras will follow them all the way to the Sports Festival, and that 1-B will have to be twice as good to be seen at all. The room goes cold. Kendo chops him in the back of the neck before he finishes and apologizes to the room for him. Then Vlad King walks in from the faculty meeting, turns off the screen and says it plainly: the timetable could have put 1-B in that dome. Training gets harder from tomorrow, and anyone who wants to help 1-A can start by being ready.

The party can steady a shaken classmate, push back on Monoma or find the grain of sense in what he said, keep Tetsutetsu from storming next door, or ask Vlad King what the faculty knows; he shares only what the news has. If the scene opens the next morning instead, the same talk happens in the Class 1-B Homeroom before first period.

The event is complete when Vlad King has spoken and the class settles on getting ready, or the party leaves.

b1_monoma_provocation.title: Monoma's Provocation
b1_monoma_provocation.beats:
Lunchtime in the days after Hero Name Day, at Lunch Rush's Cafeteria at U.A. Academy. The internship lists are posted and the Sports Festival replays are still everywhere; strangers recognize Class 1-A on the train, and Class 1-B has noticed. Neito Monoma, newly Phantom Thief, has opened a campaign. All morning he drifted past 1-A in the Main Building Hallway with a slow clap and a question about how fame feels, and now he carries his tray to the table where Katsuki Bakugo, Eijiro Kirishima and Momo Yaoyorozu are eating.

Default course, as pressure the player can change: Monoma sets the tray down without sitting, smiles wide and asks, with exquisite courtesy, whether the podium was comfortable, and whether a winner in restraints counts as a champion in 1-A. The laugh goes on too long. Kirishima tries to laugh it off; Yaoyorozu answers with cold, precise courtesy; Bakugo does not look up, then sets down his chopsticks, and his palms start to crackle. Monoma leans closer, one hand drifting toward Bakugo's sleeve. Before contact, Itsuka Kendo, 1-B's class representative, arrives behind him, chops him once in the back of the neck, catches him and tells the table, "Sorry about him." Behind her, Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu shouts across to Kirishima that their rematch is still on, and Sen Kaibara takes Monoma's tray away with a flat remark about lunch.

By path: a 1-B party is in Monoma's audience and can feed the act, rein him in before Kendo does, or turn the taunt into a fair challenge Bakugo will respect. A 1-A party sits at the target table: the bait is plain, and taking it means a cafeteria fight the faculty will hear about, while ignoring Monoma infuriates him more than any comeback. Either class can set up Tetsutetsu and Kirishima's rematch for another day. No real fight happens here: a Quirk used indoors brings a teacher at once.

The event is complete when Monoma has been chopped or talked down and both classes go back to lunch, or the party leaves.

b1_joint_sparring.title: Joint Sparring Day
b1_joint_sparring.beats:
A weekday afternoon in late spring at U.A. Academy. Vlad King has talked Shota Aizawa into a combined sparring block in the Main Gymnasium: not a graded exercise, only pairs from Class 1-A and Class 1-B on taped squares, a whistle, and Vlad King's insistence that his class is ready. Aizawa agreed because fighting unfamiliar Quirks is rational, and his tone says nothing else about it pleases him. If the drills move outdoors, the second half runs in the Mock City Streets of Ground Beta.

Default course, as pressure the player can change: the teachers call the pairs. Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu and Eijiro Kirishima get each other again and charge before the whistle ends, steel against hardened skin, until both are winded and grinning; the crowd wants a winner and gets none. Itsuka Kendo draws Momo Yaoyorozu, who creates a net, a staff and then a plan; Kendo reads the plan instead of the tools, and the bout turns into a slow, careful contest of who adapts first. Neito Monoma touches three people on the way to his square and narrates every copy. He asks Katsuki Bakugo for a bout, Bakugo's answer is loud, and Aizawa's eyes glow red before an explosion leaves a palm. Ibara Shiozaki prays before her match and binds her opponent with an apology.

The rules hold: a bout stops at a call or a tap, nobody strikes a downed partner, and Aizawa erases anyone who forgets. Vlad King keeps a running tally on a whiteboard he never mentioned to Aizawa.

By path: a 1-B party is paired with a 1-A student and can win, lose well or learn the other class's habits. A 1-A party gets a 1-B opponent whose Quirk it has seen only on the Sports Festival broadcast, and Monoma will try to touch it before the whistle. Either side can turn a grudge bout into respect, or into a scene the teachers end early.

The event is complete when the last pairs bow out and the two teachers compare notes, or the party leaves.

b1_movie_night.title: 1-B Movie Night
b1_movie_night.beats:
An evening in late June in the Class 1-B Dorm Lounge at U.A. Academy. Itsuka Kendo has put the snacks in order on the low table: chips by the left armrest, rice crackers by the right, one bag open at a time so nothing ends up in the sofa. The lights are down. It is Neito Monoma's turn to pick the film, and he has chosen a long American heist picture about a gentleman thief who robs a rival's museum to prove he is the better man. He has seen it four times and quotes it under his breath.

Default course, as pressure the player can change: the film runs with commentary. Pony Tsunotori explains everything the subtitles miss: the baseball joke, the roadside diner, why the detective keeps calling everyone "buddy", the Fourth of July fireworks over the finale; she is delighted to be the expert for once. Reiko Yanagi wanted a ghost story instead, and slowly lifts a cushion behind anyone who mocks her pick. Sen Kaibara names every hole in the plot, one line each. Hiryu Rin says nothing and eats steadily. Jurota Shishida politely asks people to stop talking. Yui Kodai shrinks the empty bags without a word. Then the thief's loyal partner takes the fall for him, and Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu cries openly and loudly and is not embarrassed in the least. Monoma declares the thief obviously the hero; Kendo points out that he is the villain.

The party can choose the next film, argue the ending, help Pony with a joke that does not translate, or catch Monoma admitting why he loves the thief: the man wins with treasures that belong to other people. Vlad King looks in around ten, asks whether this is a study group, and stays for the last twenty minutes.

The event is complete when the credits roll and Kendo assigns the cleanup, or the party leaves.

b1_kendo_study.title: Kendo's Study Session
b1_kendo_study.beats:
Evenings in the week before the final exams, in the Class 1-B Dorm Lounge at U.A. Academy. Itsuka Kendo has pushed the tables together, written a schedule on the whiteboard (hero law, then math, then modern literature, ten-minute breaks strictly enforced) and assigned tutors by subject: Juzo Honenuki on math, Nirengeki Shoda on hero law, and Kojiro Bondo, quietly the best essay writer in the class, on literature. Earlier the same group held a long table in the Library until the librarian's look sent them home.

Default course, as pressure the player can change: Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu and Togaru Kamakiri need the most help and accept it the least. Tetsutetsu attacks every problem set at full volume and declares victory before checking the answer; Kamakiri glares at a word problem and dares it to make sense. Neito Monoma sits apart with a closed book, insists he does not need a study group, and corrects everyone's answers aloud from across the room. Setsuna Tokage sends a single floating piece to peek at his notes and reports that they are color-coded. Kendo has heard from an upperclassman that the practical will be robots again, the same as the entrance exam, and passes it on with a warning that it is only a rumor; the room relaxes about the practical and dreads the written test. Nobody here knows the real format.

The party can tutor or be tutored, broker a truce between Kamakiri and an equation, or draw Monoma into the group without letting him win the argument. Kendo will take the hardest student herself unless someone offers; noticing that she has not opened her own books all week, and doing something about it, is a quiet win.

The event is complete when the night's practice quiz is graded and Kendo sends everyone to bed, or the party leaves.

b1_shopping_trip.title: The 1-B Shopping Trip
b1_shopping_trip.beats:
A free day in mid-July, with the forest training camp ahead. Class 1-B rides into Musutafu to shop at Kiyashi Shopping Mall on a day of its own, and the Main Atrium swallows twenty people in under a minute. Itsuka Kendo holds the list: hiking boots, a rain shell, insect repellent, a flashlight, a week of socks, and a meeting time at the fountain she repeats three times.

Default course, as pressure the player can change: the class scatters. Setsuna Tokage splits into pieces to cover the Fashion Floors all at once and reports prices from four shops in one breath, until a security guard asks why a hand is floating by the sunglasses. Pony Tsunotori hunts for boots that fit hooves and wants a cowboy hat for the mountains. Kinoko Komori asks the staff how humid the camp will be and buys three rain hats. Yui Kodai shrinks the class's purchases until they fit in one tote bag. Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu heads straight for the Food Court and anything with iron in it. Neito Monoma demands to know what Class 1-A bought and buys one more of each item. Ibara Shiozaki finds the music, the screens and the crowds hard to bear and stays near the fountain, praying quietly; she will not say she wants to leave.

The party can shop with any group, help Pony find boots, keep Tokage out of trouble with security, or notice Shiozaki and find her a quieter floor, for which she thanks the party gravely. If Class 1-A's lockdown at this mall has already happened, police stand at the entrances and the class talks about it in low voices; this day stays ordinary and no villain appears. A party that stayed at U.A. Academy meets the class at the Campus Bus Terminal on its way back, loaded with bags, and can help Kendo check the list.

The event is complete when the class meets at the fountain with everything on the list and heads home, or the party leaves.

b1_test_of_courage.title: The Test of Courage Night
b1_test_of_courage.beats:
The second night of the forest training camp, at the Wild Wild Pussycats Lodge. A brutal day of Quirk drills is over, both classes cooked their own curry at the Outdoor Kitchen and ate it under the trees, and at dinner Pixie-Bob announced the treat for tomorrow night: a test of courage in Beast's Forest, Class 1-A walking a dark route in pairs while Class 1-B does the scaring. Class 1-B has taken over a corner of the Lodge Hall to plan. Through the windows there is only forest and a clear, starry sky.

Default course, as pressure the player can change: Neito Monoma has drawn the route from memory and built a plan with stations, timings and a script. Kinoko Komori is thrilled with the damp and promises mushrooms on every trunk at the turn. Reiko Yanagi will float a lantern a few steps behind each pair and let it go out. Shihai Kuroiro will rise out of the black between the trees, and rehearses his line twice until someone laughs and he mumbles the third. Manga Fukidashi tests which sound effect makes the best scare, very quietly for once. Yui Kodai has a small doll to enlarge at the right moment. Itsuka Kendo sets the one rule: scare them, never touch them, and nobody leaves the path. Monoma wants a station so frightening that 1-A will talk about it for the rest of the year; Kendo trims it down, and he sulks for a full minute.

The party can write a scare, rehearse one on a classmate, argue Monoma down or egg him on, or step out to the Training Clearing, where Vlad King and Tiger are laying out gear for the dawn drills; Vlad King looks the plan over, approves it loudly and orders everyone to bed early. The night stays calm: crickets, a cool wind, laughter from the 1-A side of the lodge.

The event is complete when the plan is set and Vlad King sends 1-B to the bunk rooms, or the party leaves.

b1_license_prep.title: License Exam Prep
b1_license_prep.beats:
The last days before the provisional license exam, at U.A. Academy under the lockdown that has held since the summer. Class 1-B will sit the exam on the same day as Class 1-A at a different venue, and nobody knows the format: only that the Hero Public Safety Commission runs it and that many examinees fail every year. Vlad King has booked the Main Gymnasium for 1-B's special-move drills, and at the end of each session he hands the floor to Itsuka Kendo.

Default course, as pressure the player can change: Kendo's point is simple. The whole country watched 1-B's Quirks on the Sports Festival broadcast, so other schools will have studied them; the class that stays together is the class that passes. On the whiteboard she builds pairs and trios and who covers whom: Yui Kodai's barriers behind Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu's charge, Juzo Honenuki's mud in front of Setsuna Tokage's scouting pieces, Yosetsu Awase anchoring anything that moves. Neito Monoma wants the opposite, ambush teams that pick off the schools coming for them, and Tetsutetsu wants to charge whatever is closest. The argument gets loud, and Kendo lets it, then asks Monoma to plan inside her structure instead of around it. Vlad King roars approval at the end of every drill and pretends he is not nervous.

The party can run a drill, test a pairing, take Monoma's side or Kendo's, or find a third plan both will accept. Kendo will keep working until the lights go off unless someone sends her to bed. In the evening the scene moves to the Class 1-B Dorm Lounge, where the class quizzes each other on hero law and the rules for using a Quirk in an emergency.

The event is complete when the class agrees on how it will move on exam day and Kendo calls it a night, or the party leaves.

b1_festival_rivalry.title: The Cultural Festival Rivalry
b1_festival_rivalry.beats:
The days before the School Festival at U.A. Academy. Class 1-B rehearses its stage play, "Romeo and Juliet and the Prisoner of Azkaban: The Return of the King," in costume on the Main Gymnasium stage: a tragedy, a prison break and a coronation folded into one script, which Neito Monoma insists will crush Class 1-A's band.

The cast in costume: Monoma as Romeo, in a doublet and cape; Yui Kodai as Juliet, in a long gown, who also uses her Quirk to grow and shrink the props between scenes; Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu as Count Paris, the hooded villain whose last-act secret is that he is Romeo's father; Nirengeki Shoda and Yosetsu Awase as Romeo's men, whom Romeo shields in the tower duel. Itsuka Kendo keeps the rehearsal on schedule from the wings in her uniform, and the rest of the class runs the lights, the sets and the effects.

Default course, as pressure the player can change: the rehearsal runs long. Monoma will not cut a line of Romeo's monologues, though the festival gives each class a strict time slot. Tetsutetsu keeps throwing back his hood before the reveal. Kodai's prop changes are perfect and silent, and nobody thanks her. Drums from Class 1-A's band practice carry across campus, and Monoma counts every missed beat aloud. Kendo wants one clean run before dark.

The party can take a small part, help backstage, cut the script, mend a costume, calm Monoma or fire him up, or help Kendo get a full run inside the time limit. A party at the Class 1-B Dorm Lounge finds the costume team sewing late into the evening.

The event is complete when the cast finishes one full run within the time slot, or the party leaves.

b1_hot_pot.title: 1-B Hot Pot Night
b1_hot_pot.beats:
A cold evening in mid-December at U.A. Academy. Class 1-B has pooled its money for a hot pot night, and the Class 1-B Dorm Lounge smells of broth from the Dorm Kitchen, where Itsuka Kendo runs the pot with a ladle and a timetable: vegetables first, then tofu, then the meat, in that order, no exceptions. Two burners sit on the low tables, and the class crowds around them on cushions.

Default course, as pressure the player can change: before anyone eats, Ibara Shiozaki asks for a moment of quiet and says grace; the class waits, Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu with his chopsticks already raised. Then the meat goes in and the war begins. Tetsutetsu and Togaru Kamakiri reach for the same slice of beef every time, Tetsutetsu arguing that he needs the iron, Kamakiri arguing that he was faster. Kendo enforces a rotation. Neito Monoma critiques the broth, the cut of the meat, the dipping sauce and the seating plan, and somehow eats more than anyone. Hiryu Rin quietly adds a spice from home that makes half the table sweat and the other half ask for more. Kinoko Komori offers mushrooms, and Kendo checks that they came from a store. Pony Tsunotori, at her first proper hot pot, learns the word for the rice porridge made from the last of the broth and repeats it aloud until she has it. Vlad King looks in, is pressed to stay, and eats a bowl standing up.

The party can cook, guard the meat, take Monoma's critique seriously, or notice that Kendo has not sat down all evening and take over the ladle so she can. Whether she lets someone else run the pot is the small stake of the night.

The event is complete when the last of the broth has become porridge and the class cleans up together, or the party leaves.

b1_after_joint_training.title: After the Joint Training
b1_after_joint_training.beats:
An evening in the days after the Joint Training, in the Class 1-B Dorm Lounge at U.A. Academy. The five rounds at Training Ground Gamma are over and their results stand as this story decided them; nobody replays them here, they argue about them. Momo Yaoyorozu has come over from next door with her notebook, Eijiro Kirishima with a bag of snacks for Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu, and Itsuka Kendo has cleared the low table for a proper debrief: what worked, what failed, what each class learned about the other.

Default course, as pressure the player can change: Kendo and Yaoyorozu compare plans and find they made the same mistake from opposite sides; they write it down. Juzo Honenuki adds one quiet correction to each of their notes. Tetsutetsu and Kirishima argue over who took the harder hits and agree it was both. Ibara Shiozaki asks forgiveness of everyone she bound. Neito Monoma stands on a chair and demands a rematch, all five rounds, this week, and asks the 1-A guests with exquisite courtesy how it feels to need help from General Studies, forgetting that 1-B had Hitoshi Shinso on its side too. The talk turns to Shinso: the teachers gave their verdict at the end of the day, by canon default that he is on track to join the Hero Course next spring, and even Monoma admits through his teeth that the capture scarf was well used. Katsuki Bakugo, off at his work-study by default, is a topic of the debrief but not in the room.

By path: a 1-B party is a host and can lead the debrief, back Monoma's rematch, or tell him what he did well in his round, which leaves him speechless. A 1-A party is a guest in rival territory: Monoma will needle, Tetsutetsu will offer a drink and a challenge, and an honest word of credit for 1-B's plans earns Kendo's respect.

The event is complete when the notes are traded and Vlad King looks in to send the 1-A guests home, or the party leaves.

side_full_cowl.title: Full Cowl
side_full_cowl.beats:
Late April, daytime, during the Hero Agency Internship week at Gran Torino's Apartment. The cramped Main Room is littered with laundry and boxes, and the retired pro Sorahiko Torino plays the doddering old man, asking Izuku Midoriya who he is before dropping the act mid-sentence and ricocheting off the walls, floor and ceiling with Jet faster than the eye can track.

Default course as pressure: Gran Torino batters Izuku across the room to show him why his fighting failed at the Sports Festival. Izuku treats One For All as a special trump card he switches on in a single limb when he is desperate, instead of part of his own body, and his admiration for All Might keeps his movements stiff. The lesson pauses only when the microwave dings in Gran Torino's Kitchenette. The old man pulls out a plate of taiyaki that is scorching outside and still icy in the center because the turntable was jammed. Looking at the unevenly heated fish pastry gives Izuku the answer: instead of focusing power into one point after he moves, he must circulate a low, even five percent through his whole body from the start. By the final bouts he holds One For All: Full Cowl across the room, trading high-speed rebounds with his mentor and landing a grazing blow before Gran Torino puts him on the floorboards again.

By path: a Class 1-A or Class 1-B student interning at Gran Torino's Apartment or visiting on a joint patrol drill is thrown straight into the same close-quarters gauntlet. Gran Torino calls both young people "kid," bounces off the walls to test their reflexes from blind angles, and forces the party to keep its Quirk active and controlled on the move rather than saving one big swing.

The event is complete when Izuku holds Full Cowl at five percent through a three-minute spar in the apartment and Gran Torino sits down to finish his warm taiyaki.

v_stain_meets_league.title: The Hero Killer at the Bar
v_stain_meets_league.beats:
Late April, evening to late night at the League Hideout Bar, days before the Hosu incident. The broker Giran brings a prospective ally through the Alley Entrance to the Bar Counter: Stain, the Hero Killer, bandage-wrapped and armed with knives and a katana. Kurogiri polishes glasses behind the bar while Tomura Shigaraki slouches on a stool with the severed hand he calls Father over his face.

Default course as pressure: Kurogiri hopes to recruit the notorious killer, and Shigaraki expects an easy alliance between men who destroy heroes. Instead, the talk sours within minutes. Shigaraki brags about smashing everything that annoys him, starting with All Might and the U.A. Academy brats from the USJ. Stain answers with a low, rasping "Hah..." and judges Shigaraki a brat throwing a tantrum without conviction. When Shigaraki reaches out to decay him, Stain vaults the counter, pins him to the floorboards with a blade at his throat, cuts his shoulder, and paralyzes both Shigaraki and Kurogiri with Bloodcurdle. Only when Shigaraki, bleeding and clawing at his neck, forces out that he wants to ruin a society that worships All Might does Stain sheathe his knife. Calling it a seed of conviction worth watching, Stain demands that Kurogiri warp him back to Hosu to finish his own purge.

By path: a League of Villains Recruit is in the bar when Giran arrives and faces Stain's measure firsthand. The recruit can step between the Hero Killer and Shigaraki, cross blades to test Stain's speed, or answer Stain's demand for a creed before Kurogiri talks the room down; Stain spares no one who fights for petty spite alone, but stays his hand if the recruit forces a standoff or speaks with real purpose.

The event is complete when Stain judges the League's answer and steps through Kurogiri's warp gate back to Hosu.

side_kamino_reckoning.title: The Rebuke
side_kamino_reckoning.beats:
Early August, evening, outside Heights Alliance in the Heights Alliance Yard at U.A. Academy. The crisis in Kamino Ward is over, All Might has retired, and Class 1-A has been called out before dinner to face Shota Aizawa under the courtyard lights. The air between the five students who went to Kamino and the classmates who stayed behind is strained and quiet.

Default course as pressure: Aizawa addresses the class in his flat, low voice. He tells Izuku Midoriya, Tenya Iida, Shoto Todoroki, Eijiro Kirishima, and Momo Yaoyorozu that breaking rules to play vigilante in Kamino shattered the faculty's trust, and tells everyone else who knew of their plan and said nothing—everyone except Katsuki Bakugo, Kyoka Jiro and Toru Hagakure, who were hurt or unconscious that night—that they share the blame. If U.A. Academy were not under emergency campus lockdown after All Might's retirement, he would expel every one of them except those three on the spot; instead, he orders them to rebuild their trust strictly by the book and walks inside. In the awkward silence, Tsuyu Asui finally speaks up, tears spilling down her face: she tells the five how hurt and frightened she was that they went into danger after she warned them, and how badly she wants them all to be friends again without breaking the rules. The rescuers apologize in full, hugging her in the yard. Meanwhile, Katsuki Bakugo grabs Denki Kaminari, drags him behind the bushes to force him into his short-circuited "Wheey" state so the class laughs, and shoves an envelope of cash into Kirishima's chest to repay the night-vision goggles Kirishima bought to save him.

By path: a Class 1-A student stands in the yard for Aizawa's judgment—counted among those who went, those who stayed silent, or the few who spoke against it—and helps mend the rift with Tsu and the others in the Class 1-A Dorm Lounge afterward.

The event is complete when Tsuyu's tears dry, Bakugo pays his debt, and Class 1-A heads into the Class 1-A Dorm Lounge together.

side_big_three.title: The Big Three
side_big_three.beats:
Mid-September, daytime at U.A. Academy, at the start of the second term. To explain the Hero Work-Studies that go beyond first-term internships, Shota Aizawa brings the academy's top three third-year students—the Big Three—into Class 1-A Homeroom: Mirio Togata, Tamaki Amajiki, and Nejire Hado.

Default course as pressure: the introduction starts oddly. Tamaki stares intensely at the class to picture them as potatoes, then gives up, turns to face the homeroom wall, and mutters that he wants to go home. Nejire immediately darts from desk to desk firing rapid-fire questions about Mina Ashido's horns, Shoto Todoroki's burn scar, and everyone else's Quirks before anyone can answer. Mirio opens with a flat pun that lands on dead silence, laughs loudly anyway, and proposes moving to the Main Gymnasium so the first-years can learn by fighting him all at once. On the gym floor, Mirio's clothes drop as his Quirk activates, he apologizes mid-slip, and within seconds he sinks through the floor with Permeation to take out the long-range attackers first before dropping the close-range fighters with single precision body blows. Even when Izuku Midoriya reads his resurface angle, Mirio slips the counter through sheer prediction. Afterward, fully dressed again, Mirio explains that Permeation leaves him blind, deaf, and breathless underground; what beat Class 1-A was not a flashy power, but the experience and foresight he gained on work-study under Sir Nighteye. It is a supervised bout where no student is badly hurt.

By path: a Class 1-A student faces Mirio on the Main Gymnasium floor alongside the class and tests a plan against his prediction; a Class 1-B student observing from the Main Building Hallway or joining the joint session gets the chance to step onto the mat and test 1-B's teamwork against Lemillion.

The event is complete when Mirio finishes the bout, explains how work-study built his skill, and the Big Three take questions from the first-years.

side_nighteye_stamp.title: Nighteye's Stamp Test
side_nighteye_stamp.beats:
Late September, daytime at the Sir Nighteye Hero Agency. Mirio Togata brings Izuku Midoriya into the Agency Office to apply for a Hero Work-Study under All Might's former sidekick, Sir Nighteye. The office walls are lined with rare All Might posters and memorabilia, Centipeder works quietly in the Meeting Room, and Nighteye's doctrine that an agency must run on humor is enforced on the spot as Bubble Girl struggles through a flat joke.

Default course as pressure: Izuku tries to meet the humor rule by contorting his face into an All Might impression. It fails miserably; Nighteye stares at him through rectangular glasses with cold severity because the impression wrinkles a detail of All Might's brow wrong. Nighteye states bluntly that Mirio Togata should have been chosen as All Might's successor, not Izuku, and refuses to sign Izuku's work-study contract automatically. Instead, he holds up his official agency seal and gives a three-minute test: if Izuku wants the stamp on his form, he must take the seal from Nighteye's hand and stamp the paper himself while Mirio steps outside. With one use of Foresight, Nighteye slips every Full Cowl rush, hurling heavy five-kilogram seals to pin Izuku back while pressing him on why All Might chose him. Izuku still cannot touch Nighteye before the three minutes expire, but as he rebounds off the walls, he takes extra care never to step on a single All Might poster on the floor. Seeing that devotion—and wanting to show Izuku the realities of the street—Nighteye takes the form and stamps it himself.

By path: a Class 1-A or Class 1-B student who comes with Mirio and Izuku to apply at the Sir Nighteye Hero Agency must first attempt a joke to satisfy Nighteye's humor requirement, then either join the three-minute stamp test in the Agency Office or run an observation drill with Centipeder and Bubble Girl to earn Nighteye's signature.

The event is complete when the three-minute test ends and Sir Nighteye stamps the work-study paperwork.

side_fat_gum_patrol.title: Unbreakable
side_fat_gum_patrol.beats:
Early October, daytime in Osaka Downtown and the Fat Gum Hero Agency. The BMI Hero Fat Gum walks a lively street patrol through the Covered Arcade and Dotonbori Canal with his third-year intern Tamaki Amajiki and his new Class 1-A work-study student Eijiro Kirishima, chatting with shopkeepers and sharing takoyaki between street checks.

Default course as pressure: a street gang fight breaks out in the Covered Arcade and spills into the Back Streets. Fat Gum sinks the fleeing thugs straight into his body, and Tamaki pins the rest with clam shells and octopus tentacles, until a panicked gunman in the crowd fires a strange dart from the shadows. The round hits Tamaki in the arm; when he tries to manifest his Quirk again, nothing happens—his power has been temporarily erased. Before the shooter can escape, a cornered confederate injects himself with the black-market drug Trigger, sprouting long blades from his body that slice through Eijiro's ordinary Hardening and threaten bystanders in the alley. Remembering how he froze in the past, Eijiro refuses to back down and pushes his Quirk beyond its normal limit, hardening every inch of his skin, teeth, and eyes into jagged armor: Red Riot Unbreakable. He shatters the Trigger-boosted blades, drives the villain back into Fat Gum's waiting belly, and secures the arrest. Afterward, at the Fat Gum Agency Front Office, Tamaki's Quirk begins to return after rest, and Fat Gum bags the crushed dart casing as hard evidence of a Quirk-destroying drug on the streets.

By path: a Class 1-A or Class 1-B student on work-study patrols beside Kirishima and Tamaki; a Licensed Pro Hero or Licensed Sidekick working the Osaka beat joins Fat Gum's pursuit in the Back Streets, helps shield civilians from the Trigger blades, or tracks the shooter who fired the dart.

The event is complete when the Trigger-boosted villain is in Fat Gum's custody, Tamaki is checked over, and the bullet evidence is secured.

side_eri_visit.title: A Smile for Eri
side_eri_visit.beats:
Late October, daytime in the Patient Rooms of Musutafu General Hospital, a week after the Shie Hassaikai raid. The fever from Eri's horn has subsided, and Shota Aizawa stands near the door as her guardian so he can erase her Quirk if it stirs. Izuku Midoriya and Mirio Togata arrive with a basket of fruit to see her for the first time since the rescue.

Default course as pressure: Eri sits propped up in the hospital bed, small and quiet, apologizing before anyone asks a question. She thanks Izuku and Mirio for saving her and asks after everyone who was hurt, blaming herself because she still does not know what her power does or why people bled for her. Even when Mirio makes a goofy face and peels an apple into slices for her, her expression remains still; the shadow of Kai Chisaki lingers, and she does not know how to smile. Remembering that U.A. Academy is preparing its autumn School Festival, Izuku and Mirio ask Aizawa's permission and invite Eri to come see the festival—a day of music, dancing, and sweet stalls—promising that if she comes, they will help her find a real smile. Eri does not understand what a festival is, so she asks politely to hear more, and Aizawa agrees to arrange a brief, supervised preview walk of U.A. Academy before the crowds arrive so the child will not be overwhelmed on the day. The scene stays gentle and child-safe throughout.

By path: a Class 1-A student visiting the Patient Rooms with Izuku helps put Eri at ease at her level—talking quietly about campus life, peeling fruit, or promising what Class 1-A will build for the festival—without crowding or frightening her.

The event is complete when Eri accepts the invitation to the School Festival and Aizawa approves her supervised campus visit.

side_festival_rehearsal.title: The Band
side_festival_rehearsal.beats:
Late October to early November, evenings at U.A. Academy in the final week before the School Festival. In the Class 1-A Dorm Lounge, Tenya Iida and Momo Yaoyorozu lead a vote to choose Class 1-A's festival event—something that will lift the spirit of the whole campus, other courses included, after months of tension.

Default course as pressure: the class settles on a live concert with a dance performance and stage effects, and everyone looks straight at Kyoka Jiro. She turns red, twists her earlobe jacks, and tries to deflect, until Denki Kaminari and Eijiro Kirishima remind her how much her music means to her; she agrees to lead the band and sing. Auditions in the Music Room quickly sort the players: Katsuki Bakugo blasts the drum kit with explosive precision after refusing at first and swearing they will crush every listener in the hall, Momo takes the keyboard, Kaminari and Tokoyami take guitars, and Jiro takes bass and vocals. In the lounge, Mina Ashido drills the dancers—Izuku Midoriya, Ochaco Uraraka, Tenya Iida, and the rest—while Shoto Todoroki, Eijiro Kirishima, and Yuga Aoyama plan an ice-and-light disco ball for the gym ceiling. Meanwhile, training outside in the Heights Alliance Yard before dusk, Izuku works on long-range wind pressure and visits Mei Hatsume in the Development Studio, where she enthusiastically outfits him with her newest "baby": support gloves that focus twenty-percent finger flicks into clean Air Force blasts.

By path: a Class 1-A student takes a role in the band, the dance crew, or the stage-effects team across the Class 1-A Dorm Lounge and Music Room, or tests gear alongside Izuku and Hatsume in the Development Studio.

The event is complete when the band's arrangement locks in, the dance and stage cues are set, and Izuku tests his Air Force gloves.

v_gigantomachia_trials.title: The Giant
v_gigantomachia_trials.beats:
Throughout November, day and night, wherever the League of Villains is camped in the wilderness before the Battle of Deika. After All For One's bodyguard Gigantomachia rejected Tomura Shigaraki as too weak to succeed his master, Dr. Kyudai Garaki gave the League one condition for his backing and resources: bend the giant to Shigaraki's will in combat.

Default course as pressure: for weeks on end, the League fights Gigantomachia across rugged ravines and mountain slopes. Every forty-eight hours and forty-four minutes, the giant stops only for three hours of sleep before waking to hunt Shigaraki all over again. Dabi's blue flames scorch the rock without slowing him, Himiko Toga and Spinner dart from cover to buy seconds, Twice makes doubles to pull the bruised out of reach, and Mr. Compress pockets boulders and exhausted comrades alike, yet Gigantomachia tears through hillsides roaring for his master. Exhausted and sleepless, Shigaraki refuses to retreat; his speed sharpens and his Decay begins spreading beyond the five fingers he touches directly. Just as Shigaraki swears he will tame the giant in the next waking cycle, word comes through the underworld: the Meta Liberation Army's leader, Re-Destro, holds the broker Giran captive in Deika City and challenges the League to come fight his army or watch their broker die.

By path: a League of Villains Recruit endures the grueling mountain attrition alongside Shigaraki, Dabi, Toga, Twice, Spinner, and Compress—taking shifts to bait Gigantomachia's charges, covering Shigaraki during the three-hour rest windows, and weighing in when Re-Destro's ultimatum over Giran arrives.

The event is complete when the League survives another waking bout with Gigantomachia and hears Re-Destro's challenge to march on Deika City.

v_hawks_joins.title: The Number Two
v_hawks_joins.beats:
Mid-December, evening to late night in the Yokohama Harbor District, after the Paranormal Liberation Front's founding and the start of Tomura Shigaraki's four-month procedure. Out on the Container Docks and near the Dockside Safehouse, Dabi meets the Wing Hero Hawks, Japan's Number Two pro hero, who has been courting the League since the Kyushu High-End attack.

Default course as pressure: Hawks lands with his usual breezy smile, hands in his flight jacket pockets, and asks to be brought into the inner circle now that the League and the Meta Liberation Army have merged. Dabi leans against a shipping container, low and sardonic, and refuses to trust a hero's words alone: if the Number Two wants a seat in the Front, he has to prove he has crossed the line in blood. When Hawks returns for the second meeting, he carries a heavy duffel bag onto the docks and unzips it at Dabi's feet to reveal what looks to be the corpse of the missing Number Three hero, Best Jeanist. (Narrator only, covert truth the recruit does not know: Best Jeanist is alive in suspended animation under the Commission's secret operation; on the docks, the recruit sees only what Dabi sees.) Dabi inspects the body in the bag with a flat smirk, remarks that Hawks really is crazy despite doubting whether it is truly Jeanist, and grants Hawks access as a lieutenant's contact while keeping him under quiet watch.

By path: a League of Villains Recruit accompanies Dabi to the Container Docks as backup, watches the perimeter for Hero Public Safety Commission tails, questions Hawks face-to-face when he hands over the bag, and decides whether to report concerns about the Wing Hero's true motives.

The event is complete when Hawks presents the duffel bag on the docks and Dabi accepts him into the Front's network on probation.
